Containers are mostly made of **steel**. This allows them to withstand wind, waves and heavy stacking. They are **cuboid** in shape, that is, a long, rectangular box with doors on one side. Because they all come in **standard sizes**, they fit on every container ship, every goods train and every lorry.

In the port, huge cranes lift the containers off the ship one by one. These cranes are called **container gantry cranes**. Unloading a ship is called **discharging** in shipping. Because everything is standardised, moving the containers goes very quickly.

The largest container ships, such as the **MSC Irina**, are about **400 metres** long. They can load over **24,000** standard containers (as of 2025). The measurement used is the **TEU**, where one unit equals one 20-foot container. Such ships only fit into very large ports with deep water.

The **Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC)** has been the largest container shipping company in the world since 2022. Its headquarters are in **Geneva**, even though Switzerland has **no sea coast**. Containers reach Switzerland along the Rhine as far as the ports near Basel. From there they continue by rail and by lorry.

gewusst: A big container ship is about as long as four football pitches end to end.
Switzerland has its own ocean-going fleet, even though it has no sea.

teile.einleitung: When people meet, they greet each other. Depending on the country and language, this is done with different words and gestures. A greeting shows friendliness and respect.
wichtigste: In Italian you greet friends with “Ciao”.
In Spanish you say “Hola”, in Turkish “Merhaba”.
In German-speaking Switzerland people politely say “Grüezi”, in Romansh “Allegra”.
In Japan people bow as a greeting.
The Maori in New Zealand press nose and forehead together in the “hongi”.
In Switzerland friends often give each other three kisses on the cheek.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland people greet in four national languages. In German-speaking Switzerland you say “Grüezi” to people you address formally. To friends you say “Hoi” or “Sali”. In Ticino you hear “Ciao” or “Buongiorno”, in French-speaking Switzerland “Bonjour” and “Salut”. In **Romansh**, people in Graubünden greet with “Allegra”.

In **Italian**, “Ciao” means both “hello” and “goodbye”. In **Spanish** you say “Hola”, and the H is not pronounced. In **English** you wish someone “Good morning” in the morning. In **Turkish** people greet with “Merhaba”. In **Hawaii** you say “Aloha”, a word that also means love and friendship.

In **Japan** people greet each other with a **bow**. The deeper you bow, the more polite and respectful the greeting. In India people often put their palms together in front of the chest and say “Namaste”. In many countries of Europe, by contrast, the **handshake** is usual, especially when you do not know each other well.

The **Maori** in New Zealand traditionally greet each other with the **hongi**. In it, the noses and foreheads of the two people touch. In Switzerland, friends and relatives often give each other **three kisses** on the cheeks. In other countries it is two or only one. If you travel to a foreign country, it is best to watch how people there greet each other.

gewusst: The Italian “Ciao” comes from an old Venetian expression meaning “your servant”.
In Switzerland people often greet each other when hiking in the mountains, even if they do not know each other.

teile.einleitung: The Antarctic Treaty is an international agreement on Antarctica. It was signed in 1959 and ensures that the continent is used only peacefully. Research is expressly welcome, the military is forbidden.
wichtigste: The Antarctic Treaty was signed in Washington on 1 December 1959.
Twelve states originally signed it, and it came into force in 1961.
It applies to all areas south of 60 degrees south.
Military use of Antarctica is forbidden.
The territorial claims of individual states are frozen.
The treaty states may inspect each other’s stations.
Switzerland joined the treaty in 1990.

abschnitte.text: In **1957 and 1958** the International Geophysical Year took place. Many countries were doing research together in Antarctica at the time. From this the idea of a treaty arose. On **1 December 1959** **twelve states** signed the Antarctic Treaty in Washington, including the USA and the Soviet Union. It came into force in 1961. Many more countries joined later.

The treaty applies to all land and ice areas **south of 60 degrees south**, that is, to the whole of Antarctica. Antarctica may only be used **peacefully**. Military bases, manoeuvres and **weapons tests** are forbidden. Nuclear tests and the storage of nuclear waste are also banned. Researchers are to work freely and exchange their results.

Several countries make **claims** to parts of Antarctica. The treaty does not decide who owns which area. It simply **freezes** the claims. Nobody has to give up their claim, but new claims are not allowed. In this way a dispute that could otherwise have led to conflict was avoided.

So that everyone keeps to the rules, **inspections** are allowed. Observers from the treaty states may visit all stations, ships and installations at any time. They check, for example, that no weapons are stored there. This open control was something special at the time of the **Cold War**.

**Switzerland** joined the Antarctic Treaty on **15 November 1990**. Since then it has been one of the parties to the treaty. Swiss researchers in Antarctica often work together with other countries, for example in studying ice cores. Today over 50 states belong to the treaty.

gewusst: The Antarctic Treaty was the first arms control agreement of the Cold War era.
Antarctica is the only continent without states of its own and without a permanent population.

teile.einleitung: The Azores High is a large high-pressure area over the Atlantic, usually near the Azores. It influences the weather in the whole of Europe. If it spreads in summer as far as Central Europe, Switzerland often has sunny and warm days.
wichtigste: The Azores High usually lies over the Atlantic near the Azores.
In a high, air sinks and clouds dissolve.
If it reaches Central Europe, it brings Switzerland fine summer weather.
Its counterpart in the north is the Icelandic Low.
In the Northern Hemisphere the air circles clockwise around a high.

abschnitte.text: In a **high-pressure area** the air pressure is higher than in the surroundings. The air there slowly sinks and warms up as it does so. As a result clouds dissolve, and it usually stays dry and sunny. In the Northern Hemisphere the air flows **clockwise** around a high. The Azores High belongs to a belt of high-pressure areas in the subtropics.

The Azores High usually lies over the Atlantic near the **Azores**, a Portuguese group of islands. In summer it often shifts north. If it spreads as far as **Central Europe**, it keeps rain areas from the Atlantic away. Then Switzerland often enjoys several sunny and warm days in a row. If it retreats, lows with rain can advance again.

Further north there is often the **Icelandic Low**, an area of low air pressure. Between the Azores High and the Icelandic Low the westerly winds blow towards Europe. If both are strongly developed, many lows with mild, moist air reach Europe. Meteorologists watch this interplay closely, because it shapes the weather in Europe strongly.

gewusst: In Europe, high-pressure areas are given names every year, just as low-pressure areas are.

teile.einleitung: The Atchafalaya River is a river in the south of the USA, in the state of Louisiana. It branches water off the Mississippi and flows to the Gulf of Mexico by a route of its own. Because the Mississippi would most like to switch entirely into this river, it is held back by a huge structure.
wichtigste: The Atchafalaya lies in Louisiana in the south of the USA.
It is a distributary of the Mississippi and also takes in water from the Red River.
Its route to the Gulf of Mexico is shorter and steeper than that of the Mississippi.
Since the 1960s the Old River Control Structure has stopped the Mississippi from switching course.
The Atchafalaya Basin is one of the largest swamp areas in the USA.

abschnitte.text: Rivers always look for the easiest way to the sea. In its lower course the Mississippi makes a long bend to New Orleans. The **Atchafalaya**, on the other hand, leads much more directly to the Gulf of Mexico. Because its route is shorter, it also has a steeper **gradient**, that is, more slope. The water therefore prefers to flow in there.

Without intervention the Mississippi would probably move its main channel into the Atchafalaya. Then cities such as Baton Rouge and New Orleans would lie on an almost empty river bed. That is why the US Army Corps of Engineers built the **Old River Control Structure**. Since the 1960s it has used large locks and weirs to regulate how much water reaches the Atchafalaya. In this way a large part stays in the Mississippi.

The Atchafalaya flows through a huge **swamp area** with cypress forests, lakes and oxbows. There live alligators, herons and many fish. People in the area also catch crayfish there. At its mouth the river deposits a lot of mud. In this way a new **delta** is growing there, that is, new land made of deposits.

gewusst: The name Atchafalaya comes from the language of the Choctaw and means roughly “long river”.
In a great flood in 1973 the control structure was badly damaged but held.

teile.einleitung: The clownfish is a small, colourful fish from warm coral reefs. It lives in a sea anemone and has been world-famous since the animated film “Finding Nemo”.
wichtigste: Clownfish live in warm coral reefs in the Indian Ocean and the Pacific.
They live among the tentacles of a sea anemone.
A layer of mucus protects them from the anemone’s stings.
The best-known clownfish is orange with white stripes.
Most grow to about 10 centimetres long.
It is mainly the male that guards the eggs.

abschnitte.text: Clownfish are **small fish**, and most grow to about **10 centimetres** long. The best known is **orange** with **white stripes** that often have a black edge. There are several species in different colours. They are also called **anemonefish**.

Clownfish live in **coral reefs** in the warm **Indian Ocean** and the **Pacific**. There they live among the tentacles of a **sea anemone**. These tentacles have **stinging cells** that hurt other fish. The clownfish, however, has a special **layer of mucus** on its skin, so the tentacles do not sting it.

The clownfish and the sea anemone **help each other**. The anemone protects the fish from enemies. The clownfish **drives off fish** that want to eat the anemone. This kind of living together for mutual benefit is called **symbiosis**.

Clownfish live in small groups. The female is the largest animal in the group. If she dies, the **largest male becomes the new female**. The eggs are laid close to the anemone. It is mainly the **male** that guards them and fans fresh water over them.

In the animated film **“Finding Nemo”**, a clownfish father searches for his son Nemo in the big ocean. After the film, many people wanted a clownfish in their aquarium. Today many clownfish are bred for aquariums so that they do not have to be taken from the reefs.

gewusst: Clownfish can change sex during their lives.
A clownfish usually hardly ever moves far from its anemone.

teile.einleitung: Chile is a very long, narrow country on the west coast of South America. It stretches from the dry Atacama Desert in the north to glaciers and islands in the cold south.
wichtigste: The capital of Chile is Santiago de Chile.
Its neighbours are Peru in the north, Bolivia in the north-east and Argentina in the east.
Chile is over 4,000 kilometres long, but usually less than 200 kilometres wide.
No country produces more copper than Chile.
In 1960 Chile had the strongest earthquake ever measured.
The flag has a white star in a blue field.

abschnitte.text: Chile lies between the **Pacific** in the west and the **Andes** in the east. In the north its neighbour is **Peru**, in the north-east **Bolivia**, and in the east **Argentina**. The flag is white and red, with a blue field in the top left corner containing a **white star**. People speak Spanish, and pay with the Chilean peso. The faraway **Easter Island** also belongs to Chile.

The capital **Santiago de Chile** lies in a valley in front of high mountains. More than a third of all the country’s people live in the greater area. The port city of **Valparaíso** is known for its **colourful houses** on steep hills. Old funicular railways climb the slopes there. The old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

In the north lies the **Atacama Desert**, one of the driest places on Earth. In the middle the climate is mild, and fruit and wine are grown there. In the south there are forests, lakes, fjords and large **glaciers**. Because Chile lies where **tectonic plates** meet, the ground often shakes. The **Valdivia earthquake** of 1960 had a magnitude of 9.5, the strongest ever measured.

Chile has huge **copper mines**, mainly in the north. No other country produces as much **copper**. The metal is used for power cables, electronics and engines. Copper exports are very important for the country’s economy.

A cold ocean current flows off the coast. The **Humboldt penguin**, named after the explorer **Alexander von Humboldt**, lives there. It is found on the coasts of Chile and Peru. In the Andes live llamas, alpacas and the great Andean condor.

gewusst: Chile is more than twenty times as long as it is wide on average.
The Atacama Desert is so dry that large observatories stand there, because the sky is almost always clear.

teile.einleitung: Bycatch is the name for animals that end up unintentionally in the net or on the hook when fishing. They were not what the fishers were after. Bycatch is a big problem for protecting the oceans.
wichtigste: Bycatch means animals that are caught unintentionally.
This includes dolphins, sea turtles, sharks, seabirds and fish that are too small.
Many animals are thrown back into the sea dead or injured.
There is especially a lot of bycatch with large trawl nets and long fishing lines.
Better nets and rules can reduce bycatch.

abschnitte.text: Fishers usually want to catch a particular species, for example tuna or prawns. But other animals end up in the nets too. This unwanted catch is called **bycatch**. It includes **dolphins, sea turtles, sharks** and seabirds. Young fish that are still too small also belong to it. Many of these animals are thrown back into the sea dead or injured.

Some species that often end up as bycatch are **threatened** anyway, such as some sea turtles and sharks. If many young fish die, fewer fish grow up. That harms the whole **ecosystem**, that is, the interplay of all living things in the sea. Especially a lot of bycatch is caused by **trawl nets** that are dragged across the sea floor, and by very long lines with many hooks.

There are nets with **escape openings** through which turtles or small fish can get away. Larger meshes let young fish through. Some nets have devices that send out sounds and so warn dolphins and porpoises. Many countries have rules about where and how fishing is allowed. If you buy fish, in Switzerland too, you can look out for **labels** for sustainable fishing.

gewusst: When catching prawns with trawl nets, there is often more bycatch in the net than prawns.

teile.einleitung: Lignite, also called brown coal, is a brown, soft fuel from the ground. It was formed from plants that grew in swamps and bogs millions of years ago. Lignite is younger than hard coal and gives less energy.
wichtigste: Lignite is geologically younger than hard coal.
It contains more water and therefore gives less energy per kilogram.
Lignite is mostly mined in open-cast mines.
It is mainly burned in power stations to generate electricity.
Burning it produces especially large amounts of CO2.

abschnitte.text: Many millions of years ago, dense forests grew in **swamps and bogs**. Dead plants sank into the water and were covered by mud and sand. Without air, they did not rot completely. Under the pressure of the layers above, they first became **peat** and then **lignite**. If it stays deep in the earth for much longer, it can become **hard coal**.

Lignite is **geologically younger** than hard coal. It is softer, often crumbly, and contains a lot of **water**. For this reason it gives **less energy** per kilogram when burned. It is therefore not transported far, and power stations are often built right next to the pits. Lignite usually lies not very deep and is mined in **open-cast mines**, with huge excavators under the open sky.

Lignite is mainly burned in **power stations** to produce **electricity**. This produces especially large amounts of **CO2**, more than most other ways of generating electricity. Whole villages sometimes have to make way for open-cast mines. Germany has decided to stop generating electricity from coal by 2038 at the latest. In Switzerland, too, some lignite used to be mined, for example in the **Käpfnach mine** in Horgen, which is now a museum.

gewusst: The bucket-wheel excavators in big lignite mines are among the largest land vehicles in the world.
In lignite you can sometimes still find remains of wood, leaves and tree trunks.

teile.einleitung: Chubut is a province in the south of Argentina, in the Patagonia region. What makes it special is that descendants of Welsh settlers have lived here since the 19th century.
wichtigste: Chubut is a province in Patagonia in the south of Argentina.
It lies between the Andes and the Atlantic.
In 1865 settlers from Wales came here.
In some places you can still hear Welsh today.
The Welsh tea houses are well known, for example in the town of Gaiman.

abschnitte.text: In 1865, **emigrants from Wales** arrived by ship on the coast of Chubut. They wanted to found a settlement where they could keep up their **language** and culture. Life in the dry landscape was very hard at first. With irrigation canals, they made the valley of the Chubut river fertile.

In places such as **Gaiman** and Trelew, much recalls the Welsh settlers. There are **tea houses** where tea is served with cake, and chapels in the Welsh style. In some schools, **Welsh** is still taught today. Most people speak Spanish, however.

Chubut includes the **Valdés Peninsula**, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. There you can watch whales, elephant seals, sea lions and penguins. Inland, Patagonia is wide, windy and dry. In the west, the province reaches the Andes with lakes and forests.

gewusst: Patagonia is one of the few places outside Britain where Welsh is spoken.

teile.einleitung: Antarctica is the continent around the South Pole and the coldest place on Earth. It is almost entirely covered by a thick shield of ice and has no towns and no permanent inhabitants. Only penguins, seals and researchers brave the icy cold here.
wichtigste: Antarctica is the southernmost continent and lies around the South Pole.
It is almost entirely covered with ice.
The weather is mostly very cold, stormy and dry.
Penguins live in Antarctica, for example emperor penguins.
Researchers live there only for a time in research stations.
In the Antarctic ice is most of the Earth’s fresh water.
The Antarctic Treaty provides that Antarctica may only be used peacefully.

abschnitte.text: Antarctica lies at the southern end of the Earth and is surrounded by the **Southern Ocean**. It covers about 14 million square kilometres, so it is larger than Europe. In the middle of the continent lies the **South Pole**. The highest mountain is the Vinson Massif at almost 4,900 metres.

The **ice sheet** of Antarctica is on average about two kilometres thick, in some places almost five kilometres. In it around 70 per cent of the Earth’s fresh water is stored. In 1983 the lowest air temperature ever measured, minus 89.2 degrees, was recorded at the Russian station Vostok. Although there is so much ice, hardly any snow falls, which is why Antarctica counts as the largest **cold desert** in the world.

On the coasts live various **penguins**, such as emperor penguins and Adélie penguins. Emperor penguins breed in the middle of the icy winter and warm their egg on their feet. In the sea swim seals, whales and countless small crustaceans called **krill**, which serve many animals as food. There are no polar bears here, they live only in the Arctic at the North Pole.

For a long time Antarctica was unexplored because it is so remote and cold. On 14 December 1911 the Norwegian **Roald Amundsen** and his team were the first to reach the South Pole. The Briton Robert Falcon Scott arrived about a month later and died with his companions on the way back. Today an American research station stands at the South Pole.

In Antarctica there are dozens of **research stations** of various countries. In summer a few thousand people work there, in the dark winter considerably fewer. They study, for example, ancient ice to find out what the climate was like in the past. The **Antarctic Treaty** of 1959 forbids military use and the mining of mineral resources, and Switzerland has also joined it.

Antarctica plays an important part in the climate of the whole Earth. If its ice melts, sea level rises everywhere in the world. Researchers therefore watch closely how the glaciers and sea ice change. Swiss researchers are also involved in such projects.

begriffe.erklaerung: A huge, thick layer of ice that covers a whole country or continent.
A very dry region with hardly any precipitation that is very cold.
Small, shrimp-like crustaceans that live in huge swarms in the sea.
A building in which scientists live and work to study something.
The southernmost point of the Earth.

gewusst: At the South Pole the sun does not set for months in summer and does not rise for months in winter.
If all the ice of Antarctica melted, sea level would rise by around 58 metres.
Antarctica has no time zone of its own, and each station mostly uses the time of its home country or its supply base.

teile.einleitung: The Bahamas are an island state in the Atlantic Ocean, south-east of Florida. They consist of around 700 islands with white beaches and turquoise water. Here Christopher Columbus first set foot on land in the Americas in 1492.
wichtigste: The Bahamas lie in the Atlantic, not in the Caribbean Sea.
They consist of around 700 islands, only a few of them inhabited.
The capital is Nassau on the island of New Providence.
The official language is English.
In 1973 the Bahamas became independent from Great Britain.
The national bird is the flamingo.

abschnitte.text: The Bahamas consist of around **700 islands** and many tiny rocks and sandbanks. People live on only a few of the islands. The islands are flat and made of **limestone**. They lie in the **Atlantic Ocean**, south-east of Florida in the USA. The water around the islands is often very shallow and glows turquoise.

On **12 October 1492** **Christopher Columbus** landed on an island in the Bahamas. The native people called it **Guanahani**, and Columbus gave it the name San Salvador. It was his first landing in the Americas. Later the Bahamas became a **British colony**. In **1973** they became an independent state but still belong to the Commonwealth.

The capital **Nassau** lies on the island of **New Providence**. A large part of the population lives there. Because the Bahamas were British for a long time, **English** is the official language. People pay with the Bahamian dollar. The most important branch of the economy is **tourism**: many cruise ships dock at Nassau.

The **flamingo** is the national bird of the Bahamas. On the island of **Inagua** especially many of them live. Also famous are the **swimming pigs** of Big Major Cay. These domestic pigs live on the beach of a small island and swim out to visitors’ boats. They are a popular tourist attraction.

The Bahamas lie in an area where **hurricanes** often form in late summer and autumn. These are enormous tropical storms with strong wind and rain. Because the islands are so flat, the sea can push far inland in a storm. In 2019 Hurricane Dorian caused great damage on some islands.

gewusst: Off the island of Andros lies one of the longest coral reefs in the world.
In the Bahamas people drive on the left, as in Great Britain.

teile.einleitung: An estuary is a special kind of river mouth. The river widens like a funnel towards the sea, and low and high tide reach far inland. Many of the world’s great ports lie on such river mouths.
wichtigste: An estuary is a funnel-shaped river mouth influenced by the tides.
In an estuary fresh water mixes with salt water to make brackish water.
In the turbidity zone many suspended particles collect.
The port of Hamburg lies on the estuary of the Elbe.
The Gironde in France is formed from the Garonne and Dordogne.
The Río de la Plata is the estuary of the Paraná and the Uruguay.

abschnitte.text: An **estuary** is a river mouth that opens out **like a funnel** towards the sea. What matters is the **tides**, that is, low and high tide. At high tide the seawater presses far upstream, and at low tide the water flows out again. In the process sand and mud are flushed out, so the mouth stays open. A **delta** is different: there the river deposits a lot of material and splits into several arms.

In an estuary the **fresh water** of the river meets the **salt water** of the sea. **Brackish water** with a medium salt content is formed. Where the two kinds of water meet, fine particles clump together and are moved back and forth by the tides. This creates the **turbidity zone**, where the water is especially cloudy. Only animals and plants that can cope with changing salt content live here.

The port of **Hamburg** lies around 100 kilometres inland on the **Elbe**. Because the tides reach into the port, large ships use the high tide. In France the **Garonne** and **Dordogne** join north of Bordeaux to form the **Gironde**, which counts as the largest estuary in Western Europe. The **Thames** widens below London into a broad estuary towards the North Sea. To protect against storm surges the **Thames Barrier** was built there.

In South America the **Paraná** and **Uruguay** flow together and form the **Río de la Plata**. On its banks lie the capitals Buenos Aires and Montevideo. In Canada the **St Lawrence River** connects the Great Lakes with the Atlantic. Its estuary becomes many dozens of kilometres wide towards the gulf. It is among the largest estuaries in the world.

gewusst: The Río de la Plata is so wide at its mouth that you cannot see the other bank.
The Rhine, which rises in Switzerland, does not end in an estuary but in a delta in the Netherlands.

teile.einleitung: Population growth describes how the number of people on Earth, in a country or in a city changes over time. It depends on how many children are born, how many people die and how many move in or out. Since 2022 over 8 billion people have lived on Earth.
wichtigste: According to the UN, the world population passed the mark of 8 billion in November 2022.
Since 2023, according to a UN estimate, India has been the most populous country in the world.
Natural growth is the birth rate minus the death rate.
At 2 per cent growth per year, a population doubles after around 35 years.
With about 2.1 children per woman, a population stays the same size in the long run without immigration.
Thomas Robert Malthus warned in 1798 that population grows faster than food.
The model of the demographic transition describes how births and deaths change as a country develops.

abschnitte.text: For a long time the world population grew only very slowly, because many children died young. Around the year 1800 there were for the first time about **1 billion** people on Earth. After that things went faster and faster: in 1927 there were 2 billion, in 1974 already 4 billion. In November 2022, according to the UN, the mark of **8 billion** was passed.

Births and deaths are often measured in **per mille**, that is, per 1,000 inhabitants. If a country has a birth rate of 30 and a death rate of 10 per mille, it grows naturally by 20 per mille, that is by 2 per cent a year. At this pace a population doubles after around 35 years. Added to this is **migration**, that is, people moving in or out.

The model of the **demographic transition** divides development into phases. At first birth rate and death rate are both high, and the population hardly grows. Thanks to better medicine, hygiene and nutrition, the death rate then falls while the birth rate stays high, and now the population grows most strongly. Later the birth rate falls too, and growth becomes slow again.

Since 2023, according to a UN estimate, India has had more inhabitants than China, with each having over 1.4 billion people. In many countries of Africa the population is still growing strongly, because women there have many children on average. In Europe, Japan or South Korea, by contrast, fewer than 2.1 children per woman are born, the so-called **replacement level**. Without immigration these countries would shrink in the long run.

The English scholar **Thomas Robert Malthus** wrote in 1798 that population grows faster than food production. He therefore feared famines. His warning did not come true worldwide in this way, because farming brought far more yield thanks to fertiliser, machines and new varieties. Even so, the question of how everyone gets enough food and water is still important today.

Around 1900 about 3.3 million people lived in Switzerland. In 2023, according to the Federal Statistical Office, the 9 million mark was passed. Growth today comes mainly from **immigration**, because only few children are born per woman. As a result the population is also becoming more diverse.

begriffe.erklaerung: The number of births per 1,000 inhabitants in a year.
The number of deaths per 1,000 inhabitants in a year.
About 2.1 children per woman, so that each generation replaces the previous one.
When people move to another country or another area.

gewusst: The world needed only about 11 years to go from 7 to 8 billion people.
The UN expects the world population to reach a peak in this century and then fall slightly.

teile.einleitung: Australia is the smallest continent on Earth and at the same time a single large country. It lies in the Southern Hemisphere between the Indian and the Pacific Ocean. Here kangaroos hop through the dry outback, koalas sleep in eucalyptus trees, and in the middle of the desert the red rock Uluru glows.
wichtigste: Australia is a continent and a state at the same time.
The capital is Canberra, not Sydney.
The kangaroo carries its young in a pouch and lives only in Australia.
The koala sleeps a great deal and eats eucalyptus leaves.
Uluru is a famous red rock in the heart of Australia.
Aboriginal Australians have lived in Australia for at least 50,000 years.
Because Australia lies in the Southern Hemisphere, it is summer there when it is winter here.

abschnitte.text: Australia lies south-east of Asia, surrounded by the **Indian Ocean** and the **Pacific**. The country covers about 7.7 million square kilometres, so around 186 times as big as Switzerland. Even so, only about 27 million people live there (as of 2024). The large island of Tasmania in the south also belongs to the state.

Most of the interior is hot and dry and is called the **outback**. In the middle of it stands **Uluru**, a huge sandstone rock that rises about 350 metres from the plain and glows red at sunset. Off the north-east coast lies the **Great Barrier Reef**, the largest coral reef in the world, more than 2,000 kilometres long. In the south-east there are mountains, forests and beaches.

Many of Australia’s animals are found nowhere else in the world. The **kangaroo** and the koala are **marsupials**, and their young grow up in a pouch on the mother’s belly. The koala eats almost only eucalyptus leaves and sleeps up to 20 hours a day, because its food supplies little energy. The platypus is a mammal that lays eggs, and the emu is a large flightless bird.

The **Aboriginal Australians** are the first inhabitants of Australia and have one of the oldest cultures in the world. For them Uluru is a sacred place, which is why climbing the rock has been forbidden since 2019. In 1770 the British navigator James Cook explored the east coast. From 1788 the British founded colonies, first near Sydney, and in 1901 Australia became a federation of its own.

Most people live on the coast, especially in the south-east. The largest cities are **Sydney** with its famous Opera House and Melbourne. Because the two cities could not agree on which should be the capital, the new capital **Canberra** was built between them for the purpose. The official language is English, and many people descend from immigrants from Europe and Asia.

Australia is often confused with Austria, because the names sound similar in English, namely Australia and Austria. From Switzerland you usually fly for over 20 hours to reach Australia. Because the country lies on the other side of the Earth, it is, for example, midday there when it is deep night here. Some Swiss emigrant families also live in Australia today.

begriffe.erklaerung: A mammal whose young grows up in a pouch on the mother’s belly.
The dry, hardly inhabited interior of Australia.
The first inhabitants of Australia, who lived there long before the Europeans.
A reef in warm seas made of the limestone skeletons of tiny coral animals.
The half of the Earth that lies south of the equator.

gewusst: In Australia there are more kangaroos than people.
The Great Barrier Reef is so large that you can even see it from space.
With its bill the platypus can sense weak electrical signals from its prey.

teile.einleitung: Altocumulus is the technical name for the familiar “sheep” clouds. These clouds consist of many small puffs and look like a flock of sheep in the sky. They float at medium height.
wichtigste: Altocumulus is popularly called “sheep” clouds.
They consist of many small cloud puffs.
They lie at medium height, roughly between 2 and 7 kilometres.
The name comes from Latin.
They mostly consist of tiny water droplets.

abschnitte.text: “Sheep” clouds are called **altocumulus** in technical language. They consist of many small, white or grey **cloud puffs**. They are often arranged in rows or fields. From below it looks like a **flock of sheep** moving across the sky. That is where the name comes from.

The name comes from **Latin**: “altus” means high and “cumulus” means heap. Altocumulus are **mid-level clouds**. In our latitudes they lie roughly between **2 and 7 kilometres** in height. They mostly consist of tiny **water droplets**, sometimes also of ice crystals.

abschnitte.titel: Mixing them up with other clouds
abschnitte.text: **Cirrocumulus** look similar. But they lie higher and their puffs look much smaller. Lower down are the **stratocumulus**, whose puffs look larger and darker. A simple trick: if you stretch out your arm, the puffs of altocumulus are about as wide as one to three fingers.

gewusst: Altocumulus on a muggy summer morning can be a sign of thunderstorms later.

teile.einleitung: The Chinook is a warm, dry downslope wind on the eastern side of the Rocky Mountains in North America. It works in a similar way to the foehn in Switzerland and can make snow melt quickly in winter.
wichtigste: The Chinook blows on the eastern side of the Rocky Mountains in Canada and the USA.
It is a foehn-like, warm and dry downslope wind.
The air warms as it descends from the mountains.
It can make the temperature rise sharply within hours.
Because it makes snow vanish quickly, it is also called the “snow eater”.

abschnitte.text: Moist air from the Pacific rises over the Rocky Mountains, cools and loses its moisture as rain or snow. On the other side, the **air sinks** again. As it does so, it warms **dry-adiabatically**, which means that because it is compressed, it gets warmer without any heat coming from outside. In this way it arrives warm and dry in the valley.

The **foehn** in the Swiss Alps forms in exactly the same way. During a foehn, it is often warm and very clear on the north side of the Alps. The Chinook is therefore a foehn-like wind, only on a different continent. With both, a typical wall or arch of cloud often forms above the mountains.

In winter the Chinook can make the temperature rise sharply **within hours**. The snow then melts very quickly or even evaporates. That is why it is also called the **snow eater**. It is especially well known in the Canadian city of **Calgary**, where it often interrupts the winter cold.

gewusst: The name Chinook comes from a native people in the north-west of North America.

teile.einleitung: The Chilean pine, or monkey puzzle tree, is a striking conifer from the Andes. With its hard, spiky leaves it looks almost prehistoric, and it is the national tree of Chile.
wichtigste: The monkey puzzle tree grows in the Andes in the south of Chile and in neighbouring Argentina.
It has hard, pointed, scale-like leaves.
It is the national tree of Chile.
Its large seeds were an important food for the Mapuche people.
The tree grows slowly and can live to a great age.

abschnitte.text: The **monkey puzzle tree**, also called the **Chilean pine**, has branches thickly covered with triangular, hard and **pointed leaves**. Old trees have a tall, straight trunk and an umbrella-shaped crown. The family of araucaria trees is very old and already existed at the time of the dinosaurs.

The tree produces large cones with many edible **seeds**. For the **Mapuche** people, especially the Pehuenche, these seeds were an important **food**. They can be boiled, roasted or ground into flour. In their language the tree is called Pehuén, and it still has great importance for them today.

The monkey puzzle tree is the **national tree** of Chile and is protected there. Its natural forests have become smaller through logging and fires. In Europe it is often planted as an **ornamental tree** in gardens and parks, including in Switzerland in mild places.

gewusst: Some monkey puzzle trees in the Andes are well over 1,000 years old.

teile.einleitung: Australia is the smallest continent on Earth and at the same time a state of its own. It is surrounded by sea on all sides and is known for kangaroos, deserts and the Sydney Opera House. Together with New Zealand and many islands in the Pacific it forms the region of Oceania.
wichtigste: Australia is a continent and a country at once.
It is entirely surrounded by sea: the Pacific to the east, the Indian Ocean to the west.
In the interior it is mostly hot and dry, and most people live on the coasts.
Typical animals are kangaroos and koalas.
The main language is English.
South-east of Australia lies New Zealand.

abschnitte.text: Australia is the only continent that is almost entirely taken up by a single state. It borders no other continent and is surrounded by **sea** on all sides. To the east lies the **Pacific**, to the west the **Indian Ocean**. Together with New Zealand and many Pacific islands, Australia belongs to the region of **Oceania**. The capital of the country is **Canberra**, but the largest city is Sydney.

Large parts of the interior of Australia are **hot and dry**. There are deserts, steppes and red earth. Australians call this area the **outback**. In the middle of it stands **Uluru**, a huge red rock. It is sacred to the **Aboriginal Australians**, the first inhabitants of Australia. Because the interior is so dry, most people live on the coasts.

Australia was separated from other continents for a very long time. That is why quite distinctive animals developed there. The best known is the **kangaroo**, which lives wild only in Australia and on New Guinea. It is even on the country’s coat of arms. The **koala**, the wombat and the platypus also live there. Many of these animals carry their young in a pouch.

In Australia people speak mainly **English**, because the country was a British colony for a long time. The large cities such as Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane lie by the sea. In Sydney the famous **Opera House** stands right on the harbour. Its white roofs look like sails. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Off the north-east coast lies the **Great Barrier Reef**, the largest coral reef in the world. It is so large that you can even see it from space. Countless colourful fish, turtles and corals live there. Because the water is getting warmer, many corals are threatened today.

gewusst: When it is winter in Switzerland, it is summer in Australia, because the country lies in the Southern Hemisphere.
In Australia there are more kangaroos than people.

teile.einleitung: Coltan is a dark ore from which the metals tantalum and niobium are obtained. Tantalum is found in almost every smartphone, but mining sometimes takes place under disputed conditions.
wichtigste: The name coltan is short for columbite and tantalite.
The metals tantalum and niobium are obtained from coltan.
Tantalum is mainly used for capacitors in smartphones and laptops.
In eastern Congo, armed groups partly finance themselves through the coltan trade.
Tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold are regarded as conflict minerals (3TG).
Since 2022, due diligence duties have applied in Switzerland to such raw materials.

abschnitte.text: **Coltan** is not a single mineral but a mixture of **columbite** and **tantalite**. That is where the name comes from. The two minerals contain the metals **niobium** and **tantalum**. In small amounts, niobium makes **steel** stronger for pipelines and bridges.

Tantalum is mainly used for **capacitors**. These are small components that store electric charge. **Tantalum capacitors** store a lot of charge in a tiny space and are very reliable. That is why they are found in smartphones, laptops and many other devices.

A large part of the coltan comes from Central Africa. In the provinces of **North and South Kivu** in the east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, it is often mined by hand under difficult conditions. **Armed groups** there partly finance themselves through the trade. That is why people speak of **conflict minerals**.

**Tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold**, or **3TG** for short, are regarded as conflict minerals. In the USA, the **Dodd-Frank Act** of 2010 requires listed companies to disclose where they come from. In the EU, a regulation on **due diligence** for importers has applied since 1 January 2021. In **Switzerland**, due diligence and reporting duties on conflict minerals and child labour have applied since 1 January 2022, as a counter-proposal to the Responsible Business Initiative.

The element **tantalum** is named after **Tantalus**, a figure from Greek legend. Tantalus stood up to his chin in water but could never drink. In a similar way, tantalum takes up hardly anything even in **acid**. It is therefore very resistant to corrosion.

gewusst: The phrase “the torments of Tantalus” still describes a longing that is never satisfied.
Tantalum is so well tolerated that it is also used for medical implants.

teile.einleitung: The Casiquiare is a natural river in Venezuela. It links the Orinoco river system with that of the Amazon. A river fork like this is called a bifurcation, and it is very rare in the world.
wichtigste: The Casiquiare lies in the south of Venezuela.
It branches off from the Orinoco and flows to the Rio Negro.
The Rio Negro is a tributary of the Amazon.
In this way two great river systems are linked naturally.
A river fork like this is called a bifurcation.

abschnitte.text: Normally a **watershed** separates two river systems. Rain that falls on one side flows into one river, and on the other side into another. With the **Casiquiare** it is different. It **branches off from the Orinoco** and flows to the **Rio Negro**, a large tributary of the **Amazon**. Part of the Orinoco’s water thus reaches the Amazon. A river fork like this is called a **bifurcation**.

Indigenous people and missionaries had known about the link for a long time. In Europe, however, many scholars did not believe in it. In **1800**, the German explorer **Alexander von Humboldt** and the Frenchman **Aimé Bonpland** travelled along the Casiquiare. They confirmed that the Orinoco and the Amazon really are connected. Humboldt later described the journey in detail.

abschnitte.titel: In the middle of the rainforest
abschnitte.text: The Casiquiare flows through dense **tropical rainforest** in the south of Venezuela. The area is very remote, and there are hardly any roads. Boats are the most important means of transport. **Indigenous peoples** live in the region and use the river for fishing and travel.

gewusst: In theory you can travel by boat from the Orinoco to the Amazon without leaving the water.
The Casiquiare is regarded as the best-known example of a river fork in the world.

teile.einleitung: The Beagle Channel is a strait at the very south of South America, near Tierra del Fuego. It connects the Atlantic with the Pacific and forms part of the border between Argentina and Chile. It is named after the ship on which Charles Darwin later also travelled.
wichtigste: The Beagle Channel lies near Tierra del Fuego in the south of South America.
It is named after the ship HMS Beagle.
The Beagle explored the waterway around 1830.
On its shore lies the Argentine city of Ushuaia.
Part of the border between Argentina and Chile runs through the channel.

abschnitte.text: **HMS Beagle** was a ship of the British navy. On its first research voyage around **1830** it explored the waters around **Tierra del Fuego**. In doing so the strait was discovered and named after the ship. On the second voyage of the Beagle from 1831, the young naturalist **Charles Darwin** was on board. He also saw the channel and observed the plants, animals and people of the area.

The channel is around **240 kilometres** long and narrow in many places. On both sides mountains rise up, which carry snow in winter. On the north shore lies the Argentine city of **Ushuaia**, which is often called the southernmost city in the world. On the Chilean side lies the small town of **Puerto Williams**. Sea lions, cormorants and other seabirds live in the channel.

Argentina and Chile argued for a long time over who owned some **islands** at the eastern end of the channel. In 1978 the situation was very tense. Then the **Pope** mediated between the two countries. In 1984 they signed a **peace treaty** that fixed the border.

gewusst: In the channel, on a small rocky island off Ushuaia, stands a red-and-white lighthouse that is very popular with tourists.

teile.einleitung: The Antarctic Ice Sheet is the largest mass of ice on Earth. It covers almost the whole continent of Antarctica and is on average around two kilometres thick. In its ice lies a huge archive of climate history.
wichtigste: Around 90 per cent of the Earth’s ice lies in the Antarctic Ice Sheet.
It also stores most of the world’s fresh water.
On average the ice is around 2 kilometres thick.
Ice cores show the climate of the last 800,000 years or so.
Cold fall winds, the katabatic winds, flow down to the coast.
Beneath the ice lies the hidden Gamburtsev Mountains.
In blue ice fields you find especially many meteorites.

abschnitte.text: The ice sheet covers almost all of **Antarctica**. It contains around **90 per cent** of the Earth’s ice and most of its fresh water. On average the ice is around **2 kilometres** thick, in some places over 4 kilometres. That is why Antarctica is the continent with the greatest average height. The **Transantarctic Mountains** divide the ice sheet into a larger eastern and a smaller western part.

Beneath the ice are hidden mountains, valleys and lakes. The **Gamburtsev Mountains** in East Antarctica are about as extensive as the Alps but lie under more than 600 metres of ice. They were discovered by measurements from a Soviet expedition in 1958. It is thought that this is where the ice sheet began to grow. Beneath the ice there are also lakes of liquid water, such as **Lake Vostok**.

The ice does not lie still, it slowly **flows** to the sea. It moves especially fast in **ice streams**, which often travel hundreds of metres a year. Through them the ice sheet loses a large part of its mass. At the coast the ice pushes out over the sea and forms floating **ice shelves**. Icebergs break off from them.

Above the high ice the air cools greatly and becomes heavy. It then flows downhill to the coast. These cold fall winds are called **katabatic winds**. At some coastal places they reach hurricane force. At Vostok station in 1983 one of the lowest air temperatures ever measured was recorded, almost minus 90 degrees.

Tiny **air bubbles** containing old air are trapped in the ice. Researchers drill out long **ice cores**, for example at Dome C in East Antarctica. From them they read off the CO₂ content and the temperatures of the last **800,000 years** or so. The **University of Bern** was also involved. In **blue ice fields** you also find many meteorites, because the flowing ice carries them there.

gewusst: If the whole Antarctic Ice Sheet melted, sea level would rise by many dozens of metres.
The ice is so heavy that it presses the bedrock beneath it down into the depths.

teile.einleitung: The Altiplano is a huge high plateau in the Andes in South America. It lies at around 3,500 to 4,000 metres above sea level. On it lies the famous Lake Titicaca.
wichtigste: The Altiplano is a high plateau in the Andes.
It lies at around 3,500 to 4,000 metres.
It extends over parts of Peru, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina.
Lake Titicaca lies on the Altiplano.
After the Tibetan Plateau it is the second-largest high plateau on Earth.

abschnitte.text: The name **Altiplano** is Spanish and means **high plain**. It lies at around **3,500 to 4,000 metres** above sea level, so higher than most peaks in the Swiss Alps. The Altiplano extends over parts of **Peru**, **Bolivia**, **Chile** and **Argentina**. It is regarded as the **second-largest high plateau** in the world, and only the **Tibetan Plateau** is larger.

The Altiplano lies between two chains of the Andes: the **Western Cordillera** (Cordillera Occidental) and the **Eastern Cordillera** (Cordillera Oriental). It is a **high basin**. Over a long time it was filled with **debris** worn away from the mountains. This is how the wide, flat plain came about.

On the Altiplano lies **Lake Titicaca**, on the border between Peru and Bolivia. It is among the highest large lakes on Earth. Life on the Altiplano is hard because of the thin air and cold nights. Even so, people have lived here for thousands of years, keeping **llamas** and **alpacas**, for example.

gewusst: The Altiplano lies more than twice as high as the highest peak of the Swiss Jura.

teile.einleitung: Bangladesh is a country in South Asia with very many people in little space. Apart from city-states and microstates, it is the most densely populated large country in the world. Fertile soils make this possible, while floods and storms make it dangerous.
wichtigste: At the 2022 census Bangladesh had around 170 million inhabitants.
On just under 150,000 km² live over 1,100 people per km².
Switzerland has around 220 inhabitants per km², so Bangladesh is about five times more densely populated.
The country lies largely in the delta of the Ganges and Brahmaputra.
Floods and cyclones threaten millions of people.
The capital and largest city is Dhaka.

abschnitte.text: **Population density** states how many people on average live on one square kilometre. You calculate **number of inhabitants divided by area**. Bangladesh has around 170 million inhabitants on just under 150,000 km², which gives over **1,100 inhabitants per km²**. Switzerland has around 9 million inhabitants on around 41,000 km², so about 220 per km². Only city-states and microstates such as **Monaco** or **Singapore** are more densely populated still.

Bangladesh lies largely in the **delta** of the great rivers **Ganges** and **Brahmaputra**. The rivers bring fertile mud, which is deposited as **alluvial land**. Together with the rain of the **monsoon**, this allows several **rice harvests** a year. That is why so many people can live and feed themselves here. Most people still live in the countryside today.

Large parts of the country lie only a few metres above the sea. **Monsoon floods** cover wide areas every year. From the Bay of Bengal, tropical cyclones move across the coast. Because so many people live close together, millions are often affected. A rising **sea level** increases the risk. Bangladesh is therefore building more protective structures and warning systems.

The capital **Dhaka** has over 20 million people in its urban area and is among the most densely populated cities in the world. Since the 1970s the **fertility rate**, that is, the average number of children per woman, has fallen from over 6 to around 2. Better **education**, especially for girls, and better health care contributed to this. Bangladesh is regarded as a success story in this respect.

gewusst: Bangladesh is about three and a half times the size of Switzerland but has almost twenty times as many inhabitants.
Bangladesh is one of the ten most populous countries in the world.

teile.einleitung: Chiloé is a large island in the south of Chile. It is famous for its colourful wooden churches and for houses that stand on stilts above the water.
wichtigste: Chiloé lies off the coast of southern Chile in the Pacific.
On the island stand many churches built entirely of wood.
Sixteen of these churches are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
The main town of the island is Castro.
In Castro stand colourful stilt houses, the palafitos.

abschnitte.text: From the 18th century, craftsmen on Chiloé built **churches entirely of wood**. Missionaries brought the idea, but it was mainly the island’s people who built the churches. Many churches have colourful walls of wooden shingles and a tall tower at the front. **Sixteen** of them have been **UNESCO World Heritage Sites** since 2000.

In the main town of **Castro** stand colourful **palafitos**. These are wooden houses on stilts that stand above the water at high tide. Fishing families could thus travel straight to their house by boat. Today the palafitos are a popular subject for photographs.

It is often damp and rainy on Chiloé, which is why the landscape is very green. People live from **fishing**, farming and tourism. You reach the mainland by **ferry** across a narrow strait. The island has its own legends and customs, which have made it well known.

gewusst: The wooden churches of Chiloé combine European building skills with the knowledge of the local craftsmen.

teile.einleitung: Brazil is the largest country in South America. It is known for the Amazon rainforest, for football and for the carnival. People in Brazil speak Portuguese, because the country was a Portuguese colony for a long time.
wichtigste: Brazil is the largest country in South America, and its capital is Brasília.
In the 2022 census, around 203 million people were counted.
The largest city is São Paulo.
The official language is Portuguese, and the currency is the real.
Brazil has won the men’s football World Cup five times (as of 2026).
The flag is green with a yellow diamond and a blue globe.

abschnitte.text: In area, Brazil is the **largest country in South America** and one of the largest in the world. It borders almost all the other countries of the continent. The **equator** crosses the north of the country, and the **Tropic of Capricorn** passes just by **São Paulo**. In the north lies a large part of the **Amazon rainforest**, the largest rainforest on Earth. The capital is **Brasília** in the interior.

In the **2022** census, around **203 million** people were counted. That is more than twenty times as many as in Switzerland. The largest city is **São Paulo**, with over 11 million inhabitants, the largest city in all of South America. **Rio de Janeiro** is also very well known, with the statue of Christ on a mountain above the city. The people of Brazil have ancestors from Europe, Africa, Asia and among the indigenous peoples.

Brazil was for a long time a **Portuguese colony**. That is why **Portuguese** is the official language, while most neighbouring countries speak Spanish. Brazil became independent in **1822**. Since 1994 people have paid with the **real**. The flag is **green** with a **yellow diamond**. In the middle is a **blue globe** with stars and a band with the motto “Ordem e Progresso”, meaning “Order and Progress”.

Football is very popular in Brazil. The men won the World Cup **five times**: in 1958, 1962, 1970, 1994 and 2002 (as of 2026). No other country has won more often. The most famous player was **Pelé**. He became a **three-time world champion**, in 1958, 1962 and 1970. No other player has managed that.

The **carnival** takes place every year before Lent. In Rio, **samba schools** parade with enormous floats and colourful costumes along a specially built street, the Sambadrome. **Capoeira** also comes from Brazil. This martial art looks like a dance and is practised to **music and singing**. It was developed by people of African descent.

gewusst: Brazil is the largest coffee producer in the world.
On the border with Argentina lie the mighty Iguazú Falls.
Brazil has more Portuguese-speaking inhabitants than Portugal itself.

t1q7k1jm.t: Labour migration to the Gulf states

teile.einleitung: Since the 1970s millions of people from other countries have worked in the Gulf states. They build cities and work in shops, hotels and homes. Human rights organisations often criticise their situation, while the states point to reforms.
wichtigste: The strong labour migration began with the rise in oil prices from 1973.
Most workers come from South Asia.
In Qatar around 85 to 90 per cent of the population are foreigners.
The kafala system ties residence to an employer.
The Gulf Cooperation Council consists of six states.
The 2022 football World Cup in Qatar drew attention to working conditions.
In 2021 Qatar introduced a minimum wage for all workers.

abschnitte.text: From **1973** oil prices rose sharply. The Gulf states suddenly took in a great deal of money and built roads, ports, hospitals and whole cities. The local population, however, was small. That is why the states brought in **millions of foreign workers**. The destination countries include the six members of the **Gulf Cooperation Council**: Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman.

Most workers come from **South Asia**, above all from India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Nepal. Many also come from the Philippines or from Africa. They work in **construction**, in services and as **domestic workers**. In **Qatar** only about a tenth of the inhabitants hold citizenship. Around 85 to 90 per cent are foreign workers and their families.

For a long time the **kafala system** applied in the Gulf states. Under it the employer is the **sponsor** of the worker. Changing jobs or leaving the country was therefore often possible only with his consent. It is also criticised that some employers keep **passports**, even though this is forbidden in many places. The workers can then neither quit nor leave the country.

Before the **2022 football World Cup** in Qatar, stadiums, roads and hotels were built mainly by migrant workers. Human rights organisations criticised the heat, wage fraud and deaths on building sites. Qatar pointed to reforms: in March **2021** a **minimum wage** came into force that applies to everyone regardless of nationality. The International Labour Organization (ILO) praised it as the first of its kind in the region. Other Gulf states have also adjusted their rules.

Many workers send a large part of their wages home. These **remittances** are very important for their families and countries of origin. One example is the Indian state of **Kerala**. Since the 1970s very many people from there have worked in the Gulf. In Kerala their money shapes house building, consumption and education.

gewusst: In several Gulf states, clearly more foreigners than locals live.
The word “kafala” comes from Arabic and means roughly sponsorship.

teile.einleitung: A population pyramid is a diagram that shows the age structure of a population. In it you can see how many men and women there are in each age group. From its shape you can tell whether a country is young or ageing.
wichtigste: The population pyramid shows the population by age and sex.
At the bottom are the youngest, at the top the oldest.
A country with many children has a pyramid with a broad base.
With a stable population a bell shape appears.
If there are fewer children than adults, an urn shape appears.
Without immigration it takes about 2.1 children per woman for the population to stay the same size.
In Switzerland this figure was around 1.3 in 2024.

abschnitte.text: A **population pyramid** consists of many horizontal bars. On one side are the men, on the other the women. From bottom to top, people are ordered by **year of age**: the youngest at the bottom, the oldest at the top. The longer a bar is, the more people there are of that age. This way you can see the **age structure** of a country at a glance.

If very many children are born, the bottom bar is the broadest. Going upwards the diagram becomes narrow, because fewer people grow old. That is the **pyramid with a broad base**. In the **bell shape** the lower bars are about equally broad, and the population stays about the same size. In the **urn shape** the lower part is narrower than the middle. The population is ageing and, without immigration, shrinking.

For a population to stay the same size without immigration, it takes on average about **2.1 children per woman**. Two children replace the parents. The extra tenth makes up for the fact that not all children grow up themselves and that slightly more boys than girls are born. In **Niger** a woman has around 6 children on average, and the population there is very young. **Japan** has had few births for decades, its pyramid has an urn shape, and its population has been shrinking since around 2010.

According to the **Federal Statistical Office**, Switzerland’s birth rate in 2024 was around **1.3 children per woman**. That is the lowest value ever measured. At the same time the **baby boom generation** is reaching retirement age, and life expectancy is rising. That is why the group of people **over 65** is growing especially strongly. This matters, for example, for the **AHV**, the state pension scheme, because more pensions have to be paid.

gewusst: Switzerland’s population is growing despite fewer births, mainly because of immigration.
Wars and baby boom years can still be seen in a population pyramid decades later as notches or bulges.

teile.einleitung: The mountain pine beetle is a small bark beetle from the west of North America. Since the 1990s it has killed huge pine forests in the Rocky Mountains and in British Columbia. Mild winters helped it do so.
wichtigste: The mountain pine beetle is only a few millimetres long.
It bores under the bark of pine trees.
Since the 1990s it has multiplied massively in Canada and the USA.
Mild winters let many larvae survive.
Dead forests can burn more easily.

abschnitte.text: The **mountain pine beetle** belongs to the **bark beetles**. It is only about half a centimetre long. The females bore through the bark of pine trees and lay their eggs there. The **larvae** eat their way under the bark through the layer that carries the tree’s sap. The beetles also bring a fungus with them. If a tree is attacked by very many beetles, it dies.

Since the 1990s the beetle has multiplied massively in the **Rocky Mountains** and in the Canadian province of **British Columbia**. Huge pine forests turned red and died. Normally very cold winters kill a large part of the larvae. But because of **mild winters**, far more survived. Large pine forests of the same age also offered the beetle plenty of food.

Dead trees dry out and can easily **burn**. The timber industry lost a lot of wood. A dead forest also no longer stores **carbon dioxide** but releases some as it rots or burns. Researchers see the outbreak as an example of how **climate change** can alter forests. Switzerland also knows problems with bark beetles, here mainly on spruces.

gewusst: The beetle infestation in British Columbia is regarded as one of the largest insect outbreaks ever observed in North America.

teile.einleitung: The Chicago River flows through the middle of the big city of Chicago in the USA. It is famous because engineers reversed its direction of flow around 1900.
wichtigste: The Chicago River flows through the centre of Chicago.
It used to flow into Lake Michigan.
Around 1900 its direction of flow was reversed.
Since then it has flowed along a canal towards the Mississippi.
This was meant to keep the drinking water from the lake clean.

abschnitte.text: Chicago grew very quickly in the 19th century. The city’s **sewage** reached **Lake Michigan** by way of the river. But the city also drew its **drinking water** from this lake. This was dangerous for people’s health.

To solve this, the **Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal** was built and opened in 1900. Since then the river has flowed **away from the lake**. Its water reaches the **Mississippi** by way of other rivers. The structure is regarded as a great achievement of engineering.

Today the Chicago River is lined with skyscrapers, bridges and riverside paths. Pleasure boats carry visitors who marvel at the architecture. Every year on **St Patrick’s Day**, the Irish holiday in March, the river is dyed bright **green**.

gewusst: Only a few rivers in the world have been altered so that they flow in the opposite direction.

teile.einleitung: The Bering Strait is a strait between Asia and North America. It separates Russia from Alaska and connects the Pacific with the Arctic Ocean. At its narrowest point it is only about 82 kilometres wide.
wichtigste: The Bering Strait separates Asia from North America.
It lies between Russia and Alaska (USA).
At its narrowest point it is about 82 kilometres wide.
It is named after the navigator Vitus Bering.
During the Ice Age there was a land bridge here.

abschnitte.text: The **Bering Strait** lies at the far north of the Pacific. In the west lies the Russian peninsula of **Chukotka**, in the east **Alaska**, which belongs to the USA. The strait connects the **Bering Sea** in the south with the Arctic Ocean in the north. It is not very deep. In winter it is often covered with ice.

In the middle of the Bering Strait lie the two **Diomede Islands**. The larger one belongs to Russia, the smaller one to the USA. They are only about four kilometres apart. Between them runs the **International Date Line**. That is why it is already a day later on the Russian island than on the American one.

abschnitte.titel: The land bridge of the Ice Age
abschnitte.text: During the **Ice Age** a lot of water was bound up in huge glaciers. The sea level was therefore lower, and where the Bering Strait is now there was a **land bridge**. Over it animals and also people migrated from Asia to America. Researchers call this region **Beringia**. When the ice melted, the sea rose, and the land bridge disappeared.

gewusst: The strait is named after Vitus Bering, a navigator from Denmark who explored the region in the service of Russia.
In clear weather you can see the other Diomede Island from one of them, even though it is already a different day there.

teile.einleitung: The baobab is a mighty tree with a very thick trunk. In German it is also called the Affenbrotbaum, or monkey-bread tree. It grows mainly in the dry savannas of Africa and can live for over 1,000 years.
wichtigste: In German the baobab is also called the Affenbrotbaum, the monkey-bread tree.
It stores water in its thick trunk.
It can live for over 1,000 years.
In the dry season it loses its leaves.
Its large white flowers mostly open at night.
Elephants sometimes eat its bark, because it contains water.

abschnitte.text: The baobab has an enormously **thick trunk**, which in old trees reaches many metres in circumference. By comparison the crown looks small. The trees grow mainly in the dry **savannas of Africa**. There are several baobab species. Most of them grow in **Madagascar**, one in Africa and one in Australia.

In the soft wood of its trunk the baobab stores a lot of **water**. This lets it survive long **dry seasons**. During this time it drops its leaves and so loses less water. Without leaves its bare branches look like roots reaching into the sky. That is why it is sometimes called the “upside-down tree”. In dry seasons elephants tear bark and wood from the baobab, because it holds a lot of water.

Baobabs grow slowly and can live to a great age. Some trees reach **over 1,000 years**. The oldest known baobab was around 2,400 years old. Because the wood has no clear annual rings, researchers determine the age with special methods of measurement. Some old baobabs are hollow inside.

The baobab has large **white flowers**. They open in the late afternoon and bloom through the night. **Bats** such as fruit bats, which drink the nectar, help with pollination. After that elongated **fruits** with a hard shell grow, up to about 50 centimetres long. The pulp is edible and is eaten by people and by animals such as baboons.

For many people in Africa the baobab is very valuable. From the dry **pulp** of the fruit they make drinks and dishes. The young leaves are eaten as a vegetable. From the fibres of the bark ropes are made. Even in Switzerland you can buy baobab fruit powder today.

gewusst: In Madagascar there is a famous avenue where huge baobabs stand in a row.
In the book “The Little Prince” there are baobab trees that threaten to overgrow the tiny planet.

teile.einleitung: The carbon footprint shows how many greenhouse gases are produced by a person, a product or a company. It is usually measured in tonnes of CO2 equivalents. This makes it possible to compare what does more or less harm to the climate.
wichtigste: The carbon footprint measures the greenhouse gases produced by an activity or a product.
Different gases are converted into CO2 equivalents.
In 2023, the world average was about 4.7 tonnes of CO2 from fossil sources per person.
More than half of the footprint of Swiss consumption arises abroad.
Beef usually has an especially large footprint per kilogram.
The Swiss researcher Mathis Wackernagel helped to develop the ecological footprint.

abschnitte.text: Besides **CO2** there are other **greenhouse gases**, such as **methane** and **nitrous oxide**. They have effects of different strength. That is why each gas is converted into the amount of CO2 that has the same effect. The result is called **CO2 equivalents**. This makes it possible to add all the gases together. The carbon footprint is part of the **ecological footprint**, which the Swiss researcher **Mathis Wackernagel** developed with William Rees in the 1990s.

According to the **Global Carbon Project**, in 2023 each person worldwide caused on average about **4.7 tonnes of CO2** from fossil sources. There are very big differences between countries, however. In the case of **Switzerland** you have to look closely: according to the **Federal Statistical Office**, more than half of the emissions from Swiss consumption arise **abroad**, for example in making imported goods. The domestic inventory does not show these emissions.

A car, for example, emits **150 grams of CO2** per kilometre and drives **12,000 kilometres** a year. You then work out 150 g times 12,000. This gives 1,800,000 g, that is, 1,800 kg or **1.8 tonnes** of CO2. There are big differences in food too. **Beef** usually has the largest footprint per kilogram, because cattle give off a lot of methane when they digest and need a lot of feed.

Some emissions cannot be seen. **Embodied emissions** arise in the production, transport and disposal of a product or building. In new buildings they often make up a large share. Under the **Greenhouse Gas Protocol**, companies sort their emissions into three areas. **Scope 1** is direct emissions, and **Scope 2** is emissions from purchased energy. **Scope 3** covers the supply chain and the use of products sold, and is often the largest part.

The personal carbon footprint became well known in the mid-2000s through a campaign by the oil company **BP**. Around 2004 it launched an online calculator. **Critics** see this as an attempt to shift responsibility from companies to individuals. **Supporters** think that the footprint helps people understand their own choices better. Both views are still debated today.

gewusst: A return flight from Europe to somewhere overseas can cause several tonnes of CO2 per person.
Over a few decades, methane in the air has a much stronger effect than the same amount of CO2.

teile.einleitung: The Chicxulub crater is a huge impact crater beneath the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico. It formed about 66 million years ago when a large body from space crashed into the Earth.
wichtigste: The crater lies in the north-west of the Yucatán Peninsula, partly under the sea.
It has a diameter of about 180 kilometres.
It formed about 66 million years ago.
The impact is regarded as the main cause of the extinction of the dinosaurs.
On the surface, a ring of cenotes traces the edge of the crater.

abschnitte.text: About **66 million years ago**, an asteroid about **ten kilometres** across hit the Earth. It left a crater about **180 kilometres** across. Today the crater is **buried** under thick layers of rock. It cannot be seen directly, but is found by measuring gravity and the magnetic field.

The impact threw huge amounts of dust and gases into the air. Sunlight was weakened for a long time, and the climate changed greatly. Many animal and plant species died out, including the **dinosaurs**, with the exception of the birds. Experts see the impact as the **main cause** of this great mass extinction.

On the surface of Yucatán, many **cenotes**, or waterholes in the limestone, form a striking **semicircle**. It follows the edge of the buried crater. There the rock is more brittle, and water can dissolve it more easily. In this way the landscape reveals what lies hidden deep in the ground.

gewusst: The crater is named after the small village of Chicxulub on the coast of Yucatán.
Birds are the only descendants of the dinosaurs that survived.

teile.einleitung: Catatumbo lightning is a special weather phenomenon in Venezuela. Where the Río Catatumbo flows into Lake Maracaibo, there are thunderstorms lasting for hours on very many nights. The place is regarded as one of the most lightning-rich on Earth.
wichtigste: Catatumbo lightning occurs at Lake Maracaibo in Venezuela.
There are thunderstorms there on very many nights of the year.
The lightning often goes on for several hours.
The place is regarded as one of the most lightning-rich on Earth.
Sailors used the lightning for navigation in the past.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Maracaibo** lies in the north-west of **Venezuela**. Where the **Río Catatumbo** flows into the lake, there are thunderstorms on **many nights** of the year. Often lightning then flashes across the sky for hours. Measurements by satellite showed that the area is one of the **places with the most lightning on Earth**. The phenomenon is also called “Relámpago del Catatumbo”, meaning “Catatumbo lightning”.

The lake is warm, and a lot of water evaporates above it. Around the lake rise the high mountains of the **Andes**. At night, cooler winds from the mountains meet the **warm, moist air** over the lake. The moist air rises quickly, and **thunderclouds** form. Because the conditions are similar almost every night, the spectacle repeats itself again and again.

The lightning can be seen from far away. In the past it helped **sailors** in the Caribbean to find their way. That is why it is also called the “**Lighthouse of Maracaibo**”. The lightning is so important to the region that it appears on the **flag** of the Venezuelan state of **Zulia**.

gewusst: Sometimes you can see the lightning but hear no thunder, because it is so far away.
In dry periods the storms can stay away for a few weeks.

teile.einleitung: The Aswan Dam lies in the south of Egypt and dams the Nile into a huge lake, Lake Nasser. The High Dam was built in the 1960s. It brings electricity and water, but also has great consequences for people, cultural monuments and nature.
wichtigste: The Aswan Dam dams the Nile in the south of Egypt.
A smaller old dam was built in 1902, the High Dam from 1960 to 1970.
The reservoir is called Lake Nasser.
The dam prevents the yearly flooding of the Nile.
It produces electricity from hydropower.
The temples of Abu Simbel and Philae were moved.
The Nubians had to leave their villages.

abschnitte.text: Near the town of **Aswan** there are two dams. A smaller old dam was built as early as **1902**. The great **High Dam** was built from **1960 to 1970** with the help of the **Soviet Union**. It dams the Nile into **Lake Nasser**, one of the largest reservoirs in the world. The lake reaches into Sudan. It is named after the then Egyptian president Gamal Abdel Nasser.

In the past the Nile flooded the land every year in late summer. The dam holds back this **flood water** and releases the water evenly. In this way it protects against floods and droughts, and farmers can irrigate all year round. **Turbines** in the dam produce electricity from **hydropower**. As with the reservoirs in the Swiss Alps, the force of falling water is used.

With the Nile flood, fertile **mud** used to reach the fields and fertilise them. Today this mud settles in Lake Nasser. That is why farmers have to buy **artificial fertiliser**. On the coast of the Nile Delta, too, the mud is missing. There the sea is wearing away the land in some places.

The reservoir threatened ancient Egyptian **temples**. UNESCO called for a great rescue campaign, in which many countries took part. The rock temples of **Abu Simbel** were sawn into blocks between 1964 and 1968 and rebuilt in a higher place. The temple of Isis at **Philae** was often under water after the old dam was built. In the 1970s it was moved to the higher island of Agilkia.

South of Aswan lay the land of the **Nubians**, with villages along the Nile. The reservoir flooded this area. In Egypt and Sudan around **100,000 people** were resettled. Many Nubians had to move to new villages far from the river. For them this was a great loss of their homeland and way of life.

gewusst: To pay for the building of the High Dam, Egypt nationalised the Suez Canal in 1956.
During the move, the temple of Abu Simbel was cut into over a thousand blocks.

teile.einleitung: The Aral Sea in Central Asia was once one of the largest lakes in the world. Since the 1960s it has largely dried up, because a great deal of water was taken from its tributaries. It is regarded as one of the greatest man-made environmental disasters.
wichtigste: The Aral Sea lies between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
Until the early 1960s it was the fourth-largest inland lake on Earth.
It was fed by the rivers Amu Darya and Syr Darya.
Their water was diverted mainly for cotton fields.
On the old lake bed the desert Aralkum formed.
A dam built in 2005 partly saved the North Aral Sea.
