abschnitte.titel: A lake as big as Ireland
abschnitte.text: The Aral Sea lies between **Kazakhstan** in the north and **Uzbekistan** in the south. Until the early 1960s, at around 68,000 square kilometres, it was the **fourth-largest inland lake** on Earth, about as big as Ireland. It had no outflow. It was fed by the rivers **Amu Darya** and **Syr Darya**, which come from the mountains of Central Asia.

At the time of the **Soviet Union**, huge **cotton fields** were laid out in Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan. Cotton was called “white gold”. To irrigate the fields, a great deal of water was taken from the rivers. As a result hardly any water reached the lake. The water level fell, and the lake became smaller and saltier.

With the water the fish disappeared, and with them the work of many fishermen. The port town of **Moynaq** used to lie on the shore. Today the water is over 100 kilometres away. Old, rusty fishing boats lie there in the sand in a **ship graveyard**. On the former lake bed the **Aralkum** formed, the youngest desert on Earth. From there the wind carries salty dust far into the country.

In the lake lay **Vozrozhdeniya Island**. The Soviet Union ran a secret laboratory and test site for **biological weapons** there. As the water level fell, the island became a peninsula around 2001. This caused concern that animals or people might come into contact with buried disease-causing germs.

The lake broke up into several parts. In 2005 **Kazakhstan** had the **Kok-Aral Dam** built. It holds the water of the Syr Darya back in the northern part. Since then the water level there has risen again, the water is less salty, and there are **fish** again. The large southern part, by contrast, is still drying out.

gewusst: The name Aral Sea means roughly “sea of islands”, because there used to be over a thousand islands in it.
Since 1960 the Aral Sea has lost most of its area.

teile.einleitung: Buenos Aires is the capital of Argentina. The large port city lies on the Río de la Plata, a very wide river mouth. The city is famous for the tango, for colourful houses and for very wide streets.
wichtigste: Buenos Aires is the capital of Argentina and lies on the Río de la Plata.
The people of Buenos Aires are called Porteños, meaning “port dwellers”.
A landmark is the Obelisk, about 68 metres tall.
The Avenida 9 de Julio is regarded as one of the widest streets in the world.
In the La Boca district, many houses are painted in bright colours.
The president has his seat in the Casa Rosada.

abschnitte.titel: City on the Río de la Plata
abschnitte.text: Buenos Aires lies on the **Río de la Plata**, a very wide mouth of the rivers Paraná and Uruguay. On the other side lies the country of **Uruguay**. The city is an important **port**. That is why its inhabitants call themselves **Porteños**, which means “port dwellers”. The name Buenos Aires means “good airs” or “fair winds” in Spanish.

In the middle of the city stands the **Obelisk**, a white tower about **68 metres** tall. It is a landmark of Buenos Aires. It stands on the **Avenida 9 de Julio**, which is regarded as one of the **widest streets in the world**. It has many lanes in each direction. On foot, you need several sets of traffic lights to cross it. Its name recalls 9 July 1816, the day of Argentina’s independence.

In the **La Boca** district, many houses are painted in bright colours. In the past, people used **leftover paint from the port** for this. La Boca is also home to the stadium of the well-known football club Boca Juniors. The **tango** arose on the Río de la Plata in the 19th century, a dance and a kind of music that is now known all over the world. Many immigrants from Italy and Spain shaped the city.

The seat of the Argentine **president** is called the **Casa Rosada**, which means “pink house”. Because of its colour the building is easy to recognise. It stands on the **Plaza de Mayo**, the most important square in the city. Many large gatherings and demonstrations have taken place here in Argentina’s history.

**Pope Francis** came from Buenos Aires. His name at birth was **Jorge Mario Bergoglio**, and he was born in the city in **1936**. Before he became pope, he was Archbishop of Buenos Aires. He was the **first pope from the Americas** and the first from the Jesuit order.

gewusst: The Teatro Colón in Buenos Aires is regarded as one of the most important opera houses in the world.
The tango of the Río de la Plata is part of UNESCO’s intangible cultural heritage.

teile.einleitung: The Americas form a huge double continent that stretches from the icy north almost to Antarctica. They consist of North America and South America, which are joined by the narrow land bridge of Central America. From polar bears in Canada to parrots in the rainforest, there is almost everything here that the Earth has to offer.
wichtigste: The Americas consist of two parts: North America and South America.
Central America joins the two parts like a narrow bridge.
In 1492 Christopher Columbus came to the Americas with his ships.
The name America comes from the navigator Amerigo Vespucci.
Brazil is the largest country in South America by area, and Portuguese is spoken there.
The capital of Canada is called Ottawa.
The Panama Canal in Panama connects the Atlantic with the Pacific.

abschnitte.text: The Americas lie between the **Atlantic Ocean** in the east and the **Pacific Ocean** in the west. The double continent reaches from the Arctic in the north to Tierra del Fuego at the southern tip of South America. Together the Americas cover about 42 million square kilometres, so around a thousand times as big as Switzerland. After Asia, it is the second-largest landmass on Earth.

In the west, long mountain ranges run almost the whole length of the double continent: in North America the **Rocky Mountains**, in South America the **Andes**. The highest mountain in the Americas is Aconcagua in Argentina at almost 7,000 metres. In South America the Amazon flows through the largest rainforest on Earth. In North America there are huge prairies, the Great Lakes and the deserts in the south-west of the USA.

The first people came to the Americas from Asia across a land bridge in the Ice Age many thousands of years ago. From them arose many **indigenous peoples**, such as the Aztecs in Mexico, the Maya in Central America and the Incas in the Andes. Around the year 1000 the Vikings under Leif Erikson briefly reached the coast of North America. With **Christopher Columbus** the conquest by the Europeans began in 1492, which brought a great deal of suffering and disease to the native peoples.

In the Americas there are 35 independent states. The largest countries are Canada, the USA and Brazil. In North America people speak mainly English, and in Canada French as well. In most countries of Central and South America people speak **Spanish**, but in Brazil **Portuguese**. Alongside these, many indigenous languages live on, for example Quechua in the Andes.

The **Statue of Liberty** in New York was a gift from France and was unveiled in 1886. The Panama Canal is around 82 kilometres long and opened in 1914. Since then ships no longer have to sail all the way around South America. Other well-known places are the Grand Canyon in the USA, Niagara Falls on the border between Canada and the USA and the statue of Christ in Rio de Janeiro. Ottawa, the capital of Canada, is smaller than the better-known cities of Toronto and Montreal.

In the 19th century many Swiss people emigrated to the Americas because at home there was often too little work and food. That is why there are places in the USA with names such as New Glarus or Vevay, and in Brazil the town of **Nova Friburgo**, which was founded by people from Fribourg. Even today many Swiss people abroad live in North and South America. The USA is among Switzerland’s most important trading partners.

begriffe.erklaerung: A continent that consists of two large parts that are joined together.
The people who lived in an area before the Europeans arrived.
A waterway for ships built by people.
A narrow strip of land that joins two larger landmasses.
When people leave their home country to live in another country.

gewusst: Columbus believed until his death that he had found a sea route to India, which is why he called the native people “Indians”.
Potatoes, tomatoes, maize and chocolate originally come from the Americas.
The name America appeared for the first time in 1507 on a world map by the German cartographer Martin Waldseemüller.

teile.einleitung: The Central Business District, or CBD for short, is the central business area of a large city. Office towers, banks, shops and administration buildings stand close together here, and land is more expensive than anywhere else in the city.
wichtigste: CBD stands for Central Business District.
Offices, banks, shops and administration are concentrated in the CBD.
Land prices are highest there because the place is the easiest to reach.
Because land is expensive, buildings are especially tall.
In the daytime there are far more people in the CBD than at night.
The CBD is shaped by the tertiary sector, that is, by services.

abschnitte.text: In the **CBD**, many people work in offices, banks, insurance companies and government departments. There are large shops, hotels and restaurants. Almost all these businesses belong to the **tertiary sector**, that is, services. You hardly find factories or farms here. Swiss cities such as Zurich also have a business centre like this, only smaller than in the great world cities.

In the centre, roads, railways and bus routes come together. This makes the CBD the **easiest place to reach** for customers and workers. Many firms want to be there and bid high prices against each other. William Alonso’s **bid-rent model** explains that trade and services in the centre can pay the most, while housing and farming lie further out. The place with the highest land values is called the **peak land value intersection**, usually a busy crossroads.

When a square metre of land costs a great deal, it is worth building **many storeys** on the same area. That is why most of a city’s **skyscrapers** stand in the CBD. From above, you can often recognise the business district by its skyline. The further you move from the centre, the lower the buildings usually become.

Many people **commute** to the CBD every morning and go home again in the evening. As a result, the **daytime population** is much larger than the night-time population. In the process of **city formation**, offices and shops gradually push homes out of the city centre. Fewer and fewer people live in the centre, and in the evening it becomes quiet there.

In Chicago, the CBD is called **The Loop**. The name comes from the railways that circle the centre in a loop, first cable cars and later an elevated railway. In Paris, a new business district, **La Défense**, was built west of the city boundary. This kept the historic city centre free of skyscrapers.

gewusst: In English, “loop” means a circle or ring, hence the name of Chicago’s centre.
La Défense is one of the largest office centres in Europe.

teile.einleitung: Aridity means dryness. A climate is called arid if more water could evaporate than falls as precipitation. Experts measure aridity with various indices, and it shapes soils, rivers and landscapes.
wichtigste: A climate is arid if possible evaporation exceeds precipitation.
The word comes from the Latin “aridus” for dry, and “humidus” means moist.
Around 1910 Albrecht Penck distinguished humid, arid and nival climates.
The de Martonne aridity index is N / (T + 10).
According to UNEP an area below 0.05 counts as hyper-arid.
Typical of arid regions are wadis, exotic rivers and basins without outflow.
Irrigation without good drainage can make soils salty.

abschnitte.text: A climate is called **arid** if the **possible evaporation** is greater than the precipitation. Then the ground dries out, and rivers often carry water only at times. The opposite is **humid**: more precipitation falls than can evaporate, so there are permanently flowing rivers. “Aridus” means dry in Latin, “humidus” moist. The geographer **Albrecht Penck** distinguished humid, arid and **nival** climates around 1910. In the nival climate precipitation falls as snow and is carried off mainly by glaciers.

The Frenchman **Emmanuel de Martonne** developed an aridity index. You divide the annual precipitation N in millimetres by the mean annual temperature T in degrees plus ten: **N / (T + 10)**. An example: 600 mm of precipitation and 10 °C give 600 / 20 = **30**. The smaller the value, the drier the climate, and below 10 it counts as arid. **UNEP** divides precipitation by potential evaporation. Below **0.05** an area is hyper-arid, up to 0.2 arid and up to 0.5 semi-arid.

A **wadi** is a dry valley that carries water only after rare rainfall. Then dangerous **flash floods** can suddenly occur. An **exotic river** such as the **Nile** brings water from wet regions through a desert without receiving tributaries there. On the way it loses water through evaporation and seepage. In **endorheic regions** rivers never reach the sea. They end in inland lakes or salt pans, for example at the Caspian Sea or the Dead Sea.

In arid regions **irrigation** is often used. If there is no good drainage, **salinisation** threatens. The water rises up through the soil and evaporates at the surface. The dissolved salts are left behind and build up, because hardly any rain washes them out again. Salty soils become infertile.

Switzerland has a **humid** climate, and almost everywhere enough precipitation falls. Even the **Valais**, one of the driest parts of the country, is not arid. Even so, it was often too dry there for farming. That is why people built **suonen** centuries ago, long water channels that bring glacier water to meadows and fields.

gewusst: The Nile gets its water mainly from East Africa and the Ethiopian Highlands.
Antarctica too counts as a desert because of its very low precipitation.

teile.einleitung: The Coriolis force arises because the Earth rotates. It deflects winds and ocean currents. Without it, areas of high and low pressure would behave very differently.
wichtigste: The Coriolis force is named after the Frenchman Gaspard Gustave de Coriolis.
It is an apparent force that only appears in a rotating frame of reference.
In the northern hemisphere it deflects moving air to the right, and in the southern hemisphere to the left.
At the equator, the horizontal deflection is zero.
Its strength depends on speed and on latitude.
It is far too weak to affect the water in a washbasin.

abschnitte.text: The Earth turns once a day on its own axis. Anyone standing on the Earth turns with it but does not notice. When something moves over long distances, such as air, it seems to be deflected from its path. This deflection is described by the **Coriolis force**. It is called an **apparent force** because it only appears to someone who is rotating along with the Earth.

The force is named after the French physicist **Gaspard Gustave de Coriolis**, who described it mathematically in the 19th century. In 1851, **Léon Foucault** made the Earth’s rotation visible in Paris. He set a very long **pendulum** swinging. Over the course of hours, the plane of its swing slowly turned, although nobody touched the pendulum.

In the **northern hemisphere**, moving air is deflected to the **right**, and in the **southern hemisphere** to the **left**. That is why areas of low pressure here turn anticlockwise. The force is stronger the faster something moves and the closer it is to the poles. At the **equator**, the horizontal deflection is zero.

Tropical cyclones need the Coriolis force to make the air turn into a vortex. Closer than about 5 degrees to the equator, it is too weak for this. That is why such storms hardly ever form there. The **trade winds** are also deflected by the Coriolis force.

People often say that the water in a **washbasin** always drains in a particular direction in the northern hemisphere. This is not true. For such small amounts and short distances, the Coriolis force is far too weak. What matters is the shape of the basin and small movements in the water.

gewusst: A Foucault pendulum can be seen in many museums, and the turning of its plane of swing shows the Earth’s rotation.
Because the deflection is zero at the equator, cyclones practically never cross the equator.

teile.einleitung: Container ships carry a large share of the world’s goods across the seas. Clothes, toys, mobile phones or bananas travel in standardised steel boxes, the containers. This invention has greatly changed world trade.
wichtigste: The American haulier Malcolm McLean is regarded as the inventor of modern container transport.
In 1956 the converted tanker “Ideal X” sailed with containers for the first time.
The dimensions of containers were set by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO).
The world’s largest container shipping company, MSC, is based in Geneva.
In 2024, Rotterdam was the largest container port in Europe.
Through the Rhine ports in Basel, Switzerland is connected to the sea.

abschnitte.text: In the past, sacks, barrels and crates were loaded onto ships one by one by hand. This often took days and was expensive. The haulier **Malcolm McLean** had the idea of lifting whole containers straight from the lorry onto the ship. In 1956 the converted tanker **“Ideal X”** carried such containers for the first time. As a result, handling costs fell sharply.

For containers to fit every ship, train and lorry, uniform dimensions are needed. These were set by the **International Organization for Standardization (ISO)**. The measure often used is the **TEU**: one TEU equals a container 20 feet long, that is, about 6 metres. The largest ships today carry over 20,000 TEU. Huge cranes, the **container gantry cranes**, move the boxes in a short time.

The largest ships call at only a few big ports, the **hubs**. From there, smaller **feeder ships** carry the containers on to smaller ports, for example in the Baltic Sea. Since the expansion of the **Panama Canal** in 2016, ships of the **Neopanamax** size, with about 14,000 TEU, can pass through. Previously the limit, the Panamax size, was about 5,000 TEU.

A big ship uses a great deal of fuel, and consumption rises sharply with speed. For this reason shipping companies often deliberately sail more slowly. This is called **slow steaming**, and it saves costs and CO2. Many ships sail under a **flag of convenience**, for example from Panama or Liberia. There, fees and taxes are low and some rules are less strict.

Switzerland has no coast, but it plays a major part in container shipping. The **Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC)** was founded in 1970 and is based in **Geneva**. In 2022 it overtook the Danish company Maersk to become the largest container shipping company in the world. Through the **Swiss Rhine ports** in and around Basel, Rhine vessels sail to the sea ports of Rotterdam and Antwerp.

gewusst: The world’s largest container shipping company is based in a country with no sea: Switzerland.
In 2024, Rotterdam handled about 13.8 million TEU, just ahead of Antwerp-Bruges.
The world’s largest container ports are not in Europe but in Asia.

teile.einleitung: Blood diamonds, also called conflict diamonds, are diamonds whose sale pays for armed conflicts. Rebel groups used the money to buy weapons. The Kimberley Process was created to stop this trade.
wichtigste: The money from blood diamonds is used to pay for armed conflicts.
In Sierra Leone, the rebel group RUF paid for its civil war from 1991 to 2002 in this way.
In Angola, UNITA financed its fight with diamonds for decades.
The Kimberley Process certification system has applied since 2003.
It is named after the town of Kimberley in South Africa.
Critics point out that it does not cover violence committed by states.
Botswana is seen as an example of how diamonds can help development.

abschnitte.text: Diamonds form deep in the **Earth’s mantle** under great pressure and heat. They reach the surface in volcanic pipes made of **kimberlite**. This is where the **primary deposits** lie. Rivers can also wash diamonds out of the rock and leave them in **alluvial ground**. Such deposits are called **alluvial**. There, diamonds can be mined with just a shovel and a sieve, without expensive equipment.

Because alluvial diamonds are so easy to mine, rebels were able to raise money with them. In **Sierra Leone**, the **Revolutionary United Front** (RUF) controlled diamond fields in the east of the country during the civil war from 1991 to 2002. In **Angola**, the rebel movement **UNITA** sold raw diamonds worth billions of dollars during the civil war. The groups used the money to buy weapons, and the wars lasted longer. Ordinary people suffered greatly as a result.

In 2000, diamond-producing countries met in **Kimberley** in South Africa, a historic centre of diamond mining. This led to the **Kimberley Process**. Its certification system has applied since **2003**. Raw diamonds that are traded need a **certificate of origin** confirming that they do not come from conflict zones. Switzerland also takes part in the Kimberley Process.

A common criticism of the Kimberley Process is that it only covers **rebels**. Human rights abuses by **governments**, for example in the Marange diamond fields in Zimbabwe, do not fall under the rules. A positive example is **Botswana**. The country uses its diamond income, earned through the joint company **Debswana** with the firm De Beers, to pay for schools, health care and roads.

gewusst: Diamond is the hardest natural material and is made only of carbon.
A rough diamond often looks plain, like a cloudy pebble, and only cutting makes it sparkle.

teile.einleitung: Aquaculture is the farming of fish, shellfish, crustaceans and algae in water. Instead of catching them in the sea, the animals are raised in tanks, ponds or net pens. Today about half of the fish used for food come from aquaculture.
wichtigste: Aquaculture is the farming of fish and other water animals.
Farming takes place in ponds, tanks or net pens in the sea.
About half of the fish eaten come from aquaculture.
China is by far the largest producer.
In Switzerland mainly trout are farmed.
Aquaculture can take pressure off the seas, but also brings environmental problems.

abschnitte.text: In aquaculture **fish** such as carp, salmon, trout or tilapia are farmed. **Mussels**, oysters and **prawns** also often come from farms. Then there are algae, which are eaten mainly in Asia. Farming takes place in ponds, in tanks on land or in large **net pens** in the sea. Salmon, for example, is often farmed in net pens in Norway.

Aquaculture is not new. In **China** carp were kept in ponds a very long time ago. The Romans also farmed oysters. In Europe monasteries built fish ponds in the Middle Ages so that they could eat fish on fast days. Today China is by far the **largest producer** in the world.

Many fish stocks in the sea are **overfished**. At the same time more and more people want to eat fish. Aquaculture can help to take pressure off the seas. Today about **half** of the fish and seafood used for food come from farms. For many people in poor countries it is an important source of protein and income.

Aquaculture also has drawbacks. Some farmed fish get feed made from **wild fish**. Droppings and leftover feed can pollute the water. In crowded pens, diseases and parasites spread easily. For prawn farms, **mangrove forests** were cleared in some countries. Labels such as organic or ASC are meant to mark more environmentally friendly farming.

There are also fish farms in Switzerland. Most often **trout** are farmed, often in tanks with fresh stream water. There are also installations in which the water is cleaned and reused. Such **recirculating systems** need little water. Even so, most of the fish eaten in Switzerland comes from abroad.

gewusst: Mussels on farms need no feed, they filter their food out of the water themselves.
The word aquaculture comes from the Latin “aqua” for water.

teile.einleitung: An auto rickshaw is a small three-wheeled motor vehicle that serves as a taxi in many countries of Asia. In Thailand it is called a tuk-tuk, in India mostly an auto-rickshaw. It is small, nimble and usually open at the sides.
wichtigste: A tuk-tuk has three wheels: one at the front and two at the back.
The name comes from the putt-putting sound of the engine.
Tuk-tuks serve mainly as small taxis.
In Bangkok and in India they are especially common.
The first rickshaw was pulled by a person.
A rickshaw with pedals is called a cycle rickshaw.

abschnitte.text: An auto rickshaw has **one wheel** at the front and **two wheels** at the back. The driver sits at the front, and at the back there is usually room for two or three passengers. Most tuk-tuks have a roof but **no side doors**. That is why you feel the wind as you ride. Because they are narrow and short, they weave through dense city traffic between cars and buses.

The small engine makes a putt-putting sound that goes “tuk tuk”. That is how the **tuk-tuk** got its name. The word **rickshaw**, on the other hand, comes from Japanese. It means roughly “vehicle moved by human power”.

The first rickshaw appeared in the 19th century in Japan. It was a small cart that a person pulled on foot. Later the **cycle rickshaw** was invented, in which the driver pedals as on a bicycle. Only in the 20th century did rickshaws get an **engine**. Today in some cities there are also rickshaws that run on gas or an electric motor, because they give off fewer exhaust fumes.

In **Bangkok**, the capital of Thailand, tuk-tuks are well-known taxis, and many tourists ride in them too. In **India** millions of auto rickshaws run, many of them yellow and green or yellow and black. You wave to them at the roadside and are driven to your destination. The price is often agreed before the ride.

gewusst: Auto rickshaws also run in some countries in Africa and South America.
In some Swiss cities cycle rickshaws take tourists around in summer.

teile.einleitung: The Ethiopian Highlands are a huge area of mountains and plateaus in the east of Africa. Because they lie so high, they are called the “roof of Africa”. A large part of the Nile’s water comes from here.
wichtigste: The Ethiopian Highlands are called the “roof of Africa”.
The highest mountain in Ethiopia is Ras Dashen in the Simien Mountains.
Geladas and the Walia ibex live here, found nowhere else.
In the rainy season the Blue Nile brings most of the Nile’s water.
The capital Addis Ababa lies at around 2,400 metres.
Coffee originally comes from the Kaffa region.

abschnitte.text: The Ethiopian Highlands are the largest continuous area in Africa lying above **1,500 metres**. That is why they are called the **“roof of Africa”**. They consist of plateaus, deep gorges and mountains. In the north lie the **Simien Mountains** with **Ras Dashen**, the highest mountain in Ethiopia. It is a good 4,500 metres high, so about as high as the highest peaks of the Swiss Alps.

In the highlands live animals found only here. The **geladas** are monkeys with a red patch on the chest, which is why they are also called **bleeding-heart baboons**. They live in large groups on the high pastures and eat almost only grass. In the Simien Mountains lives the **Walia ibex**, a close relative of our **Alpine ibex**. It is severely endangered and is protected.

In the **rainy season** in summer a great deal of rain falls in the highlands. The **Blue Nile**, which flows out of Lake Tana, then swells greatly. It supplies most of the Nile’s water that arrives in Egypt. In the past this triggered the yearly **Nile flood**, which brought fertile mud to the fields. Today Ethiopia dams the Blue Nile with the **Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam**, which was inaugurated in September 2025 and is disputed between the Nile countries.

In the cooler highlands many people live, because there is enough rain here for **farming**. The capital **Addis Ababa** lies at around 2,400 metres and is among the highest capitals in the world. An important grain is **teff**, a very small grain from which the flatbread injera is baked. In the mountain forests of the **Kaffa** region in the south-west **Arabica coffee** grows wild. This region is regarded as the origin of the coffee plant.

gewusst: The name coffee is probably connected with the Kaffa region in Ethiopia.
Geladas are the only monkeys that live almost entirely on grass.

teile.einleitung: The Old Town of Bern lies on a peninsula in a loop of the River Aare. With its arcades, fountains and sandstone houses it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Here stand the Federal Palace, the Zytglogge and the Minster.
wichtigste: Bern was founded in 1191 by the Zähringen family.
The Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The arcades are together about 6 kilometres long.
The Zytglogge has an astronomical clock from 1530.
The tower of the Minster is the tallest church tower in Switzerland.
Albert Einstein lived at Kramgasse 49 from 1903 to 1905.

abschnitte.text: Duke **Berthold V of Zähringen** founded Bern in the year **1191**. The **Zähringen** family also founded other cities, for example **Fribourg**. The Old Town lies on a peninsula that is almost entirely surrounded by the **Aare**. After the great **city fire of 1405** the houses were built of **sandstone** instead of wood. The greenish-grey stone shapes the Old Town to this day.

The **Zytglogge** was once a city gate. Its **astronomical clock** with its figures dates from **1530**. Typical of Bern are the **arcades**: covered walkways beneath the houses. Together they are about **6 kilometres** long. This means that in Bern you can shop dry for a long time even in the rain.

The tower of the **Bern Minster** is a good **100 metres** high, more exactly about 100.6 metres. It is the **tallest church tower in Switzerland**. It was only finished in **1893**, over 450 years after building began. In the Old Town there are also many **figure fountains**. The strangest is the **Kindlifresserbrunnen**, the “child-eater fountain”, on Kornhausplatz, from the 16th century. What its figure means is still unclear.

At the edge of the Old Town stands the **Federal Palace**, high above the Aare. It was completed in **1902**. Here the **National Council** and the **Council of States** meet. At the other end of the Old Town, on the slope of the Aare, lies the **Bear Park**. Since **2009** the Bern bears have lived there, and the old **Bear Pit** next to it still belongs to it.

The famous physicist **Albert Einstein** lived at **Kramgasse 49** from **1903 to 1905**. He was working at the patent office in Bern at the time. During this period, in **1905**, his **special theory of relativity** came about. Today you can visit his former flat in the **Einstein House**.

gewusst: The bear is the heraldic animal of Bern, which is why bears have lived in the city for centuries.
The Old Town of Bern has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983.

teile.einleitung: India is the country with the most people in the world. According to the UN, around 1.46 billion people lived there in 2025. The population is young and still growing, but more slowly than before.
wichtigste: According to a UN estimate, India had around 1.46 billion inhabitants in 2025.
That is more than a sixth of the world’s population.
The last complete census took place in 2011 (as of 2025).
According to the 2019 to 2021 survey, the fertility rate was about 2.0 children per woman.
Bihar had the highest fertility rate, while Kerala is regarded as a model with a low rate.
Around 2023 about a third of the population lived in cities.
The Delhi urban area has over 30 million inhabitants.

abschnitte.text: According to an estimate by the **UN**, around **1.46 billion** people lived in India in 2025. That is more than a sixth of all people on Earth. Around 2023 India overtook China as the most populous country. The last complete **census** took place in 2011. The census planned for 2021 was postponed because of the **Covid-19 pandemic**, so current figures rely on estimates.

According to the national health survey of 2019 to 2021, the **fertility rate** was about **2.0 children per woman**. That is just below the **replacement level** of about 2.1, at which a population stays the same size in the long run. The differences are large: in the state of **Bihar** in the north it was around 3. The southern states are well below 2. **Kerala** in the south-west is regarded as a model with high literacy and low infant mortality.

abschnitte.titel: Why there are still more people
abschnitte.text: Even though the fertility rate has fallen, India’s population keeps growing. The reason is **population momentum**: very many young people are reaching the age for starting families. Even if each family has few children, there are many births overall. The high share of people of working age is an opportunity called the **demographic dividend**. The economy can then grow especially strongly if there are enough jobs and education.

According to the World Bank, around 2023 about **36 per cent** of people in India lived in cities, so roughly a third. The majority still live in **villages**. But **urbanisation** is advancing quickly. The **Delhi** urban area has over 30 million inhabitants and, with Tokyo and Shanghai, is among the largest urban regions on Earth. Mumbai and Kolkata are also huge cities.

gewusst: Very many languages are spoken in India, and the constitution lists 22 recognised languages.
In an Indian census, millions of enumerators go from house to house.

teile.einleitung: BRICS is a group of countries that want to work together more closely. The name comes from the first letters of the first members: Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. Other countries have joined since.
wichtigste: The economist Jim O’Neill coined the abbreviation BRIC in 2001.
South Africa joined later, and so it became BRICS.
In 2014 the countries founded the New Development Bank, based in Shanghai.
At the start of 2024, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates, among others, joined.
In January 2025, Indonesia became a full member.
The group wants to give the global South more weight in the world economy.

abschnitte.text: In 2001, the economist **Jim O’Neill** of the bank Goldman Sachs grouped **Brazil, Russia, India and China** together under the abbreviation **BRIC**. He meant countries whose economies might become especially important in future. The idea later grew into real cooperation between the governments. From 2009 the heads of state met at summits. **South Africa** joined as a further country, and the name became **BRICS**.

abschnitte.titel: Its own bank and reserve fund
abschnitte.text: At the summit in Fortaleza in Brazil in 2014, the countries decided to set up the **New Development Bank**. It is based in **Shanghai** and finances projects for infrastructure and sustainability. At the same time the **Contingent Reserve Arrangement** was created, a joint fund. It is meant to help members that are short of foreign currency for a short time.

At the start of 2024 the group grew: **Egypt**, **Ethiopia**, **Iran** and the **United Arab Emirates** joined. Argentina turned down an invitation. In January 2025, **Indonesia** joined as the first country in Southeast Asia. Other countries have shown interest in cooperating.

The BRICS countries want the countries of the **global South** to have more say in the world economy. They see themselves as a **counterweight** to groups such as the G7 and to organisations such as the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank. BRICS is not, however, a formal organisation with a fixed treaty. The members have very different political systems and sometimes pursue different interests. Observers therefore judge the importance of the group in different ways.

gewusst: A large part of the world’s population lives in the BRICS countries together.
The chairmanship of the group rotates every year between the members.

teile.einleitung: A bazaar is a large market with many stalls and small shops, found above all in the Orient. The word comes from Persian. Markets exist all over the world, though, including in Switzerland.
wichtigste: A bazaar is a market with many stalls in many alleys.
The Grand Bazaar in Istanbul is one of the largest covered markets in the world.
In Morocco and other Arab countries the market is called a souk.
In many bazaars people haggle over the price.
At the Zibelemärit in Bern, mainly onions are sold.
At a flea market you buy second-hand things.

abschnitte.text: A **bazaar** is a large market in the Orient. In many narrow alleys, stalls and small shops stand side by side. Often traders with the same goods are found in the same alley, for example all the spice sellers or all the goldsmiths. In the past the bazaar was the centre of a town. Traders, craftspeople and travellers met there.

abschnitte.titel: The Grand Bazaar and the souk
abschnitte.text: The **Grand Bazaar** in **Istanbul** is one of the largest covered markets in the world. It was built over 500 years ago and has thousands of shops. In **Morocco** and other Arab countries the market is called a **souk**. There you buy spices, carpets, lamps and leather goods. The souk of Marrakesh is especially well known.

In many bazaars no fixed price is shown on the goods. Buyer and seller **haggle**, which means they negotiate the price. The trader names a high price, and the buyer offers less. In the end both agree. Haggling is part of the tradition there and is often done in a friendly way and with humour.

Switzerland also has special markets. The **Zibelemärit** takes place every year in November in **Bern**. “Zibele” is Bernese German for **onions**, and they are sold there plaited into braids. In a **market hall** the stalls stand under one roof, so you can shop even when it rains. At a **flea market** people sell second-hand things such as toys, books and clothes.

In countries such as **Taiwan** or **Thailand**, **night markets** are very popular. They open when it gets dark and last until late at night. There are many stalls with hot food, drinks and all kinds of goods. Because it is hot during the day, many people prefer to go shopping in the cooler evening.

gewusst: The bazaar of Tabriz in Iran is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Many schools and parishes in Switzerland hold a bazaar with homemade things before Christmas.

teile.einleitung: Ciudad Bolívar is a city in the east of Venezuela on the great Orinoco river. It used to be called Angostura and played an important part in the struggle for the independence of South America.
wichtigste: Ciudad Bolívar lies in Venezuela on the bank of the Orinoco.
The city used to be called Angostura, which means “narrows”.
There the Orinoco is narrower than elsewhere.
In 1846 it was renamed in honour of Simón Bolívar.
It is also known for the herbal bitters Angostura.

abschnitte.text: The city lies on the **Orinoco**, one of the largest rivers in South America. At this point the river is **narrower** than elsewhere. That is why the city used to be called **Angostura**, the Spanish word for “narrows”. A large bridge crosses the Orinoco here.

At the time of the wars of independence against Spain, Angostura was an important place. **Simón Bolívar** gave a famous speech to a congress here in 1819. In several countries of South America, Bolívar is regarded as a **liberator**. In 1846 the city was renamed in his honour **Ciudad Bolívar**, “Bolívar’s city”.

In Angostura, a German doctor developed **herbal bitters** that were named after the city. **Angostura bitters** are known all over the world to this day. The company that makes them later moved to Trinidad. The old town of Ciudad Bolívar, with its colourful colonial houses, is an important part of Venezuela’s cultural heritage.

gewusst: The name Angostura lives on in a bitters that is known all over the world.

teile.einleitung: The cumulonimbus is the mightiest of all clouds. It brings thunderstorms with lightning, thunder, downpours and sometimes hail. At the top it often spreads out like an anvil.
wichtigste: The cumulonimbus is the typical thundercloud.
It can reach from the ground to a height of over 10 kilometres.
At the top it is often flat like an anvil.
It usually forms from a fast-growing cumulus cloud.
It brings lightning, thunder, heavy rain, gusts of wind and sometimes hail.
In Switzerland, such clouds form mainly on hot summer days.

abschnitte.text: The name comes from Latin: **cumulus** means heap, and **nimbus** means rain cloud. A cumulonimbus is a huge tower of cloud. It can reach from the ground to a height of over 10 kilometres. At the bottom it is dark, because hardly any sunlight gets through the thick cloud.

On hot days, warm, moist air rises. As it does so it cools, and water vapour turns into droplets: a **cumulus cloud** forms. If the air keeps rising, the cloud grows into a tower. Right at the top it is so cold that **ice crystals** form. There the cloud cannot rise any further and spreads out sideways, creating the **anvil**.

Inside the cloud, ice and water droplets collide. As they do, they become electrically charged until the voltage is released as **lightning**. **Thunder** is the bang of the suddenly heated air. Added to this are **downpours**, strong **gusts of wind** and sometimes **hail**. Aeroplanes fly around such clouds.

In Switzerland, cumulonimbus clouds form mainly in **summer** in the afternoon, often over the Alps and the Jura. Hail can then damage fields, cars and roofs. Anyone who sees a thunderstorm coming should look for shelter in a building or a car. On mountains, under lone trees and in water it is dangerous during lightning.

gewusst: In a cumulonimbus, hailstones can be blown up and down several times and grow bigger each time.
A large cumulonimbus can contain hundreds of thousands of tonnes of water.

teile.einleitung: The Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station is a research station almost exactly at the South Pole. It is run by the USA and has existed since the 1950s. It is named after the first two expeditions to reach the South Pole.
wichtigste: The station stands almost exactly at the geographic South Pole.
It is run by the USA.
The first station was built in the 1950s.
Roald Amundsen was the first to reach the South Pole, on 14 December 1911.
The station stands on thick ice, around 2,800 metres above sea level.
At the South Pole it is light for about half a year and dark for about half a year.
Most people reach the station by aircraft fitted with skis.

abschnitte.text: The Norwegian **Roald Amundsen** was the first person to reach the South Pole, on **14 December 1911**. He travelled with dog sleds. About a month later the Briton **Robert Falcon Scott** arrived with his party. Scott and his companions died on the way back in cold and storms. The station bears the names of both explorers.

The first station was built in the **1950s**, for a great international year of research. Since then it has been renewed several times. Today’s main building stands on **stilts** so that the snow can blow through underneath. The station lies on the ice of Antarctica, around **2,800 metres** above sea level. The ice beneath it is very thick and moves slowly.

In the station **researchers** live and work. They study the ice, the weather and the air. Because the air is very dry and clear, the place is well suited to observing the sky. With telescopes the universe is explored. Deep in the ice there are even instruments for tiny particles from space.

The way over the ice is very long and dangerous. That is why most people come by **aircraft** that have skis and land on the snow. In summer many more people live in the station than in winter. In winter it is so cold that aircraft usually cannot land. The people who stay then are cut off from the world for months.

At the South Pole the sun rises only **once a year** and sets once. For about half a year it shines without a break. After that it is dark for about half a year, which is called the **polar night**. In winter temperatures often fall below minus 60 degrees. Then you sometimes see the southern lights in the sky.

gewusst: At the South Pole every direction points north.
Because the ice moves, the marker of the South Pole has to be moved a few metres every year.

teile.einleitung: Cristo Redentor is the huge statue of Christ above Rio de Janeiro in Brazil. With its arms stretched wide, it looks out over the city. It is one of the best-known landmarks in the world.
wichtigste: “Cristo Redentor” means “Christ the Redeemer”.
The statue stands on Mount Corcovado in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
Without its base it is about 30 metres tall.
It was inaugurated in 1931.
On the outside it is clad in soapstone.
Since 2007 it has been one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

abschnitte.text: The statue stands on the summit of **Corcovado**, a mountain about 700 metres high in the middle of **Rio de Janeiro**. From there you can see the beaches, the bay and Sugarloaf Mountain. Many visitors travel up through the forest on a **rack railway**. A rack railway has a cogwheel that engages with a toothed rail, so it can climb steep slopes, in a similar way to mountain railways in Switzerland.

Without its base the statue is about **30 metres** tall, and a few metres more with the base. The **arms** are **stretched wide**, and the span is almost 30 metres. From a distance the figure therefore looks like a cross. The name **“Cristo Redentor”** is Portuguese and means “Christ the Redeemer”.

The statue was built of **reinforced concrete**, that is, concrete with iron bars inside it. On the outside it is clad in many small triangular tiles of **soapstone**. Soapstone is a soft stone that withstands the weather well. The figure was designed by the French sculptor Paul Landowski. It was inaugurated in **1931**.

Because the statue stands tall and exposed on the mountain, it is struck by **lightning** several times a year. For this reason it has lightning conductors, and damaged areas are repaired again and again. At night it is **lit up** and shines above the city. On special occasions it also appears in bright colours.

gewusst: In 2007, Christ the Redeemer was chosen in a worldwide vote as one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
The rack railway up Corcovado existed before the statue, and it even helped with the building.
The statue is one of the largest figures of Christ in the world.

teile.einleitung: Borneo is the third largest island in the world. It lies in Southeast Asia and is largely covered in rainforest. Three countries share the island: Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.
wichtigste: After Greenland and New Guinea, Borneo is the third largest island in the world.
The island is about 18 times as big as Switzerland.
Three countries share Borneo: Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.
The Indonesian part is called Kalimantan and covers about three quarters of the island.
Orangutans, proboscis monkeys and hornbills live on Borneo.
Brunei became rich through oil and natural gas.

abschnitte.text: Borneo lies in **Southeast Asia**, between Java, Sulawesi and the Philippines. About three quarters of the island belong to **Indonesia** and are called **Kalimantan**. In the north lie the Malaysian regions of **Sarawak** and **Sabah**. Between them lies the small **Sultanate of Brunei**. In Brunei a sultan rules, that is, a ruler with great power.

Large parts of Borneo are covered in **tropical rainforest**. It is one of the oldest rainforests on Earth and is home to a huge variety of species. Many areas have been cleared, however, mainly for **oil palm plantations**. In the north rises **Mount Kinabalu**, the highest mountain on the island at a good 4,000 metres. Its area is a national park and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

**Orangutans**, large apes with reddish fur, live on Borneo. The **proboscis monkey** is found only here. The males have a very large, hanging nose. In the sky fly **hornbills**, which have a growth on the beak like a horn. They also live in other parts of Asia and in Africa.

The **rafflesia** has one of the largest flowers in the world. It has no leaves and no stem and lives off another plant. Its flower smells of rotting meat and so attracts flies. **Pitcher plants** have cup-shaped traps filled with liquid. Insects slip inside and are digested. In this way the plants get nutrients that are missing from the soil.

Tiny **Brunei** produces a lot of **oil** and **natural gas**. As a result, people there have a high income and pay no **income tax**. In Switzerland, by contrast, people pay income tax to the municipality, the canton and the Confederation. In Kalimantan, Indonesia is also building a new capital called **Nusantara**.

gewusst: The equator runs right across Borneo.
The rafflesia grows not only on Borneo but also on other islands in Southeast Asia.
Borneo is one of the few places in the world where orangutans live in the wild.

teile.einleitung: Chuquicamata is a huge copper mine in the north of Chile, in the middle of the Atacama Desert. It is one of the largest open-pit copper mines in the world.
wichtigste: Chuquicamata lies in the Atacama Desert in the north of Chile.
Copper is mined here in an open pit, that is, an open excavation.
The pit is several kilometres long and about one kilometre deep.
The mine belongs to the Chilean state copper company Codelco.
Chile produces more copper than any other country.

abschnitte.titel: A huge hole in the desert
abschnitte.text: At Chuquicamata, **copper ore** is mined in an **open pit**. This means digging an open excavation instead of driving tunnels into the mountain. The pit is **several kilometres long** and about **one kilometre deep**. Huge lorries carry the rock upwards along spiral roads. Pure copper is then extracted from the ore.

The mine belongs to the state company **Codelco**. Copper is one of Chile’s most important exports. It is needed for **power cables**, electronics and engines. Because the pit keeps getting deeper, the ore is now also mined **underground**.

Next to the mine there used to be a settlement for the workers and their families. Because of dust and the growing pit, the residents moved to the nearby city of **Calama**. The old settlement has been almost empty ever since.

gewusst: Copper has been mined on a large scale at Chuquicamata for over a hundred years.

teile.einleitung: The Atlas is a large mountain range in the north-west of Africa. It runs for about 2,300 kilometres through Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia. The range shapes the climate of the whole region and separates the moister coast from the dry Sahara.
wichtigste: The Atlas Mountains reach from Morocco through Algeria to Tunisia.
They are about 2,300 kilometres long.
The High Atlas in Morocco is the highest part, with peaks over 4,000 metres.
The highest mountain is Toubkal at over 4,100 metres.
In the Middle Atlas large forests of Atlas cedars grow.
The range keeps moist sea air away from the Sahara.

abschnitte.text: The Atlas consists of several chains. In Morocco lie the **High Atlas**, the **Middle Atlas** and the **Anti-Atlas**. Further east, in Algeria and Tunisia, follow the **Tell Atlas** near the coast and the **Saharan Atlas** at the edge of the desert. The High Atlas is by far the highest, and the other parts are clearly lower.

The Atlas formed because the **African Plate** is slowly pressing against Europe. In the process, layers of rock were pushed together and raised. This mountain building is connected with the one that also folded up the Alps. That is why the Atlas and the Alps are in a way related.

Moist air from the Atlantic and the Mediterranean rises on the slopes of the Atlas. As it does so it cools and rains out. South of the range lies the **rain shadow**, an area that hardly any rain reaches. There the dry **Sahara** begins. So the Atlas is a natural climate border.

In the Middle Atlas, **Atlas cedars** form large forests at heights above 1,000 metres. These conifers are also planted as ornamental trees in Swiss parks. In the forests live the **Barbary macaques**, the only wild monkeys of North Africa. They have almost no tail.

gewusst: On the high peaks of the Atlas there is often snow in winter, even though the range lies in Africa.
In Morocco there is even a ski area in the High Atlas.

teile.einleitung: The Burj Khalifa is the tallest building in the world. It stands in Dubai in the United Arab Emirates and is 828 metres tall. The tower opened in 2010.
wichtigste: The Burj Khalifa stands in Dubai in the United Arab Emirates.
It is 828 metres tall and has over 160 floors.
The tower opened in 2010.
It is named after Khalifa bin Zayed, the president of the Emirates at the time.
Its shape recalls a desert flower.
At its foot lies a large fountain that dances to music in the evening.

abschnitte.titel: The tallest tower in the world
abschnitte.text: The Burj Khalifa is **828 metres** tall. This makes it much taller than any other building. It has **over 160 floors**. Inside there are flats, offices, a hotel and viewing platforms. For comparison, the tallest building in Switzerland, a tower belonging to the company **Roche** in Basel, is about 205 metres tall (as of 2025). The Burj Khalifa is therefore **about four times** as tall.

The tower stands in **Dubai**, the largest city in the **United Arab Emirates**. This country on the **Arabian Peninsula** is made up of seven emirates. Construction took about **six years**, and the tower opened in **2010**. It is named after **Khalifa bin Zayed**. He was the ruler of **Abu Dhabi** and president of the United Arab Emirates.

The architects were inspired by a **desert flower**. The floor plan has three wings that recall petals. The tower becomes narrower in steps towards the top. This shape also helps against the strong **wind** at great height. The outer wall is made of **thousands of glass panels** and **metal parts**. They reflect the sunlight and protect against the great **heat**.

Visitors travel in **very fast lifts** to the viewing platforms. In about **one minute** you are high up. From there you can see over the city, the sea and the desert. At the foot of the tower lies an artificial **lake** with a huge **fountain**. In the evening its jets shoot into the air in time with **music and light**.

gewusst: In clear weather the top of the Burj Khalifa can be seen from a very long way away.
The tower was first going to be called “Burj Dubai” but was renamed shortly before it opened.

teile.einleitung: Cumulus clouds are the white, fluffy clouds that drift across the sky on fine days. They look like cotton wool or cauliflower. They are also called heap clouds or fair-weather clouds.
wichtigste: Cumulus is Latin and means “heap”.
Cumulus clouds are white and cauliflower-like.
They usually have a flat base.
They form when warm air rises from the ground.
Small cumulus clouds are typical fair-weather clouds.
If they grow strongly, they can turn into thunderclouds.

abschnitte.text: The name **cumulus** comes from Latin and means **heap**. The clouds have sharp edges and a top that looks like a **cauliflower**. In the sun they shine bright white. Their underside is usually **flat** and a little greyer.

The sun warms the ground, and the ground warms the air above it. This warm air rises as a **thermal**. As it rises, it cools. At a certain height, the water vapour turns into tiny **droplets**, and a cloud becomes visible. Because this happens at roughly the same height everywhere, the underside is flat.

Small, flat cumulus clouds are called **fair-weather clouds**. They often form in the morning and disappear again in the evening when the ground cools. **Glider pilots** and birds such as buzzards use the rising air beneath the clouds to circle upwards without flapping their wings.

If the air is very warm and moist, cumulus clouds can grow higher and higher. They then become tall towers, the **cumulus congestus**. If they grow even further, a **cumulonimbus**, a thundercloud, forms. If tall clouds pile up quickly at midday, a thunderstorm may arrive in the afternoon.

gewusst: A medium-sized cumulus cloud can contain several hundred tonnes of water and still float, because the droplets are tiny.
Cumulus clouds often form over islands because the land warms up faster than the sea.

teile.einleitung: The Arabian Desert covers a large part of the Arabian Peninsula in Western Asia. It lies between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf. Here there are endless sand dunes, but also stone deserts, oases and plenty of oil.
wichtigste: The Arabian Desert lies on the Arabian Peninsula in Asia.
Saudi Arabia has the largest part of these deserts.
The Rub al-Khali is the largest continuous sand area on Earth.
Rub al-Khali means “Empty Quarter”.
Under the sand lie large amounts of oil.
The Arabian oryx and the dromedary are at home here.

abschnitte.text: The Arabian Desert lies on the **Arabian Peninsula** in Western Asia. Almost the whole peninsula is desert. In the west the **Red Sea** bounds the peninsula and separates it from Africa. In the east lies the **Persian Gulf**. **Saudi Arabia**, the largest country on the peninsula, has the largest part of the deserts. Parts also belong to Yemen, Oman, the United Arab Emirates and other countries.

In the south lies the **Rub al-Khali**. The name comes from Arabic and means **“Empty Quarter”**. Almost no people live in this area. The Rub al-Khali is regarded as the **largest continuous sand area** on Earth. There dune follows dune, and some are over 200 metres high. In summer it becomes extremely hot by day.

Under the desert sand lie huge amounts of **oil**. In Saudi Arabia it was discovered in the 1930s. By selling oil, countries such as Saudi Arabia, Kuwait or the Emirates have become rich. With the money, modern cities, roads and airports were built in the middle of the desert.

The **dromedary** has a single hump and comes from Arabia. People have kept it as a riding and pack animal for thousands of years. It can manage for a long time without water. The **Arabian oryx** is a white antelope with long, straight horns. It had disappeared from the wild entirely. Thanks to protection programmes it now lives free in the desert again.

For a long time **Bedouin** have moved through the desert with their herds. They traditionally live in tents and travel from pasture to pasture. Important are the **oases**, where water comes out of the ground and date palms grow. Today, though, most people in the region live in cities.

gewusst: The Arabian oryx was wiped out in the wild in 1972 and was later reintroduced in Oman and other countries.
A dromedary can drink over 100 litres of water at once.

teile.einleitung: In mountain valleys, in fine weather, a wind blows that changes direction every day. During the day the valley wind blows up the valley, and at night the mountain wind blows down the valley. The sun is the engine of this wind system.
wichtigste: Mountain and valley winds arise on sunny, calm days in mountain valleys.
During the day the slopes warm up, and the warm air rises.
That is why the valley wind blows up the valley in the daytime.
At night the slopes cool down, and cold air flows downhill.
The mountain wind therefore blows down the valley at night.

abschnitte.text: In the morning the sun shines on the **mountain slopes** and warms them strongly. The air above the slopes becomes warm and rises, because warm air is lighter than cold. Air flows in from the mouth of the valley. This creates the **valley wind**, which blows most strongly up the valley in the afternoon. Over the peaks, towering clouds often form as a result.

After sunset the slopes cool quickly. The air above them becomes cold and heavy. It flows like water down the slopes and then out through the valley. This is the **mountain wind**, and it blows **down the valley**. In the morning, cold air therefore often collects on the valley floor, sometimes with fog.

In many Alpine valleys in Switzerland you can watch this change well. **Paraglider and glider pilots** use the rising warm air to gain height. A well-known exception is the **Maloja wind** in the Upper Engadine: it blows down the valley in the daytime, because the air is drawn up from the lower-lying Val Bregaglia over the Maloja Pass. In foehn or bad weather the wind system is overlaid.

gewusst: A similar wind system exists at lakes and sea coasts: by day the wind blows from the water to the land, at night the other way round.

teile.einleitung: An atlas is a collection of maps, usually in a book, today also digital. With it you can find countries, cities, mountains and rivers all over the world. At school you learn how to use an atlas properly.
wichtigste: An atlas is a collection of many maps in book form or digital.
It contains physical, political and thematic maps.
The name comes from the Titan Atlas in Greek legend.
In the alphabetical index you can find any place quickly.
Grid squares made of a letter and a number show where a place lies on the map.
In many Swiss schools people work with the Swiss World Atlas.

abschnitte.text: An atlas brings together many maps in one place. **Physical maps** show mountains, valleys, rivers and seas, often with colours for height. **Political maps** show states, borders and capitals. **Thematic maps** deal with a particular topic, for example climate, population or the economy. Every map has a **scale** and a **key** that explains the symbols.

In Greek legend the **Titan Atlas** has to carry the vault of heaven on his shoulders. In the 16th century the cartographer **Gerhard Mercator** used the name Atlas for his collection of maps. Since then such collections have been called that. A few years earlier **Abraham Ortelius** had published a book of world maps, which counts as one of the first modern atlases.

At the back of the atlas is the **index**. There all the names are listed **alphabetically** from A to Z, as in a dictionary. Beside each name it says on which page and in which square the place can be found. The entry “p. 24, C3”, for example, means: page 24, column C and row 3.

The maps in the atlas are divided by lines into search squares, the **grid squares**. At the edge of the map there are letters for the columns and numbers for the rows. Where column and row cross lies the square you are looking for. This way you do not have to search the whole map, only a small square.

In many Swiss schools the **Swiss World Atlas** is used. It is published by the Swiss Conference of Cantonal Ministers of Education. It contains many maps of Switzerland and the whole world. It is available as a book and also in a digital form.

gewusst: An atlas never shows the Earth entirely without distortion, because a sphere cannot be shown flat without error.
There are also atlases for quite different things, for example for the stars in the sky or for the human body.

teile.einleitung: The Bonnet Carré Spillway is a large flood relief structure on the Mississippi in the USA. When the river is in flood, it diverts water above New Orleans into Lake Pontchartrain. In this way it protects the city from flooding.
wichtigste: The Bonnet Carré Spillway lies on the Mississippi in the state of Louisiana.
In a flood it diverts water into Lake Pontchartrain.
When it is opened, the water level of the Mississippi at New Orleans falls.
It was built after the great Mississippi flood of 1927.
It is operated by the US Army Corps of Engineers.

abschnitte.text: A **spillway** is a relief weir, in other words an overflow. If the **Mississippi** rises too high, the Bonnet Carré Spillway is opened. Part of the water then flows off sideways through a wide channel into **Lake Pontchartrain**. From there it continues into the Gulf of Mexico. This lowers the **water level** at **New Orleans** and takes pressure off the levees.

In **1927** there was a huge flood on the Mississippi. Large areas were under water, and very many people lost their homes. Afterwards it was decided to control the river better. The Bonnet Carré Spillway was built over the following years and finished in the early 1930s. The weir consists of many bays with **wooden beams**. To open it, they are lifted out with cranes.

Lake Pontchartrain normally contains **brackish water**, that is, slightly salty water. When the spillway is open, a lot of **fresh water** flows in from the river. This can harm animals that are used to salty water, for example **oysters**. For this reason the spillway is only opened when it is really necessary.

gewusst: In 2019 the spillway was opened twice in the same year for the first time.
Switzerland also has relief tunnels that carry floodwater past towns.

teile.einleitung: Angkor Wat is a gigantic temple complex in Cambodia. It was built in the 12th century under King Suryavarman II and is regarded as the largest religious building in the world. The temple is the landmark of Cambodia.
wichtigste: Angkor Wat was built in the first half of the 12th century.
The builder was King Suryavarman II.
Angkor Wat is regarded as the largest religious building in the world.
The central tower is around 65 metres high.
The temple is built mainly of sandstone.
Over 1,700 goddesses and dancers are carved on the walls.
The starting point for visits is the town of Siem Reap.

abschnitte.text: King **Suryavarman II** had Angkor Wat built in the first half of the **12th century**. Originally the temple was dedicated to the Hindu god **Vishnu**. Later it became a Buddhist shrine. The name means roughly **temple city**: “Angkor” comes from a word for city, “Wat” means temple.

Together with the broad **moat**, the complex measures around 1.5 by 1.3 kilometres. That is why it counts as the largest religious building in the world. In the middle stand five towers, and the **central tower** is around 65 metres high. The towers represent the sacred Mount Meru, the seat of the gods. A long causeway across the moat leads to the entrance.

The builders used large blocks of **sandstone**. Fine pictures could be carved into this stone. Long reliefs tell stories from legends and wars. Over 1,700 female figures decorate the walls, goddesses and heavenly dancers called **apsaras**. Along the paths, stone **nagas**, many-headed serpents, form the railings.

Near Angkor Wat lie many more temples. Particularly well known is **Ta Prohm**. There the jungle has been partly allowed to grow. Mighty **tree roots** clasp the old walls and gates. You can see how nature takes buildings back. The temple has also served as a setting for films.

Most visitors stay overnight in **Siem Reap**, only a few kilometres south of the temples. Especially popular is the **sunrise**: in the early morning the sun rises behind the towers, and the temple is reflected in the water in front of it. Angkor Wat is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Angkor.

gewusst: Unlike most Khmer temples, Angkor Wat faces west.
Angkor Wat appears on the flag of Cambodia.

teile.einleitung: Containerisation means that goods are transported in standardised containers. Since the 1950s it has greatly changed world trade and reshaped ports all over the world.
wichtigste: Modern container shipping began in April 1956 with the ship Ideal X.
One TEU equals one 20-foot container, and a 40-foot container counts as two TEU.
The largest container ships hold about 24,000 TEU (as of 2024).
Twistlocks join the containers at the corners.
In intermodal transport, the means of transport changes but the goods are not unloaded.
Refrigerated containers are called reefers.

abschnitte.text: In April **1956**, the **Ideal X** sailed from Newark to Houston in the USA. She was a converted tanker with **58 containers** on deck. This voyage is regarded as the start of modern **container shipping**. Soon shipping companies were building ships designed only for containers.

The unit **TEU** equals one **20-foot container**. A **40-foot container** is twice as long and therefore counts as **two TEU**. The ships of the shipping company MSC’s **Irina class** hold 24,346 TEU (as of 2024). They are about 400 metres long.

Every container has standardised **corner fittings**. The **twistlock** is pushed into them and turned, which joins containers to each other and to the ship. The **spreader**, on the other hand, is the lifting frame on the crane that picks the container up. For perishable goods such as bananas there are **reefers**, containers with built-in cooling that are supplied with electricity on board.

In **intermodal transport**, the container is lifted as a whole from the ship onto the **train** or the **lorry**. The goods themselves stay in the container and are not unloaded. This saves a lot of time and work and protects the goods. In Switzerland, containers arrive in the country by way of the Rhine ports near Basel, for example.

Container terminals need **deep water** and **a lot of space** for cranes and storage areas. Many old city ports lacked these. In England, the **London Docks** therefore fell into decline, while **Felixstowe** committed to containers early. Felixstowe became the largest container port in Britain.

gewusst: Many old port areas, such as London’s Docklands, were later converted into residential and office districts.
Containerisation meant that far fewer dockworkers were needed than before.

teile.einleitung: Copacabana is a small town in Bolivia on the shore of Lake Titicaca. It is a famous place of pilgrimage. Even the well-known beach in Rio de Janeiro is named after it.
wichtigste: Copacabana lies in Bolivia on Lake Titicaca, high in the Andes.
Lake Titicaca lies at about 3,800 metres above sea level.
The town is an important Catholic place of pilgrimage.
A figure of the Virgin Mary, the Virgen de Copacabana, is worshipped there.
The famous Copacabana beach in Rio de Janeiro bears the name of this place.

abschnitte.text: Copacabana lies on a peninsula on **Lake Titicaca**, close to the border with Peru. The lake lies at about 3,800 metres above sea level, higher than almost all the mountain peaks in Switzerland. The air there is thin and the sun is very strong. From Copacabana, boats sail to the **Isla del Sol**, the Island of the Sun, which was a sacred island for the Incas.

In the large white **basilica** of Copacabana stands a famous figure of the Virgin Mary, the **Virgen de Copacabana**. Many believers from Bolivia and Peru make a pilgrimage there. A **pilgrimage** is a journey to a holy place in order to pray. In front of the church, some people even have their cars blessed.

In Rio de Janeiro, a small chapel dedicated to the figure of Mary from Copacabana was built long ago. The beach got its name from this chapel. So one of the best-known beaches in the world is named after a place in the mountains, far from the sea.

gewusst: The famous beach in Rio is named after a place that lies over 3,800 metres up in the Andes.
Lake Titicaca is regarded as the highest navigable lake in the world.

teile.einleitung: In irrigation farming, fields receive extra water, not only from rain. This makes it possible to grow plants even in dry regions. Agriculture needs a great deal of fresh water for this.
wichtigste: Around 70 per cent of the world’s freshwater withdrawals go to agriculture.
Farming with rain alone is called rain-fed farming.
Drip irrigation brings water directly to the roots.
In the Valais, the suonen have carried glacier water to the meadows since the Middle Ages.
In Iran, underground qanats lead groundwater to the fields.
Fossil groundwater hardly forms anew under today’s climate.

abschnitte.text: If the harvest depends entirely on rain, this is called **rain-fed farming**. Worldwide, most of the farmland is worked this way. In dry regions, though, that is a great risk. In **irrigation farming**, people bring additional water from rivers, lakes or groundwater to the fields. According to the UN organisation **FAO**, around **70 per cent** of the freshwater withdrawn goes to agriculture, mainly to irrigation.

In the **Valais**, the **suonen**, called “bisses” in French, have carried glacier water over long distances to dry meadows and vineyards since the Middle Ages. Many are popular **hiking trails** today. In **Iran** there are **qanats**: these are underground tunnels that tap groundwater at the foot of a mountain range and lead it with a gentle slope, without a pump, to fields and villages. This technique is several thousand years old.

In **drip irrigation**, the water reaches the roots drop by drop through hoses. This way hardly anything evaporates, and a lot of water is saved. In **Israel** this technique was greatly developed and spread from the 1960s onwards. It is less economical to simply flood fields or to water them with large sprinklers.

The **Aswan High Dam** in Egypt, completed in 1970, stores the water of the Nile in **Lake Nasser**. This allows irrigation all year round and several harvests. But the fertile **Nile silt** stays behind in the reservoir, so farmers need more artificial fertiliser. In Libya the **Great Man-Made River** project has pumped **fossil groundwater** from the Sahara since the 1990s. This water formed thousands of years ago and is hardly replaced, so using it is regarded as **unsustainable**.

gewusst: If irrigation in hot regions is done wrongly, the soil can become salty, because salt is left behind when the water evaporates.
Even the early advanced civilisations in Mesopotamia and Egypt lived from irrigation farming.

teile.einleitung: The Andes are the longest mountain range in the world above sea level. They run like a gigantic backbone along the western edge of South America, from the Caribbean to Tierra del Fuego. Here lie icy volcanoes, old Inca cities and villages where people live at almost 4,000 metres.
wichtigste: The Andes stretch around 7,500 kilometres from north to south.
They lie on the western edge of South America along the Pacific.
The highest mountain in the Andes and in all of the Americas is Aconcagua.
The Andes reach through seven countries, from Venezuela to Argentina and Chile.
High in the Andes of Peru lies the Inca ruined city of Machu Picchu.
Lake Titicaca lies in the Andes on the border between Peru and Bolivia.
There are many volcanoes in the Andes because two tectonic plates collide here.

abschnitte.text: The Andes begin in the north in **Venezuela** and **Colombia** and end in the south in Tierra del Fuego. In between they cross Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina. At around 7,500 kilometres they are about seven times as long as the Alps. In some places they are up to 700 kilometres wide.

**Aconcagua** in Argentina, at almost 7,000 metres, is the highest mountain in the Americas and the highest mountain outside Asia. Many Andean peaks are volcanoes, for example Cotopaxi in Ecuador. The Andes are forming because the **Nazca Plate** is pushing under the South American Plate. That is why there are also repeated strong earthquakes here.

Between the mountain chains in Peru and Bolivia lies a huge high plain, the **Altiplano**, at almost 4,000 metres. Lake Titicaca is found there. In the west of the Andes lies the Atacama, one of the driest deserts in the world. In the south, in Patagonia, there are large glaciers and wild granite towers.

In the 15th century the **Incas** ruled a large empire in the Andes with the capital Cusco. They built terraced fields on steep slopes and a long network of mountain paths. The city of **Machu Picchu** lies on a mountain ridge in Peru and was built in the 15th century. In the 16th century the Spanish conquered the Inca Empire.

In the Andes live **llamas** and alpacas, which people keep as pack animals and for their wool. Their wild relatives are the vicuñas and guanacos. In the sky circles the Andean condor, one of the largest flying birds in the world. The **potato** also comes from the Andes, where it has been grown for thousands of years.

Many people in the Andes belong to indigenous peoples and speak languages such as **Quechua** or Aymara. The city of La Paz in Bolivia lies at over 3,500 metres and is one of the highest seats of government in the world. Because of the thin air, visitors there often get a headache, so-called altitude sickness. Swiss mountaineers also like to travel to the Andes to climb the high peaks.

begriffe.erklaerung: A very high, flat plain in the Andes of Peru and Bolivia.
A huge piece of the Earth’s crust that moves very slowly.
A people who ruled a large empire in the Andes around 500 years ago.
Feeling unwell with headache and shortness of breath because the air at great height has less oxygen.
A flat field built like a step into a steep slope.

gewusst: Because of the shape of the Earth, the summit of Chimborazo in Ecuador is the point furthest from the centre of the Earth.
In the Andes there are thousands of different kinds of potato in many colours.
Machu Picchu became world famous in 1911 through the American Hiram Bingham.

teile.einleitung: Bertrand Piccard is a Swiss adventurer, doctor and pioneer. He was the first to fly around the world non-stop in a balloon and later in a solar plane. His family is known for great discoveries.
wichtigste: Bertrand Piccard was born in Lausanne in 1958.
He studied medicine and became a psychiatrist.
In 1999 he and Brian Jones were the first to circle the Earth non-stop in the balloon Breitling Orbiter 3.
The balloon took off from Château-d’Oex and landed in Egypt.
In 2015 and 2016 the solar plane Solar Impulse 2 flew around the world using only solar energy.
His grandfather Auguste and his father Jacques Piccard were also famous researchers.

abschnitte.text: In March 1999 Bertrand Piccard took off with the Briton **Brian Jones** in the balloon **Breitling Orbiter 3**. They lifted off in **Château-d’Oex**, a well-known balloon location in the canton of Vaud. After almost 20 days they landed in **Egypt**. With that they were the first to make a **balloon flight around the world without a stopover**. Many other teams had failed before them.

After that Piccard wanted to show what is possible with **renewable energy**. The plane **Solar Impulse 2** flew using only solar energy. Around 17,000 solar cells on the wings supplied the electricity, and **batteries** stored energy for the night. The flight started in March 2015 in **Abu Dhabi** and ended there in July 2016 after several stages. Because the cockpit had only one seat, Piccard and the Swiss pilot **André Borschberg** flew in turns.

Bertrand Piccard studied **medicine** and became a **psychiatrist**, that is, a doctor who helps people with mental problems. He also took an interest in hypnosis. Today he works through a foundation for **clean technologies** that help the environment and are at the same time economical. He gives many talks all over the world.

His grandfather **Auguste Piccard** rose in 1931 in a balloon with a pressurised capsule as the first person into the **stratosphere**, to around 15,800 metres. His father **Jacques Piccard** dived in 1960 with Don Walsh in the submersible **Trieste** in the Mariana Trench to around 10,900 metres. That is the deepest point of the oceans. In this way the family explored the height of the air and the depth of the sea.

gewusst: Auguste Piccard was the model for Professor Calculus in the comics “The Adventures of Tintin”.
In Château-d’Oex a large international balloon festival takes place every year in winter.
