teile.einleitung: Bangladesh is a country in South Asia, almost entirely surrounded by India. It lies in the great delta of the rivers Ganges and Brahmaputra on the Bay of Bengal. Bangladesh is one of the most densely populated countries in the world and known for its clothing factories.
wichtigste: Until 1971 the area was called East Pakistan and belonged to Pakistan.
In 1971 Bangladesh became independent after a war.
The national language is Bengali, also called Bangla.
The currency is called the taka.
For a long time jute was the most important export product, today it is clothes and textiles.
At Cox’s Bazar lies a beach about 120 kilometres long.

abschnitte.text: When British India was divided in 1947, the area went to **Pakistan**, even though India lay in between. It was called **East Pakistan**. Many people there felt disadvantaged, for example because their language was not treated equally. After a war the country became independent in **1971** as **Bangladesh**. The capital is **Dhaka**.

The national language is **Bengali**, in Bengali **Bangla**. The name Bangladesh means “land of the Bengalis”. People pay with the **taka**. The neighbouring countries India and Pakistan, by contrast, have a rupee. Most people in Bangladesh are Muslims, and there is also a Hindu minority and other religions.

Bangladesh lies in the huge **delta** of the Ganges and Brahmaputra. The country is very flat and criss-crossed by many rivers. In the **monsoon season** it rains heavily, and there are often great floods. In the south lie the **Sundarbans**, one of the largest mangrove forests in the world. The Bengal tiger lives there.

For a long time **jute** was the most important export product. This plant fibre grows well in the damp delta and is made into sacks and ropes. It is also called the “golden fibre”. Today **clothes and textiles** make up the largest part of exports. Bangladesh is among the largest clothing exporters in the world. Millions of people work in the factories, often in difficult conditions.

In the south-east of the country lies the town of **Cox’s Bazar** on the Bay of Bengal. Its sandy beach is around **120 kilometres** long and is regarded as one of the longest natural beaches in the world. Many people from Bangladesh spend their holidays there.

gewusst: 21 February commemorates a language movement in what is now Bangladesh and is today International Mother Language Day.
In Bangladesh very many cycle rickshaws run, especially in the capital Dhaka.

teile.einleitung: The pineapple is a tropical fruit with a prickly skin and a green tuft of leaves. It comes from South America and today grows in many warm countries. When ripe it tastes sweet, juicy and a little sour.
wichtigste: The pineapple comes from South America.
It grows on a low plant with prickly leaves.
At the top the fruit carries a tuft of stiff leaves.
Costa Rica sells more fresh pineapples abroad than any other country.
You can grow a new plant from the tuft.
The skin is rough, hard and scaly.

abschnitte.text: The home of the pineapple lies in **South America**. People there grew it long before Europeans came to the Americas. Christopher Columbus got to know the fruit on his second voyage. **Seafarers** then brought it to many warm countries, for example to Africa and Asia. In Europe it was very expensive for a long time and was regarded as a special luxury.

The pineapple does not grow on a tree. It grows from the middle of a **low plant** that reaches about a metre high and has long, prickly leaves. Each plant usually forms only one fruit. It often takes more than a year until it is ripe. The fruit is made up of many small berries that have grown together. That is why the skin looks like many **scales**.

At the top the pineapple carries a **tuft of leaves**. If you cut it off and put it in soil, it forms **roots**. From this a new pineapple plant grows. This way you can also grow a pineapple as a houseplant in Switzerland. It rarely bears fruit there, though, because that takes a lot of warmth and light.

In Switzerland no pineapples grow outdoors, it is too cold. Many pineapples in our shops come from **Costa Rica** in Central America. There it is warm all year round. The fruits are harvested ripe and brought to Europe by ship. After harvesting, a pineapple hardly gets any sweeter.

Ripe pineapple tastes **sweet and juicy** with a little acidity. You eat it fresh, as juice or from a tin. Well known is **Hawaiian pizza** with ham and pineapple. Hawaii used to be famous for its large pineapple fields. Fresh pineapple contains a substance that breaks down protein. That is why gelatine does not set with fresh pineapple.

gewusst: Hawaiian pizza was not invented in Hawaii but in Canada.
The pineapple belongs to the bromeliad family, which also includes many popular houseplants.

teile.einleitung: Cotton is a soft, white fibre that grows on a plant. It is made into yarns and fabrics for many clothes, for example T-shirts and jeans. Cotton needs a lot of sun, warmth and water.
wichtigste: Cotton grows on a plant, the cotton shrub.
The white, fluffy fibres surround the seeds in a capsule.
Cotton is used to make T-shirts, jeans and many other fabrics.
The plant needs a lot of sun, warmth and water.
India is one of the largest cotton countries in the world.
Egypt is known for especially fine, long cotton fibres.

abschnitte.text: Cotton grows on a plant, the **cotton shrub**. It has nothing to do with the wool of sheep. After flowering, the plant forms a **capsule**. Inside lie the seeds, wrapped in white, soft **fibres**. When the capsule is ripe, it bursts open, and the fibres burst out like cotton wool.

Cotton grows only in **warm regions**. It needs a lot of sun and cannot stand frost. It also needs a great deal of **water**. For a single T-shirt, many litres of water are used in growing the cotton. In dry regions the fields are therefore watered artificially. This can put a heavy strain on rivers and lakes.

**India** is one of the largest cotton countries in the world. Cotton has been grown and processed there for thousands of years. China, the USA and Brazil also grow a lot of cotton. On the Nile in **Egypt**, cotton with especially long, fine fibres grows. It is used to make very soft fabrics.

The fibres are cleaned and spun into **yarn**. From the yarn, fabrics for clothes, bedding and towels are woven or knitted. The fabric for **jeans** is called **denim**. It is firmly woven cotton and very hard-wearing. Cotton is popular because it is soft, absorbs sweat well and is easy to wash.

Cotton has played a big part in history. In the southern states of the USA, enslaved people were once forced to work in the cotton fields. With **industrialisation**, machines for spinning and weaving appeared. In **Switzerland**, too, there were many **cotton mills** in the 19th century, for example in the Zurich Oberland and in eastern Switzerland. They were among the first factories in the country.

gewusst: The Aral Sea in Central Asia has shrunk greatly, partly because a lot of water was taken from its feeder rivers for cotton fields.
The banknotes of some countries are also made largely of cotton.

teile.einleitung: Ethiopia lies in the east of Africa, on the so-called Horn of Africa. The country has a very old history, a calendar of its own and is regarded as the home of coffee. Like Switzerland, it has no access to the sea.
wichtigste: The capital of Ethiopia is Addis Ababa, which means “new flower”.
Ethiopia is a landlocked country with no sea coast.
The coffee plant comes from the highlands of Ethiopia.
The famous skeleton “Lucy” was found in Ethiopia in 1974.
The Ethiopian calendar has 13 months.
In Lalibela there are churches that were carved out of the rock.

abschnitte.text: Ethiopia lies on the **Horn of Africa**. The country is **landlocked**, so like Switzerland it has no sea coast. A large part lies in the high **Ethiopian Highlands**. The capital **Addis Ababa** lies high in the mountains, and its name means “new flower”. Addis Ababa is also the seat of the **African Union**, an association of almost all the states of Africa.

In 1974 researchers in Ethiopia found a particularly well-known skeleton. They called it **Lucy**. Lucy lived about 3.2 million years ago and is one of the **ancestors of humans**. Ethiopia also has a very old history as a kingdom. Christianity has been widespread here for many centuries, and many Muslims also live in the country.

In **Lalibela**, around 800 years ago, eleven churches were **carved** entirely **out of the rock**. The workers chiselled them into the stone from above. The churches are part of the **UNESCO World Heritage**. In the highlands also lies **Lake Tana**, the largest lake in the country. From it flows the **Blue Nile**, which meets the White Nile in Sudan.

The **coffee plant** originally comes from the highlands of Ethiopia. Coffee is still very important there today, and it is often prepared in a festive **coffee ceremony**. A typical food is **injera**, a thin, slightly sour flatbread. You put the food on it and eat with your fingers, with no cutlery at all. Injera is usually baked from the grain **teff**.

Ethiopia has its **own calendar** with **13 months**. Twelve months have 30 days each. Added to that is a short thirteenth month with 5 or 6 days. The year begins in September. The Ethiopian calendar also counts the years differently, which is why it is some years behind our calendar.

gewusst: Because the Ethiopian calendar counts differently, Ethiopia celebrated the beginning of the year 2000 only in September 2007 by our calendar.
Ethiopia is sometimes called the “land of 13 months of sunshine”.
Ethiopia was never a colony for long, only from 1936 to 1941 was it occupied by Italy.

teile.einleitung: Slash-and-burn means that forest is burned down to make room for fields or pasture. The ash fertilises the soil for a short time. It is a very old method, but today it often has serious consequences for nature and the climate.
wichtigste: In slash-and-burn farming, forest is burned to gain farmland or pasture.
The ash fertilises the soil, but rain quickly washes the nutrients away.
In shifting cultivation the whole settlement moves on, in rotational farming only the fields move.
In English this way of using land is called shifting cultivation.
In the Amazon region, cleared land mostly becomes cattle pasture.
Burning releases CO2 that was stored in the forest.

abschnitte.text: First trees and bushes are felled or cut into, then everything is **burned**. The **ash** contains nutrients and fertilises the soil. In the first few years, harvests are therefore good. In the tropics, however, it often rains heavily. The rain **washes the nutrients** away quickly, and after a few years the yields drop sharply.

Many peoples in the tropics have lived from this method for centuries. In **shifting cultivation**, people move their fields and also their **settlement**. In **rotational farming**, the village stays in the same place and only the fields change. The old plots are abandoned and grow over again. In English this way of using land is called **shifting cultivation**. Millions of people around the world live from it.

abschnitte.titel: When the rest period gets too short
abschnitte.text: For soil and forest to recover, many years of **fallow** are needed, that is, a time without farming. If the population grows, more land is needed. Plots are then used again too soon. The fallow periods become too short, and the soils are **permanently impoverished**. In this way a sustainable method becomes a problem.

Today forest is often cleared on a very large scale. In the Brazilian **Amazon region**, cleared land mostly becomes **pasture for cattle**. Growing **soya** also plays an important part. In **Indonesia** and **Malaysia**, huge **oil palm plantations** are created on cleared rainforest. Palm oil is found in many foods and cosmetics. The fires there sometimes cause heavy smoke over whole regions.

Trees store **carbon**. When they burn, it enters the air as **CO2** and worsens climate change. In addition, the forest is no longer there afterwards as a **carbon store**. With the forest, the habitats of many animals and plants disappear too. In Europe, too, forest was once turned into farmland by burning, for example in the Middle Ages.

gewusst: The soils of many rainforests are rather poor in nutrients, despite the lush plants.
Smoke from forest fires in Southeast Asia can drift into neighbouring countries and force schools to close there.

teile.einleitung: The Atacama Desert lies in the north of Chile between the Pacific and the Andes. It is regarded as the driest desert outside the polar regions. Because of its clear sky, some of the largest observatories in the world stand here.
wichtigste: The Atacama lies mainly in the north of Chile, and a small part reaches into Peru.
It is the driest desert outside the polar regions.
In the west lies the Pacific, in the east the Andes.
Because of the clear, dry air there are many large telescopes here.
After rare rain many flowers bloom, the “flowering desert”.
There are large white salt flats.
In the 19th century saltpetre was exported all over the world as fertiliser.

abschnitte.text: The **Atacama** lies in the north of **Chile** in South America, and a small part reaches into Peru. It is regarded as the **driest desert** outside the polar regions. In some places no rain falls for years. In the west lies the **Pacific**, in the east the high **Andes**. The Andes keep out moist air from the east. Off the coast flows a cold ocean current, which likewise allows hardly any rain to form.

Because of the dry air there are hardly any **clouds**. Far from cities there is also hardly any artificial light. So you can see the stars especially clearly. That is why the European Southern Observatory **ESO**, to which Switzerland also belongs, runs large telescopes in the Atacama. On the plateau of Chajnantor stands the **ALMA** array with dozens of antennas as well.

In some places the ground is red, stony and completely dry. It is reminiscent of **Mars**. That is why researchers test vehicles and instruments in the Atacama that will later be used on Mars. In large parts there are almost no plants, and even tiny living things are rare.

Sometimes it does rain, for example in some years with the weather phenomenon El Niño. Then **seeds** that have waited a long time in the ground germinate. In a short time the desert is full of colourful flowers. This is called the **“flowering desert”**. After a few weeks everything has dried up again, but new seeds lie ready.

In the Atacama there are large **salt lakes** and white salt flats. There water has evaporated, and the salt has stayed behind. In the 19th century the desert was famous for **saltpetre**. It contains nitrogen and was sold all over the world as **fertiliser** and for explosives. Since artificial fertiliser has existed, mining has fallen sharply. Today mainly copper and lithium are extracted here.

gewusst: Chile, Peru and Bolivia fought a war over the saltpetre fields in the 19th century, after which Bolivia lost its access to the sea.
In some places in the Atacama no measurable rain falls over many years.

teile.einleitung: The Carretera Austral is a long trunk road in the south of Chile. It has been built since 1976 and opens up the remote Chilean part of Patagonia. It leads through fjords, rainforest and glacier valleys.
wichtigste: The Carretera Austral has been built since 1976.
It opens up remote Patagonia in the south of Chile.
Before it, many places could only be reached by boat.
The road begins at Puerto Montt and leads a long way south.
Some sections are still not paved today, and ferries are needed.

abschnitte.text: The south of Chile is deeply rugged. There are many **fjords**, islands, glaciers and steep mountains. For a long time there was no road there that linked the places with the rest of the country. Many villages could only be reached by **boat**. From **1976** the **Carretera Austral** was built, which means “southern road”. It begins at **Puerto Montt** and leads south for many hundreds of kilometres.

The road is not a motorway. Large parts were for a long time **gravel tracks**, and some sections still are. In some places the road ends at the water, and you have to continue by **ferry**. Weather, landslides and volcanoes can close the road for a time. Building it was very difficult because it had to go through rock and dense forest.

Along the road lie **rainforests**, lakes, glaciers and national parks. One well-known destination is the **marble caves** on the great lake General Carrera, which Chile shares with Argentina. Today the Carretera Austral is popular with **cyclists**, hikers and travellers from all over the world, including from Switzerland.

gewusst: In the region around the road, very few people live over a large area.
The road was begun during the military government under Augusto Pinochet.

teile.einleitung: Brain drain means that well-educated people leave their country and work abroad. For the country they come from this can be a loss, and for the country they move to it can be a gain.
wichtigste: Brain drain is the emigration of highly qualified people abroad.
The term arose in the 1960s for British researchers who moved to the USA.
The opposite is called brain gain, the gain for the destination country.
With brain circulation, knowledge also flows back to the country of origin.
Brain waste means that qualified people work below their level of training.
In 2024, around 40 per cent of doctors in Switzerland had a foreign diploma.

abschnitte.text: The British **Royal Society** used the expression **brain drain** in the 1960s. At that time, many British scientists moved to North America because they found better conditions there. Later the term was applied mainly to **poorer countries**, from which doctors, engineers or researchers emigrate to richer countries. The reasons are often higher wages, better jobs or more security.

The destination country experiences a **brain gain**: it gains skilled workers whose training it did not pay for. With **brain circulation**, skilled workers return or keep close contact with their homeland, so both countries benefit. People speak of **brain waste** when, for example, a trained doctor works as a cleaner. The cause is often that her foreign **diploma** is not recognised.

Some experts, including **Oded Stark**, put forward the idea of the **beneficial brain drain**. It says that the prospect of work abroad motivates more people to get a higher **education**. Because not everyone actually emigrates, the number of qualified people in the country of origin can rise overall. Other experts are more critical. The question is still debated today.

Brain drain is especially noticeable among **doctors and nurses**. When they go abroad, hospitals are short of staff, particularly in rural areas of poor countries. In 2010 the **World Health Organization** (WHO) therefore adopted a voluntary **code of practice**. It is meant to prevent rich countries from deliberately recruiting staff from countries that have a shortage.

**Switzerland** benefits greatly from skilled workers from abroad. According to the doctors’ statistics of the FMH, in 2024 around **40 per cent** of practising doctors had a foreign diploma, most of them from Germany. In 2009 the European Union introduced the **EU Blue Card**. With it, highly qualified people from non-EU countries can work in the EU more easily.

gewusst: Money that emigrants send to their families back home is an important source of income for some countries.
Brain drain also happens within a country, for example when young people move from mountain valleys to the cities.

teile.einleitung: The Columbia Icefield is a large expanse of ice in the Canadian Rocky Mountains. Its meltwater flows into three different oceans, which is very rare in the world.
wichtigste: The Columbia Icefield lies in the Rocky Mountains in Canada.
It is the largest icefield in the Rocky Mountains.
Several glaciers flow from it, such as the Athabasca Glacier.
Its meltwater reaches the Pacific, the Atlantic and the Arctic Ocean.
The glaciers are getting smaller because of climate warming.

abschnitte.text: The **Columbia Icefield** lies high up in the **Rocky Mountains**, on the border between Banff and Jasper national parks. It is a large, continuous expanse of ice. Several **glaciers** flow down from it into the valleys. The best known is the **Athabasca Glacier**, which can be seen well from a road.

At the Columbia Icefield, three large **drainage basins** meet. Part of the meltwater flows into the **Pacific** by way of the Columbia River. Another part reaches the **Atlantic** by way of Hudson Bay. The third part flows into the **Arctic Ocean** by way of the Mackenzie. Such places are called a triple divide.

The glaciers of the icefield have been getting **smaller** for decades. At the Athabasca Glacier, signs show where the ice used to end. This is a result of **climate warming**. The glaciers in the Swiss Alps are melting for the same reason.

gewusst: A raindrop on the Columbia Icefield can end up in one of three oceans, depending on which side it falls.

teile.einleitung: The Charles Darwin Research Station is on the Galápagos Islands, which belong to Ecuador. There, experts study the special animal and plant life of the islands and help to protect it.
wichtigste: The station stands near Puerto Ayora on the island of Santa Cruz.
It is named after the naturalist Charles Darwin.
It is run by the Charles Darwin Foundation.
Among other things, young giant tortoises are raised there.
The Galápagos Islands belong to Ecuador.

abschnitte.text: Many animals and plants that exist nowhere else live on the **Galápagos Islands**. The research station studies these species and looks for ways to preserve them. It works closely with **Galápagos National Park**. One big problem is introduced animals and plants that crowd out native species.

The station is especially well known for the **rearing of giant tortoises**. The young animals grow up protected until they are big enough. Afterwards they are released on their home island. The tortoise **Lonesome George** became famous: the last known animal of his subspecies, he lived here until his death in 2012.

**Charles Darwin** visited the Galápagos Islands in 1835 on his voyage on the ship Beagle. His observations later helped him to develop his **theory of evolution**. That is why the station bears his name. Today many visitors come to the station in Puerto Ayora.

gewusst: Lonesome George became a worldwide symbol of endangered animal species.

teile.einleitung: The Dardanelles are a narrow strait in Turkey. They link the Sea of Marmara with the Aegean Sea and so, indirectly, the Black Sea with the Mediterranean. This sea route has been very important since ancient times.
wichtigste: The Dardanelles link the Sea of Marmara with the Aegean Sea.
They lie in Turkey and separate Europe from Asia.
In ancient times they were called the Hellespont.
Together with the Bosphorus they form the Turkish Straits.
Passage is regulated by the Montreux Convention of 1936.
Since 2022, a huge suspension bridge has crossed them.

abschnitte.text: The Dardanelles are about 60 kilometres long and, at the narrowest point, only a little over a kilometre wide. To the north lies the **Gallipoli** peninsula, which belongs to Europe, and to the south lies Asia. The strait links the **Sea of Marmara** with the **Aegean Sea**. At the other end of the Sea of Marmara lies the **Bosphorus**, which leads to the Black Sea.

The ancient Greeks called the strait the **Hellespont**. Near its entrance lay the famous city of **Troy**. A legend tells of Leander, who swam across the Hellespont every night to visit his beloved Hero. The Persian king Xerxes had a bridge of ships built here to bring his army across.

abschnitte.titel: The fight for the sea route
abschnitte.text: Whoever controls the Dardanelles controls the sea route from the **Black Sea** to the Mediterranean. In the **First World War**, Britain and France tried in 1915 to seize the strait. The Battle of Gallipoli lasted for months and cost very many lives on both sides. The Ottoman troops held the strait.

Passage through the straits is regulated by the **Montreux Convention**, signed in 1936 in the city on Lake Geneva in the canton of Vaud. Merchant ships may pass freely in peacetime. Strict rules apply to warships. The convention is still in force today.

In 2022 the **Çanakkale Bridge** across the Dardanelles opened. It is a **suspension bridge** with a span of over 2,000 metres between the towers. When it opened, this gave it the longest span of any suspension bridge in the world. Before that, the strait could only be crossed by ferry.

gewusst: The agreement that regulates passage through the Dardanelles bears the name of a Swiss town: Montreux.
In the Dardanelles, the water at the surface flows from the Black Sea towards the Mediterranean, but in the depths it partly flows in the opposite direction.

teile.einleitung: The Burgess Shale is a famous fossil site in the Rocky Mountains in Canada. It lies in Yoho National Park and is a good 500 million years old. Even soft-bodied animals from the Cambrian have been preserved here.
wichtigste: The Burgess Shale lies in Yoho National Park in British Columbia, Canada.
The rocks date from the Cambrian and are a good 500 million years old.
Soft parts are preserved too, which is very rare among fossils.
The site was discovered in 1909 by Charles Walcott.
The animals date from the time of the Cambrian explosion.

abschnitte.titel: A window into the distant past
abschnitte.text: Usually only the **hard parts** of animals, such as bones, teeth or shells, are left as fossils. In the Burgess Shale it is different. Here **soft parts** are preserved too, such as legs, gills or even the gut. The animals were probably buried quickly by fine mud that contained hardly any oxygen. This meant they did not rot completely. The rock is called **shale** because it can be split into thin plates.

The animals lived in the sea in the **Cambrian**. During this time, many new animal forms appeared in a short time. This is called the **Cambrian explosion**. In the Burgess Shale you find peculiar creatures. **Opabinia** had five eyes and a long trunk with a grasping claw. **Anomalocaris** was a large predator with grasping arms on its head. Most common is **Marrella**, a small arthropod.

The American researcher **Charles Walcott** discovered the site in **1909**. Over the following years he collected tens of thousands of fossils. Today the Burgess Shale is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, as part of the parks of the Canadian Rocky Mountains. Visitors may only visit the sites on guided tours, so that nothing is damaged.

gewusst: One animal from the Burgess Shale was given the name Hallucigenia because it looked so strange.
The site lies high in the mountains, although the animals once lived in the sea.

teile.einleitung: Bolivia is a country in the heart of South America. It has high mountains, huge salt flats and tropical forests. Bolivia has no coast and is named after the freedom fighter Simón Bolívar.
wichtigste: According to the constitution the capital is Sucre, while the government and parliament sit in La Paz.
Bolivia is landlocked and has no access to the sea.
The country is named after Simón Bolívar and became independent in 1825.
The constitution names 37 official languages: Spanish and 36 indigenous languages.
Bolivia calls itself a “plurinational state”.
Lake Titicaca lies on the border with Peru.

abschnitte.text: Bolivia has an unusual arrangement: **Sucre** is the capital according to the constitution. The government and parliament, however, are based in **La Paz**. La Paz lies at over 3,500 metres and is considered the highest seat of government in the world. Visitors notice the thin air, and many people need a few days to get used to it.

Bolivia once had a coast on the Pacific. In the **War of the Pacific** in the 19th century, it lost this region to **Chile**. Since then Bolivia has been **landlocked**. Even so, it has a navy. It sails mainly on **Lake Titicaca** and on the big rivers in the lowlands. Bolivia has never given up its wish for access to the sea.

Many **indigenous peoples** live in Bolivia, that is, descendants of the people who lived there before the Spaniards. The constitution therefore names **37 official languages**: Spanish and 36 indigenous languages such as **Quechua**, **Aymara** and **Guaraní**. The country calls itself a **plurinational state**, a state of many peoples. Switzerland also has several national languages, but only four.

Bolivia was for a long time a **colony of Spain**. In the 19th century, **Simón Bolívar** led several countries of South America to independence. When Bolivia became independent in **1825**, it was given his name. Under the Spaniards, the city of **Potosí** was famous for a mountain of silver. Huge amounts of **silver** were dug out of the earth there.

In the west rise the **Andes** with the highland plateau, the **Altiplano**. This is where the **Salar de Uyuni** lies, the largest salt flat in the world. Beneath the salt are large reserves of **lithium**, which is needed for batteries. In the east the land becomes flatter and warmer, and tropical forests grow there that belong to the Amazon region.

gewusst: Bolivia and Paraguay are the only countries in South America with no access to the sea.
The Salar de Uyuni is so flat that after rain it looks like a gigantic mirror.
Lake Titicaca lies at over 3,800 metres above sea level.

teile.einleitung: The American bison is a mighty bovine that lives in North America. In the past millions of bison roamed the wide grasslands. By 1900 they had almost been wiped out, but today they are more numerous again.
wichtigste: The American bison lives in North America, mainly in the USA and Canada.
It is the largest land animal in North America, and a bull can weigh almost a tonne.
Many call it a “buffalo”, but it is not a true buffalo.
Bison eat mainly grasses and herbs.
Over its shoulders the bison has a large hump of muscle.
Around 1900 there were only a few hundred bison left.
Its close relative in Europe is the **wisent**.

abschnitte.text: The bison is very powerfully built. Over its shoulders it carries a high **hump** of strong muscle. Head, neck and forelegs are covered with long, dark fur. That is why it looks much mightier at the front than at the back. A male bison is called a **bull**, a female a **cow** and the young a **calf**. Both sexes have short, curved horns.

Bison are **plant eaters**. They eat mainly grasses and herbs. In the past they lived in huge herds on the **prairie**, a wide grassland in the middle of North America. The herds travelled over great distances. In winter bison push the snow aside with their heads to get at the grass. Their thick fur protects them from the cold.

For many peoples of the first inhabitants the bison was very important. They used the meat, fur, bones and sinews. In the 19th century millions of bison were shot by settlers and hunters, often only for the hide. Around 1900 only **a few hundred** animals were left. After that they were protected. Today many bison live there again, for example in **Yellowstone National Park**.

In everyday speech the bison is often called a “buffalo”. True **buffalo** are different bovines, however, for example the water buffalo in Asia or the African buffalo in Africa. There are two forms of the American bison: the **plains bison** and the larger **wood bison**, which occurs mainly in Canada.

In Europe lives the **wisent**, a close relative of the bison. It too had almost died out and was saved in zoos. In Switzerland, in the **canton of Solothurn**, there is a trial in which wisents live in a forest. People want to find out how they behave in nature and how they live together with the forest.

gewusst: Since 2016 the bison has been the official national mammal of the USA.
Despite its size, a bison can run fast and swim well.

teile.einleitung: The Antarctic Treaty of 1959 is the heart of a whole system of agreements. It includes rules on protecting the environment, on fishing and on cooperation between states. Together they make Antarctica a place for peace and science.
wichtigste: The Antarctic Treaty System includes several agreements.
The Madrid Protocol on Environmental Protection (1991) bans the mining of mineral resources except for research.
Seven states make territorial claims, including Norway.
Marie Byrd Land is the largest area without a claim.
Since 2004 the Secretariat has had its seat in Buenos Aires.
A convention of 1980 (CCAMLR) regulates fishing, especially for krill.
A state gets a vote if it carries out serious research in Antarctica.

abschnitte.text: **Seven states** make claims to parts of Antarctica: Argentina, Australia, Chile, France, New Zealand, **Norway** and the United Kingdom. Several claims overlap, especially on the Antarctic Peninsula. The treaty puts these claims on ice. Nobody claims **Marie Byrd Land** in West Antarctica. It is the largest unclaimed land area on Earth.

In 1991 an **environmental protocol** was agreed in Madrid. It declares Antarctica a **nature reserve** for peace and science. Any mining of **mineral resources** is forbidden, except for research. Anyone who plans something there must first check how it harms the environment. A review of the rules is possible at the earliest 50 years after it came into force, that is, from 2048.

A convention of **1980**, abbreviated **CCAMLR**, protects the living marine resources around Antarctica. It looks at the whole ecosystem, not just individual species of fish. **Krill** are small crustaceans and the food of penguins, seals and whales. That is why too much krill must not be caught. In 2016 a huge marine protected area was agreed in the **Ross Sea**, then the largest in the world.

The treaty states meet every year for consultative meetings. Since **2004** the permanent **Secretariat** has had its seat in **Buenos Aires**. The **Consultative Parties** are allowed to take part in decisions. A state that joined later gets this status only if it carries out significant **research** in Antarctica, for example with its own station or with expeditions. Other states may take part but may not vote.

gewusst: The protected area in the Ross Sea covers over 1.5 million square kilometres, more than the area of France, Germany and Italy together.
Because of the treaty, no new claim may be made even to ownerless Marie Byrd Land.

teile.einleitung: Auyan-Tepui is a large table mountain in the south-east of Venezuela. It has steep rock walls and a flat plateau on top. From its edge plunges Angel Falls, the highest waterfall in the world.
wichtigste: Auyan-Tepui is a table mountain in Venezuela.
Its plateau covers around 700 square kilometres.
From it plunges Angel Falls, the highest waterfall in the world.
It lies in Canaima National Park.
Table mountains like it are called tepuis in the region.

abschnitte.text: A **table mountain** has steep sides and a flat surface on top, like a table. In Venezuela and the neighbouring countries such mountains are called **tepuis**. Auyan-Tepui is one of the largest of them. Its **plateau** measures around 700 square kilometres and lies at over 2,000 metres. It consists of very old **sandstone**, which water and weather have shaped over a long time.

From the edge of Auyan-Tepui, **Angel Falls** plunges almost 1,000 metres. It is the highest waterfall on Earth. It is named after the American pilot **Jimmie Angel**, who flew over the area in the 1930s and landed his aircraft on the plateau. In the dry season the waterfall carries much less water than in the rainy season.

Auyan-Tepui lies in **Canaima National Park**, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. On the remote plateaus of the tepuis grow plants found nowhere else. The area is hard to reach. To the foot of the waterfall you usually travel by boat on the rivers.

gewusst: The water of Angel Falls drops so far that on the way it partly dissolves into a fine spray.

teile.einleitung: Upwelling is the rising of cold, nutrient-rich water from the depths of the sea to the surface. Areas of upwelling are among the most fish-rich parts of the sea in the world.
wichtigste: In upwelling, cold deep water replaces the surface water that has been driven away.
The deep water contains many nutrients such as nitrate and phosphate.
On coasts the upwelling is triggered by the wind and by Ekman transport.
In the Northern Hemisphere the water is deflected on average 90 degrees to the right of the wind.
Well-known upwelling areas lie off Peru, Namibia and north-west Africa.
The opposite process is called downwelling.

abschnitte.text: If the wind blows for a long time parallel to a coast, it pushes the surface water along. Because of the Earth’s rotation the **Coriolis force** acts: it deflects the movement to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere. Averaged over the whole moving layer, the water flows at 90 degrees to the wind direction. This effect is called **Ekman transport**. If it points away from the land, cold water flows in from below.

abschnitte.titel: Why there are so many fish there
abschnitte.text: The deep water brings many **nutrients** such as nitrate and phosphate to the top. In the sunlight this makes **phytoplankton**, tiny algae in the water, grow strongly. **Zooplankton** feeds on it, and large shoals of fish in turn live on that. Upwelling areas cover only a small part of the seas but provide a large part of the world’s fish catch.

Off the west coast of South America lies the upwelling area of the **Humboldt Current** off Peru and Chile. Off Namibia the cold **Benguela Current** flows north, and off Morocco, Western Sahara and Mauritania the **Canary Current** flows south. There is also strong upwelling off California. All these areas lie on the west coasts of continents.

The cold water cools the air above it from below. This means hardly any rain clouds form, but often dense **coastal fog**. That is why coastal deserts often lie next to upwelling areas, such as the **Namib** in Namibia or the Atacama in Chile. Some beetles in the Namib collect drinking water from the fog.

abschnitte.titel: At the equator and the opposite
abschnitte.text: There is also upwelling at the **equator** in the Pacific. The trade winds blow west there, and the water is deflected north of the equator to the north and south of it to the south. In between, cold water rises. The opposite process is called **downwelling**: surface water is pushed together and sinks. Such areas are mostly low in nutrients.

gewusst: During an El Niño the upwelling off Peru weakens, and then there are clearly fewer fish there.
Ekman transport is named after the Swedish researcher Vagn Walfrid Ekman.

teile.einleitung: Baja California is a long, narrow peninsula in the north-west of Mexico. On one side lies the Pacific, on the other the Gulf of California. The peninsula is known for deserts with giant cacti, grey whales and rich marine life.
wichtigste: Baja California is around 1,200 kilometres long and belongs to Mexico.
The Gulf of California separates it from the Mexican mainland.
The peninsula is divided into two states.
Grey whales give birth to their young in its lagoons in winter.
In the north lies the border city of Tijuana, in the south Cabo San Lucas.
Large parts are desert with giant cacti.

abschnitte.text: Baja California is around **1,200 kilometres** long, but depending on the place only about 40 to 320 kilometres wide. That makes it one of the longest peninsulas in the world. In the west lies the open **Pacific**. In the east the **Gulf of California**, also called the Sea of Cortés, separates the peninsula from the Mexican mainland.

The peninsula is divided into **two Mexican states**. The north is called **Baja California** and has the capital **Mexicali**. The south is called **Baja California Sur** with the capital **La Paz**. Right in the north lies **Tijuana**, directly on the border with the USA next to San Diego. The border crossing there is among the busiest in the world.

Baja California is very **dry** and mostly covered by desert. Giant cacti such as the **cardón**, one of the largest cacti in the world, grow there. It can grow many metres high. Right in the south lies **Cabo San Lucas**, where the Pacific and the Gulf meet. Well known there is the rock arch **El Arco** in the sea.

abschnitte.titel: Grey whales and the world’s aquarium
abschnitte.text: Every year **grey whales** migrate thousands of kilometres from the Arctic to the warm lagoons on the Pacific coast of the peninsula. There they give birth to their young in winter. The Gulf of California is also full of life: whales, dolphins, sea lions and hundreds of fish species live there. The French marine explorer **Jacques Cousteau** therefore called it the “world’s aquarium”.

gewusst: The islands and protected areas in the Gulf of California are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
In the Gulf of California lives the vaquita, one of the rarest marine mammals in the world.

teile.einleitung: In chemical weathering, rock is not simply broken up but changed into new substances by water, acids and oxygen. Over a long time this produces clay minerals, soils and even caves.
wichtigste: Chemical weathering changes the substances in rock.
It is fastest in a warm, moist climate.
According to the RGT rule, the reaction rate roughly doubles to triples for every 10 °C of warming.
In hydrolysis, feldspar and water form clay minerals such as kaolinite.
Carbonic acid from water and CO₂ dissolves limestone.
Oxidised iron colours many soils and rocks red.

abschnitte.text: Chemical reactions need **water** and go faster at higher temperatures. The **RGT rule**, also called the van ’t Hoff rule, says that for every 10 °C of warming, reactions go about two to three times as fast. This is why rock weathers much more strongly in the **humid tropics** than in cold or dry regions. There the weathered layer is often many metres thick.

In **hydrolysis**, silicate minerals such as **feldspar** react with water. Substances such as potassium are washed out, and **clay minerals** form. In strong weathering in the tropics, **kaolinite** forms especially often. Kaolinite is the main component of china clay, from which porcelain is made.

Some rocks dissolve in water. **Rock salt** dissolves very quickly even in pure water, whereas granite or quartzite hardly dissolve at all. **Limestone** is dissolved by **carbonic acid**: rainwater takes up carbon dioxide from the air and soil. This is how caves and karst landscapes form in limestone, as you can also find in the Jura and in the Swiss Alps.

Many minerals contain **iron**. When it comes into contact with oxygen, **iron oxide** forms, for example haematite. This process is called **oxidation**, and it is similar to rusting. It gives tropical soils and desert rocks their red to rusty brown colour.

In **hydration**, water is built into the crystal lattice. In this way anhydrite becomes **gypsum** and expands as it does so, which can damage rock and even tunnels. In cities, **acid rain** attacks marble statues and limestone-bearing sandstone facades. It forms from sulphur oxides and nitrogen oxides in exhaust gases.

gewusst: Porcelain is made from kaolinite, a product of chemical weathering.
Many dripstone caves were formed by carbonic acid in limestone.

teile.einleitung: An oxbow lake is a former part of a river that has been cut off from the main channel. It often looks like a lake in the shape of a crescent moon. Oxbow lakes form quite naturally when rivers flow in loops through flat land.
wichtigste: An oxbow lake is a cut-off old river loop.
River loops are called meanders.
When a meander is broken through, the old loop stays behind as still water.
In English such a lake is called an “oxbow lake”, after the bow of an ox yoke.
There are very many oxbow lakes on the Mississippi.
Oxbow lakes are valuable habitats for animals and plants.

abschnitte.text: In flat terrain a river seldom flows straight. It forms loops called **meanders**. On the outside of a bend the water flows faster and wears away the bank. On the inside it flows more slowly and deposits sand and gravel. In this way the loops become bigger and tighter over time.

At some point two parts of a loop lie only a short distance apart. In a **flood** the river can break through this narrow strip of land. It then takes the shorter route. The old loop is separated from the main channel because sand and mud are deposited at its ends. What stays behind is a still body of water: the **oxbow lake**.

The **Mississippi** in the USA is a well-known example. In its lower course it flows in great loops through a wide plain. That is why there are many crescent-shaped lakes to the left and right of the river. On maps and aerial photos you can clearly see where the river used to flow.

abschnitte.titel: A habitat with an expiry date
abschnitte.text: In an oxbow lake the water hardly flows. That is why different animals live there from those in the river, such as **frogs**, **dragonflies** and many water birds. Reeds and water lilies grow on the bank. Over time an oxbow lake fills with mud and plant remains. It is said to **silt up**, and first becomes a swamp and later dry land.

There are also oxbow lakes in Switzerland, mainly in **floodplains** along larger rivers such as the Rhine, Aare or Reuss. Many rivers were straightened in the 19th and 20th centuries. In the process old river arms were cut off, and artificial oxbow lakes came about. Today many floodplains are protected, because they are important for rare animals and plants.

gewusst: An oxbow lake shows, like a trace, where a river once flowed.
An oxbow lake can form within a few days when a flood breaks through a river loop.

teile.einleitung: Lake Baikal lies in Siberia in the east of Russia. It is the deepest and oldest lake in the world and has especially clear water. Many animals live in it that are found nowhere else, for example the Baikal seal.
wichtigste: Lake Baikal lies in Siberia in Russia.
At its deepest point it is about 1,640 metres deep.
It is around 670 kilometres long but at most about 80 kilometres wide.
At around 25 million years it is regarded as the oldest lake in the world.
Over 300 rivers flow in, but only the Angara flows out.
In winter it freezes over, and you can walk on the ice.

abschnitte.text: Lake Baikal lies in **Siberia**, a huge, cold region in Russia. On the map it looks like a narrow **sickle**. It is around 670 kilometres long but at most about 80 kilometres wide. That is roughly the distance from Geneva to well beyond Lake Constance. The lake lies in a deep **rift** where the Earth’s crust is drifting apart.

At its deepest point Lake Baikal is about **1,640 metres** deep, as deep as no other lake. That is roughly as high as a middling mountain in Switzerland. The lake is around **25 million years** old and is regarded as the oldest lake in the world. Because it is so deep and large, it holds a very large share of the liquid fresh water on the Earth’s surface.

The water of Lake Baikal is especially **clean and clear**. Under water you can see up to 40 metres. Over 300 rivers flow into the lake. Only a single river flows out, the **Angara**. Since 1996 Lake Baikal has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

In the lake lives the **Baikal seal**. It is the only seal species that lives only in fresh water. How it once got into the lake in the middle of the continent is not entirely clear. Many other animals that are found only there also live in Lake Baikal, for example special fish and crustaceans. Such species are called **endemic**.

In winter it becomes very cold at Lake Baikal. The lake then gets a thick **layer of ice**, which often stays until spring. You can walk on the ice, and in some places even cars drive across it. The ice is often so clear that you can see through it into the water.

gewusst: The Trans-Siberian Railway runs along the shore of Lake Baikal.
In winter the Baikal seal can scratch breathing holes in the ice.

teile.einleitung: A very few countries have huge populations. India and China alone together have almost three billion inhabitants. Here you can find out which countries have the most people as of 2025.
wichtigste: India and China are the two most populous countries in the world.
In third place come the USA with around 340 million inhabitants.
Fourth is Indonesia, fifth Pakistan.
Nigeria is the most populous country in Africa, with Ethiopia in second place.
Brazil is the most populous country in South America.
In the EU, Germany has the most inhabitants.
Since 2024 Switzerland has had over 9 million inhabitants.

abschnitte.text: **India** and **China** each have well over a billion inhabitants. Around 2023 India overtook China. In **fourth place** lies **Indonesia** with around 285 million people, who live on thousands of islands. It is the most populous country in South-East Asia. **Pakistan** has around 255 million inhabitants according to the UN and is in **fifth place**. There the population is growing very fast.

The **USA** stand in **third place** with around 340 million inhabitants. They lie clearly behind the two Asian giants but ahead of all other countries. **Brazil** has around 210 million inhabitants, about half of all the people in South America. **Mexico** has around 130 million inhabitants, and almost all of them speak Spanish. So more people with Spanish as their mother tongue live there than in any other country, more even than in Spain with around 49 million.

**Nigeria** is the most populous country in Africa, with well over 230 million inhabitants as of 2025. In second place in Africa comes **Ethiopia** with around 135 million. Ethiopia is also the most populous **landlocked country** in the world, that is, a country with no access to the sea. In many countries of Africa the population is very young and growing fast.

In the **European Union**, **Germany** has the most inhabitants with around 83 million, followed by **France** with around 68 million. **Switzerland** is small by comparison. According to the **Federal Statistical Office**, it has had over **9 million** inhabitants since 2024. The population is growing mainly through **immigration**. Such figures change constantly, which is why you always give the year.

gewusst: More than a third of all people on Earth live in India and China together.
Indonesia consists of thousands of islands, but most people live on the island of Java.

teile.einleitung: A container is a large, standardised steel box for transporting goods. Because all containers are built the same way, they can be quickly moved between ship, train and lorry.
wichtigste: Containers have standard dimensions and are mostly made of steel.
A 20-foot container is about 6 metres long, and a 40-foot container about 12 metres.
TEU stands for “twenty-foot equivalent unit” and equals one 20-foot container.
Malcolm McLean is regarded as the inventor of the modern shipping container.
In the port, container cranes lift the containers off the ship.
Containers fit on ship, train and lorry.

abschnitte.text: A **container** is a large box made of **steel** with doors on one side. Goods such as clothes, furniture or machines are transported in it. Containers are very sturdy and can be **stacked** high. The goods are not unpacked when they are moved from one vehicle to another, but stay in the container for the whole journey.

The length of containers is measured in **feet**. A foot is about 30 centimetres. A **20-foot container** is therefore about **6 metres** long, and a **40-foot container** about 12 metres. The unit **TEU**, “twenty-foot equivalent unit”, counts how many 20-foot containers a ship can carry or a port can handle.

The American transport businessman **Malcolm McLean** is regarded as the inventor of the modern shipping container. In **1956** he sent a ship carrying standardised containers to sea for the first time. Before that, dockworkers had to move every box and sack individually. The container cut **transport costs** enormously.

In the port, huge **container cranes** lift the containers off the ship. These cranes stand on rails on the quay and reach far out over the ship. They set the containers down on land or on board one at a time. From there they continue by **train** or **lorry**.

Switzerland, although it has no sea coast, is also linked into container traffic. In the **Rhine ports** near Basel, containers arrive on ships along the Rhine. From there they continue by rail or by lorry across the country. Many goods from Asia reach Switzerland this way.

gewusst: Because containers are so cheap, transport across the sea is often only a small part of the price of a product.
Worn-out containers are sometimes converted into offices, shops or homes.

teile.einleitung: A boomerang is a curved, flat throwing stick. Aboriginal Australians have used it for a very long time. Some boomerangs fly back to the thrower in an arc after being thrown, while others keep flying straight.
wichtigste: A boomerang is a curved, flat throwing stick.
Aboriginal Australians used it mainly for hunting.
Only light returning boomerangs come back to the thrower.
Heavy hunting boomerangs fly far and straight.
In flight a boomerang spins quickly around itself.

abschnitte.text: A boomerang is a **curved, flat piece of wood**. The **Aboriginal peoples**, the native people of Australia, have used such throwing sticks for a very long time. In the past they were mainly used for **hunting**, for example birds. Boomerangs were also used as a **tool**, for digging or making fire, and as a **toy**. Similar throwing sticks were also known in other parts of the world, for example in ancient Egypt.

Not every boomerang comes back. The heavy **hunting boomerangs** fly **far and straight** to hit an animal. The light **returning boomerangs**, on the other hand, fly in a big **arc** and come back to the thrower. They are less suitable for hunting and better for play and competitions.

A thrown boomerang **spins quickly around itself**. Its arms are curved like the **wings of an aeroplane**. This creates **lift** as it flies, which keeps it in the air. Because the boomerang is spinning, this lift is not equally strong everywhere on its arms. This steers it a little to the side all the time, and so it flies a **curve**. If you throw it correctly, the curve ends at the thrower.

Today throwing boomerangs is also a **sport**. There are competitions in which you have to throw as accurately, as far or for as long as possible. Modern sports boomerangs are often made of **plywood** or **plastic**. Throwing needs space and care, because a boomerang flying back can hurt people.

gewusst: A returning boomerang is thrown almost upright, not flat like a frisbee.
There are boomerangs with three or four arms that also fly back.

teile.einleitung: Costa Rica is a small country in Central America between two seas. It is known for its rainforests, volcanoes and many animals. It is also unusual because the country has no army.
wichtigste: The capital of Costa Rica is San José.
People speak Spanish.
The name means “rich coast”.
Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948.
The country borders Nicaragua in the north and Panama in the south-east.
It lies on the Pacific and the Caribbean Sea.
The popular saying “Pura vida” means roughly “pure life”.

abschnitte.text: Costa Rica lies in **Central America**. In the north it borders **Nicaragua**, and in the south-east **Panama**. To the west lies the **Pacific**, and to the east the **Caribbean Sea**. The country is somewhat larger than Switzerland. The capital, **San José**, lies in the highlands in the middle of the country.

After a short civil war, Costa Rica abolished its **army** in **1948**. Since then there has only been a police force. The money saved went, among other things, into schools and health care. Costa Rica is regarded as one of the most stable countries in Central America. It has been independent of Spain since 1821.

A large part of the country is protected by **national parks** and reserves. Monkeys, parrots, frogs and butterflies live in the rainforest. Very popular is the **sloth**, which hangs slowly upside down in the trees. Many people travel to Costa Rica to experience nature. This is called ecotourism.

Costa Rica lies on the **Pacific Ring of Fire**, where there are many volcanoes. Especially well known is **Arenal**, with its almost perfect cone shape. Around the volcanoes there are hot springs. The volcanic soil is fertile, and **coffee** and bananas, for example, grow in it.

The people of Costa Rica speak **Spanish**. The name of the country means **“rich coast”**. You hear the saying **“Pura vida”** everywhere there. It means roughly “pure life” and is used as a greeting, as thanks or simply as a sign of good spirits.

gewusst: Costa Rica has had no army since 1948.
Christopher Columbus reached the coast of Costa Rica in 1502 on his last voyage.
The people of Costa Rica often call themselves “Ticos” and “Ticas”.

teile.einleitung: Biogas is a flammable gas that is produced from slurry, manure, plant remains or food waste. Bacteria break these materials down without oxygen. With biogas you can generate electricity and heat.
wichtigste: Biogas is produced when bacteria break down organic matter without oxygen.
On farms, slurry, manure and plant remains are used for this.
The most important component is methane.
Biogas can supply electricity and heat.
What is left over from the plant is used as fertiliser.

abschnitte.text: In a **biogas plant**, slurry, manure, green waste or food scraps go into a large, airtight container. Inside, **bacteria** break the materials down **without oxygen**. This process is called **fermentation**. It produces a mixture of gases, mainly **methane** and carbon dioxide. The methane is flammable and supplies the energy.

Often the biogas is burned right next to the plant in an engine that drives a **generator**. This produces **electricity and heat** at the same time. Biogas can also be purified and fed into the gas grid as **biomethane** or used as fuel for vehicles. What is left over in the plant is called **digestate**. Farmers spread it on the fields as fertiliser.

In Switzerland there are many biogas plants on **farms**. Green waste from municipal green-waste collections and waste from the food industry are also fermented. Biogas counts as **renewable energy**, because the materials keep arising anew. In addition, less methane from slurry gets into the air if it is captured and used in a plant.

gewusst: In sewage treatment plants, too, gas is produced from the sewage sludge, which many plants use themselves for electricity and heat.

teile.einleitung: The Arctic is the region around the North Pole. In its middle there is no land but a sea that is often covered with ice. In summer the midnight sun shines there, and in winter the polar night prevails.
wichtigste: The Arctic is the region around the North Pole.
In its middle lies a sea that is often covered with ice.
Greenland is the largest island in the world and lies largely in the Arctic.
In summer there is the midnight sun, in winter the polar night.
The Arctic fox, the reindeer and the polar bear live in the Arctic.
The Arctic Council has eight member states.
Since 2017 Switzerland has been an observer in the Arctic Council.

abschnitte.titel: A sea at the North Pole
abschnitte.text: The **Arctic** is the region around the **North Pole**. Unlike in Antarctica, there is no continent in its middle but a **sea** that is often covered with ice. All around lie the northern edges of Europe, Asia and North America. The large island of **Greenland** lies largely in the Arctic. It is the largest island in the world and almost entirely covered with ice.

In summer the sun does not set in the Arctic for weeks. It stays light even at night. This is called the **midnight sun**. In winter it is the other way round: the sun stays below the horizon for weeks. This dark period is called the **polar night**. The closer you get to the North Pole, the longer these periods last. In the sky in winter the **northern lights** often glow.

The **Arctic fox** has white fur in winter and is well camouflaged in the snow. **Reindeer** move in large herds across the tundra. Among them the females also carry antlers. On the sea ice the **polar bear** hunts for seals. Many birds come to the Arctic only in summer to breed there.

Eight countries have territory in the Arctic: Canada, the USA with Alaska, Russia, Denmark with Greenland, **Norway**, Sweden, **Finland** and Iceland. They form the **Arctic Council**. There they work together on environmental protection, for example. Representatives of the peoples of the Arctic, such as the Inuit and the Sami, are also involved. Other countries can only be **observers**.

Switzerland has no territory in the far north. Since **2017**, though, it has had **observer status** in the Arctic Council. Swiss researchers study **glaciers**, snow and climate in the Arctic, for example. The knowledge from the Alps helps with this. The Arctic is warming markedly faster than the rest of the Earth, which is why it is watched especially closely.

gewusst: The name Arctic comes from the Greek word for bear, because the constellation of the Great Bear stands in the northern sky.
People have lived in the Arctic for thousands of years, for example the Inuit.

teile.einleitung: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef with small islands that encloses a lagoon. Atolls are found mainly in warm tropical seas, especially in the Pacific and the Indian Ocean. How they form was already explained by the naturalist Charles Darwin.
wichtigste: An atoll is a ring of coral reef and small islands around a lagoon.
The lagoon is the calm, shallow stretch of water inside.
According to Darwin, an atoll forms from a reef around a sinking volcano.
The sequence is: fringing reef, barrier reef, atoll.
The word “atoll” comes from the language of the Maldives.
The Maldives consist of 26 natural atolls.

abschnitte.text: In the 19th century Charles Darwin described how an atoll forms. First a **fringing reef** grows directly on the coast of a volcanic island. The island slowly sinks, but the reef keeps growing upwards. A lagoon forms between island and reef, and a **barrier reef** arises. When the island has sunk completely, only the ring of reef is left: an **atoll**.

For a long time Darwin’s idea was only a theory. In 1952 researchers drilled deep into the ground on the atoll **Enewetak** in the Marshall Islands. Beneath over 1,000 metres of limestone from dead corals they struck **basalt**, that is, volcanic rock. This confirmed that a sunken volcano lies beneath the atoll.

Inside an atoll lies the **lagoon**, usually calm and shallow. On the ring of reef lie small islands, which in Polynesia are called **motu**. Narrow gaps in the reef are called **passes**. The water flows through them at low and high tide, and often they are the only access for ships.

The **Maldives** in the Indian Ocean are divided into 26 natural atolls and have over 1,000 small islands. The word atoll comes from their language, Dhivehi. **Kiritimati**, Christmas Island, belongs to Kiribati and by land area is one of the largest atolls in the world. **Bikini Atoll** is well known because the USA tested atomic bombs there between 1946 and 1958. The inhabitants had to leave their home.

The islands of an atoll often rise only a few metres above the sea. If **sea level** rises, they are in great danger. The corals are also sensitive: if the water gets too warm, they can die. That is why atolls are closely watched today.

gewusst: Hardly any country in the world is as flat as the Maldives.
Coral reefs are built by tiny animals that secrete limestone.

teile.einleitung: The Andean condor is a huge vulture that lives in the Andes of South America. It is among the largest birds that can fly. With its enormous wings it glides for hours over the mountains.
wichtigste: The Andean condor is a vulture and belongs to the New World vultures.
A large male weighs up to about 15 kilograms.
Its wings measure well over 3 metres together.
It eats mainly dead animals, that is, carrion.
Its head is bald, and around its neck it wears a white ruff of feathers.
It can be seen on the coats of arms of Chile and other countries.
The female usually lays only one egg, and only every two years.

abschnitte.text: The Andean condor is very large and heavy. A male weighs up to about **15 kilograms**, while the females are clearly lighter. With wings spread it measures a good **3 metres**. That makes it one of the largest flying birds in the world. It lives in the **Andes** and on the Pacific coast of South America.

The plumage is mostly **black**, with white patches on the wings. Around its neck the condor wears a white **ruff of feathers** like a scarf. The head, on the other hand, has **no feathers**. This keeps it clean when the bird feeds inside a dead animal. The males have a fleshy crest on the head.

For such a heavy bird constant wing-flapping would be very tiring. That is why the Andean condor lets itself be carried by **updrafts**, that is, by warm rising air or wind on mountain slopes. It hardly beats its wings and glides for hours. In this way it can cover long distances and look out for food.

The Andean condor is a **scavenger**. It eats mainly dead animals, such as llamas, guanacos or cows, and on the coast dead seals as well. In this way it helps to keep nature clean. Vultures like it are therefore sometimes called the “health police”. It belongs to the **New World vultures** of the Americas, which are only distantly related to the vultures of Europe.

The female usually lays only **a single egg**, and only about every two years. Both parents look after the chick for a long time. Because there are so few young, the condor is sensitive to dangers such as poisoning or hunting. In several countries it is a national symbol and appears on the **coat of arms**, for example of **Chile**, Bolivia, Ecuador and Colombia.

gewusst: Andean condors can live to a great age, and some in zoos have reached over 70 years.
In the Swiss Alps the bearded vulture is also a vulture, with a wingspan of almost 3 metres.

teile.einleitung: The United States of America is made up of 50 states. Each state has its own capital, its own parliament and its own laws. This is a little like the cantons of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The USA is made up of 50 states.
The smallest state by area is Rhode Island.
California has the most inhabitants (as of 2024).
A state’s capital is often not its largest city, for example Austin in Texas.
Four states border Mexico and 13 border Canada.
At the Four Corners, Utah, Colorado, Arizona and New Mexico meet.

abschnitte.text: The USA is a **federal state** made up of **50 states**. Each has a **governor**, its own parliament and its own courts. Many things, such as schools or criminal law, are decided by the states themselves. The capital of the whole USA, **Washington, D.C.**, does not belong to any state. The 50 stars on the flag stand for the 50 states. In a similar way, in Switzerland the Confederation and the **cantons** share the tasks.

The **smallest** state by area is **Rhode Island** on the east coast. At about 4,000 square kilometres, it has only about a tenth of the area of Switzerland. The largest is **Alaska** in the far north. **California** has the most inhabitants, with about 39 million people in 2024. **Texas** comes second.

In the USA the capital of a state is often **not the largest city**. The capital of **Texas** is **Austin**, not Houston. In **California** the government sits in **Sacramento**, not in Los Angeles or San Francisco. And the capital of the state of **New York** is **Albany** on the Hudson River. New York City is much bigger, but it is not the seat of government.

Many states have **nicknames**. Texas is called the “**Lone Star State**” because its flag shows a single star. It recalls the time from 1836 to 1845, when Texas was an independent republic. **Michigan** consists of two large **peninsulas** between the Great Lakes. The **Mackinac Bridge** joins the two parts.

Four states border **Mexico**: California, Arizona, New Mexico and Texas. Thirteen states border **Canada**, from Alaska in the west to Maine in the east. This border is regarded as the longest land border in the world. At the **Four Corners**, **Utah**, **Colorado**, **Arizona** and **New Mexico** meet at right angles at a single point. This does not happen anywhere else in the USA.

gewusst: Hawaii was admitted in 1959 as the last of the 50 states.
Every state sends exactly two members to the Senate, no matter how big it is. In a similar way, in Switzerland every canton has two seats in the Council of States.

teile.einleitung: The Amazon is the river with the most water on Earth. It rises in the Andes in Peru and flows right across South America into the Atlantic Ocean. Around it grows the largest rainforest in the world.
wichtigste: The Amazon carries more water than any other river in the world.
It rises in the Andes in Peru.
It is around 6,400 kilometres long and runs into the Atlantic Ocean in Brazil.
Most of the Amazon rainforest lies in Brazil.
In the river live piranhas, river dolphins and giant fish such as the arapaima.
The rainforest is important for the climate of the whole Earth.
Every year large areas of forest are lost through deforestation.

abschnitte.text: The Amazon rises high in the **Andes** in **Peru**, not far from the Pacific. From there it flows east through Peru and **Brazil**. After around 6,400 kilometres it runs into the Atlantic in a huge estuary. Whether the Amazon or the Nile is longer is still debated by researchers, because the source is determined in different ways.

On average the Amazon carries over 200,000 cubic metres of water per second into the sea. That is much more than any other river and about 200 times as much as the Rhine at Basel. Over 1,000 **tributaries** feed it, including the Rio Negro with its dark water. At **Manaus** the dark and the light water flow side by side for kilometres without mixing straight away.

Around the river lies the **Amazon rainforest**, the largest tropical rainforest on Earth. About 60 per cent of it lies in Brazil, the rest in countries such as Peru, Colombia and Bolivia. No other area has so many different animal and plant species. The trees store a great deal of carbon and, through evaporation, produce part of the rain themselves.

In the Amazon lives the pink **Amazon river dolphin**, also called the boto. There are piranhas with sharp teeth, electric eels that produce electricity, and the arapaima, one of the largest freshwater fish. On the banks jaguars and caimans hunt, and in the swamps lives the green anaconda. In the canopy live monkeys, sloths and colourful macaws.

The Spaniard **Francisco de Orellana** was the first European to travel down the river to the sea, in 1541 and 1542. He reported fighting women who reminded him of the **Amazons** from Greek legends, hence the name. Long before the Europeans, many indigenous peoples lived along the river. Some of them still live almost without contact with the rest of the world.

Every year large areas of rainforest are **cleared** to make pastures, soya fields or roads. Fires and gold prospecting also harm the forest and the river. Researchers fear that parts of the rainforest could dry out if too much forest disappears. That is why many countries and organisations are working to protect it.

begriffe.erklaerung: A dense forest in warm regions where it rains a great deal.
A river that runs into a larger river.
The felling of many trees so that a forest disappears.
The original inhabitants of an area and their descendants.

gewusst: To this day not a single bridge crosses the whole Amazon.
At high tide a wave, the pororoca, can roll several metres high up the Amazon.
In the rainy season the river rises by over 10 metres in some places.

teile.einleitung: Argentina is a large country in the south of South America. It reaches from tropical forests in the north to glaciers and the “end of the world” in the south. It is known for tango, football and the barbecue feast called asado.
wichtigste: After Brazil, Argentina is the second-largest country in South America.
The capital is Buenos Aires.
The name comes from the Latin word “argentum” for silver.
Argentina declared its independence from Spain on 9 July 1816.
The tango arose in Argentina and Uruguay.
Argentina became football world champion in 2022.
The flag is light blue and white with a golden sun.

abschnitte.text: After Brazil, Argentina is the **second-largest country** in South America, and worldwide it ranks around eighth. In the west the **Andes** tower up, with Aconcagua, the highest mountain in the Americas. In the middle lies the **Pampas**, a wide, fertile grassland. In the south stretches **Patagonia** with steppes and glaciers. Right in the south lies **Ushuaia**, often called the southernmost city in the world and the “end of the world”.

The name comes from the Latin word **“argentum”** for silver. The Spanish conquerors hoped to find a lot of silver in the area. For a long time the territory was a Spanish colony. On **9 July 1816** Argentina declared its **independence** in Tucumán. The broad Avenida 9 de Julio in the capital **Buenos Aires** is named after this date.

The **tango** arose over 100 years ago in the port cities on the Río de la Plata, in Argentina and Uruguay. It is danced as a couple in a close embrace and has a music of its own. Very popular too is the **asado**. In it meat is grilled for a long time over the embers. Families and friends often meet for it at the weekend. Argentina is known for its cattle farming on the Pampas.

Football is a great passion in Argentina. The men’s national team has become **world champion** three times: in 1978, 1986 and **2022**. In Qatar it won the final against France in a **penalty shoot-out**. Famous players are Diego Maradona and **Lionel Messi**. The team plays in the colours of the flag, **light blue and white**.

The **flag** has two light blue stripes and a white stripe. In the middle is a golden **sun** with a face. In the 19th century many people from Europe emigrated to Argentina, including from **Switzerland**. They founded farming villages on the Pampas, and some places still bear Swiss names today. The national language is Spanish.

gewusst: At almost 7,000 metres Aconcagua is the highest mountain outside Asia.
On the border with Brazil lie the Iguazú Falls, which consist of over 200 individual falls.

teile.einleitung: Bonaire is a small island in the Caribbean, north of Venezuela. It belongs directly to the Netherlands, where it is a “special municipality”. Bonaire is known for its coral reefs, flamingos and salt.
wichtigste: Bonaire lies in the Caribbean off the coast of Venezuela.
Since 2010, Bonaire has been a special municipality of the Netherlands.
Sint Eustatius and Saba also have this status.
Aruba and Curaçao are separate countries within the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
The main town is called Kralendijk.

abschnitte.titel: A piece of the Netherlands in the Caribbean
abschnitte.text: Until 2010, Bonaire belonged to the **Netherlands Antilles**. When these were dissolved, a new arrangement was chosen. **Bonaire**, **Sint Eustatius** and **Saba** became **special municipalities** of the Netherlands. Together they are also called the **Caribbean Netherlands**. **Aruba** and **Curaçao**, on the other hand, are separate countries within the kingdom. People on Bonaire pay with the **US dollar**.

Around Bonaire lie colourful **coral reefs**. They are protected, and the island is popular with divers from all over the world. Many **flamingos** live on the island, searching for food in shallow salt lakes. In the south, **salt** has been produced for a long time by letting seawater evaporate in the sun. The white mountains of salt can be seen from far away.

Most people on Bonaire speak **Papiamentu**, a language that developed from Spanish, Portuguese, Dutch and African languages. Dutch is also used. The main town is **Kralendijk**. Because it rarely rains on Bonaire, many **cacti** grow there.

gewusst: In the south of the island stand small stone huts that recall the time of slavery in the salt works.
Bonaire lies outside the usual zone where hurricanes strike the Caribbean.

teile.einleitung: Brasília is the capital of Brazil. It was built in only about four years in the middle of the country and was inaugurated in 1960. From above, its layout looks like an aeroplane or a bird.
wichtigste: Brasília was inaugurated as the new capital on 21 April 1960.
Before that, Rio de Janeiro was the capital from 1763 to 1960.
President Juscelino Kubitschek drove the building forward.
The city plan, the Plano Piloto, was designed by Lúcio Costa.
The striking buildings are by the architect Oscar Niemeyer.
Since 1987, Brasília has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

abschnitte.text: For a long time **Rio de Janeiro** on the coast was the capital. The idea of building a new capital in the **interior** came early on. This was meant to help the interior of Brazil grow too. President **Juscelino Kubitschek** carried out the plan. He promised “50 years of progress in 5”. After only about four years of building, Brasília was inaugurated on **21 April 1960**.

The city planner **Lúcio Costa** won the competition for the city plan, the **Plano Piloto**, in 1957. Two crossing axes give it the shape of an **aeroplane** or a **bird**. The **Monumental Axis** forms the body, where the government and ministries stand. The curved **Residential Axis** forms the wings. There lie large residential blocks with schools, shops and green spaces.

The architect **Oscar Niemeyer** created the curving buildings made of **concrete**. Very well known is the **cathedral**, whose supports reach upwards like hands. The **National Congress** has two domes, one opening upwards and one downwards, and two tall office towers. Niemeyer wanted buildings that look light and elegant.

Brasília lies on a **plateau** more than 1,000 metres above sea level. It is drier here than on the coast. When the city was built, a river was **dammed**. This created the artificial **Lake Paranoá**. It was meant to make the climate more pleasant and today is also used for recreation, such as sailing and swimming.

Since **1987**, Brasília has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. It is one of the youngest cities on this list. The city is honoured as a unique example of 20th-century **urban planning**. Around the Plano Piloto, many more settlements have grown up in the meantime, and most of the people in the region live there.

gewusst: Brasília was built where there had been no city before.
Oscar Niemeyer lived to be over 100 and worked into old age.

teile.einleitung: Christopher Columbus was a sailor who sailed across the Atlantic with three ships in 1492. He wanted to reach Asia and instead reached islands in the Caribbean, which greatly changed the history of the Americas and of Europe.
wichtigste: Columbus probably came from Genoa in Italy.
His first voyage was paid for by the Spanish king and queen.
