He sailed with the Santa María, the Niña and the Pinta.
On 12 October 1492 he reached an island in the Bahamas and named it San Salvador.
He made four voyages to the Americas in all.
Until his death in 1506 he believed he had been in Asia.

abschnitte.text: Most researchers assume that **Columbus** was born in the port city of **Genoa** around 1451. He wanted to find a **sea route west** to the spice lands of Asia, to **India and East Asia**. Portugal turned down his plan. In the end he was supported by **Isabella of Castile** and **Ferdinand of Aragon**, the Spanish king and queen.

For the first voyage, Columbus had three ships. The largest, the **flagship**, was called the **Santa María**. It was accompanied by the smaller caravels **Niña** and **Pinta**. The Santa María ran aground off the island of Hispaniola at Christmas 1492 and was lost.

On 6 September 1492 the ships left **La Gomera** in the Canary Islands. On **12 October** they reached an island in the **Bahamas**, after 36 days, or about five weeks. The local people called the island Guanahani. Columbus named it **San Salvador**, “Holy Saviour”.

Between 1492 and 1504, Columbus sailed across the Atlantic **four times**. He reached islands in the Caribbean and the coast of Central America. Because he believed he was in India, he called the people there “Indios”. For the native peoples, the arrival of the Europeans began a hard time of disease, oppression and loss of their land.

Until his death in 1506, Columbus was convinced that he had reached islands off **Asia**. It was **Amerigo Vespucci** who spread the idea that this was a **“New World”**. The continent was later named **America** after his first name.

gewusst: America is named not after Columbus but after Amerigo Vespucci.
Vikings had already reached North America about 500 years before Columbus.

teile.einleitung: The Black Hills are an upland in the middle of the prairie in the west of the USA. They lie mainly in the state of South Dakota. For the Lakota people they are sacred, and the famous monument Mount Rushmore stands there too.
wichtigste: The Black Hills rise like an island out of the Great Plains.
They lie mainly in South Dakota.
For the Lakota, the Black Hills are a sacred place.
On Mount Rushmore, the heads of four US presidents are carved into the rock.
Who owns the area is disputed to this day.

abschnitte.text: The **Black Hills** are an isolated upland in the **Great Plains**, the wide grassland of North America. They lie mainly in the west of **South Dakota** and reach into Wyoming. Their name means “black hills”. It comes from the dense coniferous forests, which look dark from a distance. In the area there are caves, lakes and herds of bison.

For the **Lakota**, a people of the Sioux, the Black Hills are a **sacred place**. In a treaty of **1868** the USA assured them the area. A few years later **gold** was found there. Many gold prospectors streamed in, and the US government took the land from the Lakota after fighting. In 1980 the Supreme Court of the USA decided that this was unlawful and that the Lakota are owed compensation. The Lakota refused the money, because they want their land back.

On **Mount Rushmore**, the huge heads of four US presidents are carved into the granite: **George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Abraham Lincoln**. Each head is about 18 metres high. The work lasted from 1927 to 1941. The monument attracts very many visitors every year. For many Lakota, though, it is a sign that their sacred land was used without their consent.

gewusst: Nearby, the Crazy Horse Memorial has been under construction since 1948. It shows a Lakota leader and is still not finished.

teile.einleitung: Cirrus clouds are high, fine clouds that look like feathers or strands of hair. They float so high that they are made not of water droplets but of ice crystals.
wichtigste: Cirrus are high clouds, several kilometres up.
They are made of tiny ice crystals.
They look streaky, like fine feathers or hair.
In German they are also called feather clouds.
They can signal that the weather is about to change.

abschnitte.text: The name **cirrus** comes from Latin and means “lock of hair”. The clouds are thin, white and **streaky**. They often look like fine **feathers** or brushstrokes. They cast hardly any shadow because they are so thin.

Cirrus clouds float **very high**, usually above six kilometres. It is icy cold up there even in summer. That is why they are made of tiny **ice crystals**. Strong wind at that height pulls the crystals out into long threads.

If more and more cirrus appear and the sky turns milky, a **warm front** with rain may be approaching. On their own, however, cirrus are usually a sign of fine weather. **Contrails** from aeroplanes can also turn into cirrus-like clouds. When the sun shines through cirrus, a coloured **ring** sometimes forms around it.

gewusst: Cirrus are among the highest clouds that form in our weather.

teile.einleitung: The tree line is the line above which trees can no longer grow. In the Alps it lies high up on the mountains, and in the far north it separates forest from tundra. How high trees grow depends above all on the warmth in summer.
wichtigste: Above the tree line it is too cold for trees.
What matters is the temperature during the growing season.
Between the forest line and the tree line lies the struggle zone.
In Switzerland the forest line is highest in the Valais and the Engadine.
Because of global warming the tree line is slowly shifting upwards.
In the far north the polar tree line separates the taiga from the tundra.

abschnitte.titel: Why trees do not grow higher
abschnitte.text: The higher you climb, the colder it gets. But trees need enough **warmth** to form new wood. If the average temperature in the **growing season** in summer is too low, they can no longer grow properly. Wind, snow and frost add to this. Above a certain height there are therefore only shrubs, grasses and flowers.

abschnitte.titel: Forest line, struggle zone, tree line
abschnitte.text: Experts distinguish two lines. Up to the **forest line**, closed forest grows. Above it there are only single, often stunted trees that struggle against cold, wind and snow. This area is called the **struggle zone**. The **tree line** marks where even the last trees end. In the Alps, **Swiss stone pines** and **larches** often grow there, along with dense thickets of **mountain pines**, which are also called dwarf pines.

In the **inner central Alps** such as the **Valais** and the **Engadine**, the forest line is highest. There the summers are sunnier and warmer than at the edge of the Alps, and the forest reaches up to around 2,300 metres and higher. At the northern edge of the Alps it lies much lower. In many valleys the forest line lies lower than the climate would allow. For centuries farmers have cleared forest there to gain **alpine pastures** for their cattle.

When it gets warmer, young trees can also grow up higher. That is why the tree line is slowly shifting upwards because of **global warming**. Because trees grow slowly, though, this happens only gradually. Even where alpine pastures are no longer farmed, the forest often grows back.

abschnitte.titel: In the north and in the tropics
abschnitte.text: In the north of Europe, Asia and America, the coniferous forest of the **taiga** ends at the **polar tree line**. Further north follows the treeless **tundra**. In the **tropics** the tree line lies much higher than in the Alps, because at the same height it is warmer there. In tropical mountains such as the Andes, trees often still grow at over 3,500 metres.

gewusst: The mountain pine grows close to the ground with bendy branches, so snow protects it and it withstands the weight of snow well.
Swiss stone pines at the forest line can reach an age of several hundred years.

teile.einleitung: The Arctic Ocean lies around the North Pole. It is the smallest and shallowest of the five oceans. A large part is covered with sea ice, on which polar bears hunt for seals.
wichtigste: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest of the five oceans.
A large part is covered with sea ice.
In September the sea ice is usually at its smallest, in March at its largest.
Russia has the longest coast on the Arctic Ocean.
Icebreakers clear a path for ships through the ice.
Belugas and bowhead whales live in this sea.

abschnitte.text: The **Arctic Ocean** is the smallest and also the shallowest of the five oceans. It lies around the **North Pole** and is almost entirely surrounded by land: by Europe, Asia and North America. **Russia** has the longest coast, as its whole northern coast lies on this sea. Through straits it is connected with the Atlantic and the Pacific.

Because it is very cold there, the seawater freezes. A layer of **sea ice** then floats on the sea. In winter the ice grows, in summer part of it melts. At the end of summer, usually in **September**, there is the least ice, in **March** the most. For some decades the sea ice has been getting markedly smaller and thinner because of **climate warming**.

Ordinary ships get no further in ice. An **icebreaker** has a very strong hull. It drives up onto the ice and breaks it with its weight. Since the ice has been shrinking, more ships can travel along the coasts in summer. These sea routes are called the **Northeast Passage** along Russia and the **Northwest Passage** through Canada.

In the Arctic Ocean lives the **beluga**, an entirely white whale, also called the white whale. The **bowhead whale** can live to over 200 years old. On the sea ice the **polar bear** hunts for seals. It needs the ice for hunting. There are no penguins here, they live almost only in the Southern Hemisphere.

On rocky coasts in the north the **puffin** breeds with its colourful beak. It dives for small fish. The **Arctic tern** breeds in the far north and in winter flies as far as Antarctica. Every year it covers huge distances in this way. No other animal migrates so far every year.

gewusst: Beneath the North Pole there is no land, only sea and drifting ice.
In its lifetime an Arctic tern flies a distance equal to several trips to the Moon and back.

teile.einleitung: The Cuyahoga River is a river in the US state of Ohio. It flows through the city of Cleveland into Lake Erie. It became famous because in 1969 it was so polluted that it caught fire.
wichtigste: The Cuyahoga River flows through Cleveland in Ohio into Lake Erie.
In June 1969, oil and rubbish burned on its surface.
The river had already caught fire several times before.
The 1969 fire became a symbol of the environmental movement.
Afterwards the USA passed stricter laws for clean water.
Today the river is much cleaner.

abschnitte.titel: A river in an industrial city
abschnitte.text: The Cuyahoga flows in a curve through the north-east of **Ohio** and flows into **Lake Erie**, one of the five Great Lakes, at **Cleveland**. Its name comes from a Native American language and is usually interpreted as “crooked river”. In Cleveland, many factories and steelworks stood on the bank. For a long time they discharged oil, chemicals and waste into the river without filtering.

In **June 1969**, a carpet of **oil and rubbish** on the water caught fire. The fire was put out quickly and was not even the biggest: the river had already burned several times before. But this time major magazines reported on it. Many people in the USA were appalled that a river could be so dirty.

The fire became a **symbol of the environmental movement**. In 1970 the USA set up its own environmental agency, the **EPA**. In 1972 an important law for clean water followed, the **Clean Water Act**. Factories and cities now had to treat their wastewater. In Switzerland, too, many **sewage treatment plants** were built in these decades, because rivers and lakes were badly polluted.

After many years of work, the Cuyahoga is much cleaner today. Many **species of fish** live in it again. Part of the valley has been the **Cuyahoga Valley National Park** since 2000. The river shows that nature can recover when people protect it.

gewusst: A river of water burned because a thick layer of oil and rubbish was floating on it.
The 1969 fire lasted only about half an hour but changed the environmental laws of the USA.

teile.einleitung: Chichén Itzá is an ancient Maya city in the south of Mexico. Its great pyramid, El Castillo, is one of the best-known buildings in the Americas.
wichtigste: Chichén Itzá lies in the north of the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico.
The Maya built the city over 1,000 years ago.
The great pyramid is called El Castillo, or the Temple of Kukulcán.
Counting the top platform, it has 365 steps, as many as there are days in the year.
In spring and autumn a shadow snake seems to creep down the staircase.
Since 2007 Chichén Itzá has been one of the “New Seven Wonders of the World”.

abschnitte.text: Chichén Itzá lies on the **Yucatán Peninsula**, which lies between the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean Sea. The **Maya** built a large city here with temples, palaces and squares. Over 1,000 years ago it was an important centre. Today it is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and is visited by very many people every year.

The great pyramid is called **El Castillo**, which means “the castle”. It is also known as the **Temple of Kukulcán**, a feathered serpent god. On all **four sides**, a staircase leads up to a temple. Each staircase has 91 steps, making 364 together. With the top platform, that makes **365**, as many as there are days in the year.

At the **equinox** in spring and autumn, the sun casts triangular shadows on the staircase in the afternoon. It looks as if a **snake** is slowly creeping down. At the bottom of the staircase are stone snake heads. Many people come on these days to see the spectacle.

There are hardly any rivers on the surface in Yucatán. Water is found in **cenotes**, deep, round waterholes in the limestone. For the Maya they were important for **drinking water** and were seen as sacred. Near Chichén Itzá lies the famous Sacred Cenote.

abschnitte.titel: A new wonder of the world
abschnitte.text: In 2007, Chichén Itzá was chosen in a worldwide vote as one of the **New Seven Wonders of the World**. Besides the pyramid there is also a large **ball court**, where the Maya played a game with a heavy rubber ball. The buildings show how well the Maya understood astronomy and architecture.

gewusst: The number of steps on El Castillo matches exactly the number of days in a year.
The Great Wall of China is also one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

teile.einleitung: Bossa nova is a gentle style of music from Brazil. It began in Rio de Janeiro in the late 1950s. Bossa nova combines the rhythm of samba with the sounds of jazz.
wichtigste: Bossa nova began in Rio de Janeiro in the late 1950s.
The style combines samba with jazz.
Quiet singing and a guitar are typical.
Important musicians were João Gilberto and Antônio Carlos Jobim.
The best-known song is “Garota de Ipanema”.

abschnitte.text: In Portuguese, “bossa nova” means roughly “new style” or “new wave”. Unlike the loud samba of the carnival, bossa nova sounds **calm and soft**. Usually a **guitar** plays a special, slightly off-beat rhythm. Someone sings quietly over it, almost whispering. **Jazz** brought special chords that give the style its soft sound.

The singer and guitarist **João Gilberto** shaped the typical rhythm. The composer **Antônio Carlos Jobim** wrote many famous songs, often with the poet **Vinícius de Moraes**. An early, important song is “Chega de Saudade” from 1958. The music grew up in the flats and bars by the beaches of Rio, for example in **Copacabana** and **Ipanema**.

The best-known song is “**Garota de Ipanema**”, named after a beach in Rio. In English it is called “The Girl from Ipanema”. In the early 1960s, bossa nova also became very popular in the USA and in Europe. Jazz musicians all over the world played the songs. To this day, bossa nova is often heard in cafés, hotels and films.

gewusst: “Garota de Ipanema” is one of the songs that have been recorded anew most often around the world.
João Gilberto played so quietly that listeners in the concert hall often had to stay completely silent.

teile.einleitung: The Brenner Base Tunnel is a railway tunnel that runs under the Alps and links Austria and Italy. It runs from Innsbruck to Fortezza (Franzensfeste) in South Tyrol. Together with the Innsbruck bypass, it will be the longest underground railway link in the world.
wichtigste: The tunnel links Innsbruck in Austria with Fortezza in Italy.
The main tunnel measures about 55 kilometres.
Together with the Innsbruck bypass, the underground section is over 60 kilometres long.
This makes it longer than the 57-kilometre Gotthard Base Tunnel.
It is expected to open around 2032 (as of 2025).
An exploratory tunnel lies beneath the two main tubes.

abschnitte.text: The **Brenner Pass** lies at about **1,370 metres** above sea level on the border between Austria and Italy. It is one of the lowest crossings over the Alps. That is why a **railway line** and a **motorway** already cross the pass today. A great many lorries drive on the road. The new **base tunnel** passes beneath the pass deep inside the mountain, so that trains can run with almost no gradient.

The main tunnel runs from **Innsbruck** to **Fortezza** in South Tyrol and measures about **55 kilometres**. At Innsbruck it joins an existing bypass tunnel. Together this gives an underground section of **over 60 kilometres**. That is more than the 57 kilometres of the **Gotthard Base Tunnel** in Switzerland, which opened in 2016.

The tunnel consists of **two main tubes**, one for each direction of travel. A few metres below lies an **exploratory tunnel**. During construction it shows what the rock inside the mountain is like. Later it is used for **drainage** and carries mountain water away. Between the tubes there are cross-passages so that people can reach the other tube in an emergency.

An earlier opening was originally planned. **Geological difficulties**, that is, difficult rock inside the mountain, delayed the construction. According to current plans, the tunnel is due to open **around 2032** (as of 2025). The aim is to move more **goods from road to rail**. Switzerland pursues the same idea with its Alpine tunnels.

gewusst: The Brenner Base Tunnel is part of a major European railway axis from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean.
In the tunnel, the border between Austria and Italy is crossed deep inside the mountain.
